name: Gentle Neck Nod
desc: A small, slow 'yes' nod from the very top of your neck — the head gently rocks on the spine while your eyes stay level on the horizon. It's the tiny motion your head makes to say yes, not the deep drop of looking down at a phone. Return to neutral and repeat.

phases.label: Small 'yes' nod from the top of the neck, eyes level

progression: Add a 3-second hold at each end

pairs_with.name: Neck Side Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Covers lateral neck mobility after sagittal

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Shrug Release
pairs_with.reason: Releases upper trap tension that restricts neck

form_cue: Nod from the very top of the neck only — a small 'yes' the head makes rocking on the spine. Key check: your eyes can stay level on the horizon. If your gaze drops toward the floor you've flexed the lower neck (the 'looking at your phone' motion) — that's the posture we're undoing, not the target. Jaw relaxed, rest of the spine still, no momentum.
stop_condition: Stop with any dizziness, sharp pain, or numbness/tingling into the arms. This is gentle mobility, not a stretch to push — keep the nod small and don't force range.
regression: Make the nod even smaller, or do a few reps and rest — this should never feel like effort or strain.
remediation: If the range feels stiff or guarded, settle deep-neck-flexor control with chin tucks first, then add range.

name: Neck Side Tilt
desc: Tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder, hold 5 seconds, then repeat on the left. 3 times each side. Keep shoulders down and relaxed.
progression: Add gentle hand pressure on the tilting side
Combine with deep breathing on exhale

pairs_with.name: Gentle Neck Nod
pairs_with.reason: Combines sagittal and lateral neck mobility

pairs_with.name: Upper Trap Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Deepens the lateral neck release

form_cue: Tip the ear toward the shoulder with the face pointing forward — no rotation — and keep both shoulders down; don't lift the opposite shoulder up to meet the head.
stop_condition: Ease off with any dizziness, sharp pain, or tingling into the arm. A gentle side-of-neck stretch is the target; don't force the end range.
regression: Shrink the tilt, or hold the chair with the opposite hand to keep that shoulder anchored down instead of pulling the head over.
remediation: If it feels tight and guarded, warm up with a few gentle neck nods and shoulder rolls first.

name: Neck Rotation
desc: Turn your head slowly to look over your right shoulder, hold 5 seconds, then repeat left. 3 times each side. Keep chin level throughout.
progression: Turn only as far as comfortable
Try to see slightly further each rep
Add a gentle overpressure with your hand

pairs_with.name: Neck Side Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Covers all three planes of neck motion

pairs_with.name: Chin Tuck
pairs_with.reason: Strengthens deep neck flexors for better rotation

form_cue: Turn your head as if on a spindle: chin level, nose travelling straight across, shoulders square and relaxed. You should feel a mild stretch down the side of the neck you are turning away from.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness, blurred vision, sharp or pinching pain, or numbness or tingling into an arm. A gentle pull at the end of the turn is normal; pain is not, so never force the last bit of range.
regression: Turn only part of the way and shorten the hold, or do it sitting in a chair with your back supported.
remediation: If your chin tips or your shoulders turn with your head, slow down and make the turn smaller. Practise Gentle Neck Nod first to find a relaxed, level head position.

name: Chin Tuck
desc: Pull your chin straight back, making a double chin. Hold 5 seconds, release. This resets forward head posture.

phases.label: Pull your chin straight back, making a double chin

progression: Do against a wall for feedback
Add slight resistance with fingertips on chin

pairs_with.name: Gentle Neck Nod
pairs_with.reason: Chin tucks strengthen what neck nods stretch

pairs_with.name: Thoracic Extension
pairs_with.reason: Addresses the full forward-head chain

form_cue: Glide the chin straight back (a gentle 'double chin'), head sliding back over the shoulders — a horizontal motion, NOT a downward nod or a head tip. Small range; feel a light lengthening at the back of the neck.
stop_condition: Stop with any pinching at the base of the skull, dizziness, or arm symptoms. Keep it gentle — this is a motor-control drill, not a strength push.
regression: Do it lying on your back with the head supported, which removes gravity and makes the correct glide easier to find. Smaller range, fewer reps.
remediation: If you can't separate the glide from a nod, rest two fingers on your chin and let them guide the straight-back motion until the pattern is learned.

name: Upper Trap Stretch
desc: Hold the bottom of your chair with one hand, tilt your head away from that side. You should feel a stretch from neck to shoulder.

phases.label: Hold the bottom of your chair with one hand, ti...

progression: Rotate chin slightly down toward armpit for deeper stretch
Add gentle hand pressure on the head

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Shrug Release
pairs_with.reason: Both target upper trap tension

pairs_with.name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Hits the deeper neck-to-shoulder muscle

form_cue: Anchor the opposite shoulder down (hold the chair) and tilt the head away, letting the stretch come from the lengthening side — not from yanking with the free hand.
stop_condition: A gentle pull along the neck-to-shoulder line only; stop with sharp pain, dizziness, or arm tingling.
regression: Skip the hand-assist and just tilt the head; the anchored shoulder alone gives a stretch.
remediation: If one side is much tighter, spend more time there but never push harder — frequency beats force.

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
desc: Turn your head 45 degrees to one side, then look down toward your armpit. Use your hand to gently add pressure. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Find the angle that gives the best stretch
Add slight chin tuck while in the stretch position

pairs_with.name: Upper Trap Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Together they release the full neck-shoulder junction

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Strengthens what the stretch is lengthening

form_cue: Rotate about 45 degrees, drop the nose toward the armpit, and let the hand add only feather-light guidance — the stretch is in the back corner of the neck, not from cranking the head down.
stop_condition: Very gentle only. Stop with pinching, dizziness, or tingling into the arm or hand. If the overpressure hurts, drop the hand entirely.
regression: Do it with NO hand pressure — the head position alone stretches the levator for most people.
remediation: If the shoulder on that side hikes up, anchor it down (sit on the hand or hold the chair) before adding the stretch.

name: Neck CARs
desc: Slowly draw the biggest circle you can with your nose, moving through full neck range of motion. Do 3 circles each direction.

phases.label: Slowly draw the biggest circle you can with you...

progression: Add light resistance with hands at sticking points

pairs_with.name: Shoulder CARs
pairs_with.reason: Full joint circles for the whole upper chain

pairs_with.name: Chin Tuck
pairs_with.reason: CARs explore range, chin tucks build control

form_cue: Move only your head and neck, slowly, keeping shoulders down and still and your jaw relaxed. Draw a smooth circle you fully control; it should feel like an easy stretch moving around the neck, never a crunch at the back.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness, light-headedness, visual changes, sharp or pinching pain, or tingling into an arm. Ease off as your head tips back; if looking up brings on symptoms, leave that part out. Stay near a support in case you feel unsteady.
regression: Draw a much smaller circle, or do half circles across the front only (ear to shoulder, chin toward chest, other ear to shoulder). Sitting down is fine.
remediation: If the circle is jerky or your shoulders hike up, shrink it and slow down. Go back to Neck Rotation until turning each way feels smooth, then try small circles again.

name: Isometric Neck Strengthening
desc: Place your palm against your forehead and push your head into it without moving. Hold 5 seconds. Repeat on each side and the back of your head.

pairs_with.name: Chin Tuck
pairs_with.reason: Isometrics build the strength that chin tucks initiate

pairs_with.name: Neck CARs
pairs_with.reason: Mobility plus strength for complete neck health

form_cue: Push the head into the palm with NO actual movement — it's a static hold. Build the force gradually so the head stays perfectly still; don't jerk into it.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness, sharp pain, or symptoms into the arms. Keep the effort moderate — this isn't a max-force test.
regression: Use light pressure (20-30%) and a shorter hold; even gentle isometrics build control.
remediation: If holding still is hard, rest the head against a wall or headrest and press lightly into that first.

name: Neck Flexor Strengthening
desc: Lie on your back, tuck your chin and lift your head just 1 inch off the floor. Hold 5 seconds. This builds deep neck flexor endurance.

phases.label: Lie on your back, tuck your chin and lift your ...

progression: Add slight head rotation while lifted
Progress to lifting head with shoulders off the floor

pairs_with.name: Dead Bug
pairs_with.reason: Both train supine core and neck stability

pairs_with.name: Chin Tuck
pairs_with.reason: Floor version is the progression of seated chin tucks

form_cue: Tuck your chin first, as if making a double chin, then lift your head just clear of the floor and keep the tuck. The effort should be deep in the front of the neck, with your jaw relaxed and your breathing steady.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp neck pain, headache, dizziness, or numbness or tingling into an arm, or if your neck starts to shake hard. Muscle tiredness in the front of the neck is expected; pain or strain at the back of the neck is not.
regression: Do the chin tuck only and leave your head resting on the floor, or lift for a shorter hold and do fewer reps.
remediation: If your chin pokes toward the ceiling as you lift, the tuck has been lost: lower, reset the tuck and lift less. Practise Isometric Neck Strengthening until the tuck holds easily.

name: Suboccipital Release
desc: Lie on your back and place two tennis balls in a sock at the base of your skull. Let your head rest on them and gently nod yes/no for 2 minutes.

phases.label: Lie on your back and place two tennis balls in ...

progression: Use soft balls and minimal weight
Let head sink deeper into the balls
Hold still on tender spots for 30 seconds

pairs_with.name: Jaw Release
pairs_with.reason: Suboccipitals and jaw muscles are neurologically linked

pairs_with.name: Gentle Neck Nod
pairs_with.reason: Active mobility after passive release

form_cue: Rest the balls just under the bony ridge at the base of your skull, one each side of the spine, not on the neck itself. Let your head be heavy and keep the nods and turns tiny and slow. Expect firm, dull pressure.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness, nausea, visual changes, a headache that builds, sharp pain, or numbness or tingling in your face or arms. Dull, tolerable pressure is normal. Sit up slowly afterwards.
regression: Use softer balls or a rolled towel, put a folded towel over the balls to soften them, and stay for a shorter time.
remediation: If you find yourself tensing or holding your breath against the pressure, it is too much: soften the prop and lie still without nodding. Practise Chin Tuck first to learn the small nodding motion.

name: Shoulder Shrug Release
desc: Shrug your shoulders up to your ears, hold 5 seconds, then drop them completely. Repeat 5 times. Focus on the release.

phases.label: Shrug your shoulders up to your ears, hold 5 se...

progression: Focus on the drop being sudden and complete
Hold the shrug for 10 seconds before dropping
Add light weights for more tension-release contrast

pairs_with.name: Upper Trap Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Shrugs release what stretching lengthens

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Rolls
pairs_with.reason: Both warm up the shoulder girdle

form_cue: Shrug straight up toward the ears, then let them DROP and fully release — the value is in the letting-go, not the lift. Keep breathing.
stop_condition: A gentle move; stop with any neck pinch or sharp shoulder pain.
regression: Smaller shrug, or do one shoulder at a time.
remediation: If the shoulders live up near the ears, pair this with scapular depressions to learn the 'down' position.

name: Shoulder Rolls
desc: Roll your shoulders forward in big circles 10 times, then backward 10 times. Keep arms relaxed at your sides.

phases.label: Roll your shoulders forward in big circles 10 t...

progression: Make circles as large as possible
Try to isolate one shoulder at a time
Add resistance by holding light objects

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Shrug Release
pairs_with.reason: Both are shoulder warm-up basics

pairs_with.name: Arm Circles
pairs_with.reason: Progresses from shoulder-only to full arm movement

form_cue: Let the arms hang loose and move only the shoulders: up toward the ears, around and down in a smooth, slow circle. Keep your head still and your chin level. It should feel like easy movement around the shoulders and upper back.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching pain in the shoulder or neck, numbness or tingling down an arm, or dizziness. Painless clicking and a mild feeling of effort are normal; pain is not.
regression: Make the circles smaller and slower, do fewer of them, or do the exercise sitting in a chair.
remediation: If your neck tenses or your head pokes forward, you are forcing the circle. Shrink it, breathe out as the shoulders drop, and practise a simple slow shrug up and down first.

name: Arm Circles
desc: Extend arms to the sides and make small circles, gradually increasing to large circles. Do 15 seconds forward, 15 seconds backward.

phases.label: Extend arms to the sides and make small circles...

progression: Hold light water bottles for added challenge

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Rolls
pairs_with.reason: Arm circles are the next progression from rolls

pairs_with.name: Overhead Reach
pairs_with.reason: Both open up shoulder range of motion

form_cue: Arms straight out to the sides at about shoulder height, then circle from the shoulder joint, starting small. Keep the shoulders down away from your ears and your ribs and trunk still. You should feel the shoulder muscles working.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching pain at the top or front of the shoulder, numbness or tingling in the arm, or dizziness. Tired, warm shoulder muscles are normal effort; a catch or pinch in the joint is not.
regression: Keep the circles small, hold the arms lower than shoulder height, or bend the elbows and circle with your fingertips on your shoulders. Rest partway through if you need to.
remediation: If your shoulders hike up or your back sways, the circles are too big or too fast. Lower the arms, go smaller and slower, and go back to Shoulder Rolls until that is easy.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
desc: Bring one arm across your body at shoulder height and use the other hand to gently pull it closer. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Try different arm heights for varied stretch
Add a gentle rotation toward the stretched arm

pairs_with.name: Overhead Reach
pairs_with.reason: Cross-body and overhead cover different shoulder ranges

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Stretch the front, strengthen the back

form_cue: Bring the arm straight across your chest and hold it above or below the elbow, not on the joint. Keep that shoulder down and your chest facing forward. Feel the stretch in the back of the shoulder.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel pinching in the front or top of the shoulder, sharp pain, or numbness or tingling in the arm. A steady pull in the back of the shoulder is the normal stretch feeling.
regression: Pull less firmly, bring the arm across a little lower than shoulder height, or hold for a shorter time.
remediation: If the shoulder hikes up or your body twists to follow the arm, ease off the pull. Drop the shoulder away from your ear first, square your chest, then draw the arm across only as far as it stays down.

name: Overhead Reach
desc: Interlace your fingers and push palms toward the ceiling. Stretch up tall, hold 10 seconds, lower and repeat 3 times.

phases.label: Interlace your fingers and push palms toward th...

progression: Add a slight lean to each side
Reach up and slightly back for more extension
Hold for 20 seconds with deep breathing

pairs_with.name: Side Bend Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Overhead reach then side bend for full torso opening

pairs_with.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Together they cover overhead and cross-body ranges

form_cue: Interlace the fingers, turn the palms up and reach tall through both arms, with your ribs down and your lower back long rather than arched. Keep breathing. Feel a stretch along your sides, shoulders and upper back.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching at the top of the shoulder, sharp pain, numbness or tingling in the arms or hands, or dizziness or lightheadedness. A lengthening stretch is normal; lower your arms slowly.
regression: Reach only as high as is comfortable, keep the elbows a little bent, reach without interlacing your fingers, or do it sitting in a chair. Use a shorter hold.
remediation: If your lower back arches or your ribs flare as the arms go up, you have run out of shoulder range. Soften the knees, gently draw the ribs down, and stop the reach at the point where your back stays still.

name: Shoulder CARs
desc: Make a fist, then slowly trace the biggest circle you can with your arm, moving through full shoulder range. 3 circles each direction, each arm.
progression: Make the circle as large as possible
Add light resistance band at wrist

pairs_with.name: Neck CARs
pairs_with.reason: Full joint circles for the upper body chain

pairs_with.name: Wall Angel
pairs_with.reason: CARs explore range, wall angels build control in range

form_cue: Stand tall and keep the whole body still while one arm slowly draws the biggest circle it can, as if your trunk were set in concrete. The movement comes only from the shoulder. Go slowest through the stiff spots.
stop_condition: Stop with a sharp pinch or catch in the shoulder, a feeling that the joint is slipping, or numbness or tingling in the arm. Stiffness and muscle effort are normal; work around a painful spot, never through it.
regression: Make a smaller circle that stays inside your comfortable range, relax the fist, or do fewer circles. Standing side-on next to a wall can help you keep the trunk still.
remediation: If your trunk leans or twists or your ribs flare to make the circle bigger, shrink the circle until only the arm moves. Go back to Arm Circles until that feels smooth and easy.

name: Wall Angel
desc: Stand with back against a wall, arms in a goalpost position. Slowly slide arms up overhead and back down, keeping contact with the wall.

phases.label: Stand with back against a wall, arms in a goalp...

progression: Keep lower back flat against wall
Try to keep wrists touching the wall throughout
Slow the movement to 5 seconds up, 5 seconds down
Add a 3-second hold at the top and bottom

pairs_with.name: Thoracic Extension
pairs_with.reason: Both fight rounded posture from different angles

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Wall angels need scapular control

form_cue: Head, upper back and hips rest on the wall with your feet a little way out from it. Slide the arms up and down slowly, keeping your ribs down and lower back from arching. Feel the work between the shoulder blades and a stretch across the chest.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching at the top or front of the shoulder, sharp pain, numbness or tingling in the arms, or neck strain. Effort in the upper back and a chest stretch are normal.
regression: Step your feet further from the wall and bend the knees slightly, slide only part of the way up, or let your wrists come off the wall and keep just the elbows touching.
remediation: If your lower back arches or your head pops off the wall, you have gone past your range. Slide only as high as your back stays put. Practise Overhead Reach first to build the overhead position.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
desc: Stand in a doorway, arms on the frame at 90 degrees. Step forward until you feel a stretch across your chest. Hold 20 seconds.
progression: Try arms at different heights (low, mid, high)
Step one foot forward for a deeper stretch

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Open the front, strengthen the back

pairs_with.name: Wall Angel
pairs_with.reason: Both counter forward-shoulder posture

form_cue: Forearms on the frame with elbows at about shoulder height, then step forward and let the chest move through. Stand tall with ribs down and chin level. Feel the stretch across the chest and the front of the shoulders.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the front of the shoulder, numbness or tingling in the arms or hands, or dizziness. A broad pull across the chest is the normal stretch feeling.
regression: Take a smaller step so the lean is lighter, set the elbows a little lower than shoulder height, or stretch one arm at a time. Use a shorter hold.
remediation: If your lower back arches or your head juts forward, you are leaning too far. Step back, tighten your stomach gently, and lean again only as far as your trunk stays in one straight line.

name: Band Pull-Apart
desc: Hold a resistance band at shoulder height with arms extended. Pull the band apart by squeezing your shoulder blades together. 15 reps.

phases.label: Hold a resistance band at shoulder height with ...

progression: Add a 3-second hold at full pull-apart
Vary the angle: high, mid, and low pull-aparts

pairs_with.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Stretch the front, strengthen the back

pairs_with.name: Wall Angel
pairs_with.reason: Both build posterior shoulder strength

form_cue: Arms straight in front at shoulder height, wrists straight. Start the pull by drawing the shoulder blades back and together, then let the arms open. Shoulders stay down. Feel it between the shoulder blades and at the back of the shoulders.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching in the front of the shoulder, neck strain, sharp pain, or numbness or tingling in the arms. Tired muscles between the shoulder blades are normal effort. Check the band for nicks and do not pull it toward your face.
regression: Use a lighter band, hold it with your hands wider apart so there is less tension, pull only part of the way, or do fewer reps.
remediation: If your shoulders shrug up or you lean back to finish the pull, the band is too strong. Lighten it, and practise Scapular Squeeze first to find the shoulder blade movement without resistance.

name: External Rotation with Band
desc: Hold a band with elbows bent 90 degrees at your sides. Rotate forearms outward against the band. 12 reps. Builds rotator cuff strength.

phases.label: Hold a band with elbows bent 90 degrees at your...

progression: Add a 2-second hold at end range
Progress to side-lying external rotation for more range

pairs_with.name: Band Pull-Apart
pairs_with.reason: Both strengthen the posterior shoulder

pairs_with.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Stretch internal rotators, strengthen external rotators

form_cue: Keep the elbows tucked against your sides and bent to 90 degrees, wrists straight. Turn the forearms outward like a door opening on a hinge, then return slowly. Feel it in the back of the shoulders.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching pain in the shoulder, pain down the arm, or numbness or tingling. A deep, tired effort at the back of the shoulder is normal. Check the band for nicks before you use it.
regression: Use a lighter band, hold it with less tension to start, turn out through a smaller range, or do fewer reps. You can also do one arm at a time.
remediation: If your elbows drift away from your sides or you lean back, the band is too strong. Hold a small rolled towel between each elbow and your ribs as a check, and go back to Band Pull-Apart if it stays hard.

name: Shoulder Internal Rotation Stretch
desc: Place the back of your hand against a door frame at waist height behind you. Gently turn your body away to stretch the front of the shoulder. 20 seconds each side.
progression: Very gentle rotation, stop at first stretch
Vary hand height for different fibers

pairs_with.name: External Rotation with Band
pairs_with.reason: Stretch internal rotation, strengthen external rotation

pairs_with.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both open up the anterior shoulder

form_cue: Stand tall with the back of your hand resting on the frame behind you at waist height. Turn your chest slowly away, keeping the shoulder back and down rather than rolling forward. Feel a mild stretch in the front of the shoulder.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the front of the shoulder, a feeling that the shoulder is shifting or unstable, or numbness or tingling in the arm or hand. Check with a clinician first if this shoulder has ever dislocated.
regression: Turn away only a few degrees and stop at the first hint of stretch, place the hand lower than waist height, or use a shorter hold.
remediation: If the shoulder rolls forward or you lean your trunk to reach the frame, stand closer and turn less. If you cannot get the hand behind you comfortably, stay with Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch.

name: Shoulder Flexion with Dowel
desc: Hold a broomstick with both hands wider than shoulder width. Slowly raise it overhead and behind your head as far as comfortable. 8 reps.

phases.label: Hold a broomstick with both hands wider than sh...

progression: Wide grip, small range of motion
Full range overhead to behind back
Add a pause at the most challenging point

pairs_with.name: Wall Angel
pairs_with.reason: Both work overhead shoulder mobility

pairs_with.name: Thoracic Extension
pairs_with.reason: Thoracic mobility enables full overhead reach

form_cue: Wide grip, arms long, ribs down. Raise the stick slowly and evenly with both arms and stop where the shoulders stop moving comfortably, not where you can push it. Feel a stretch in the shoulders, chest and under the arms.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching at the top of the shoulder, sharp pain, a slipping or unstable feeling, numbness or tingling, or dizziness. Never force the stick behind your head. Skip this if a shoulder has dislocated, unless a clinician has cleared it.
regression: Take a wider grip and raise the stick only to forehead height or just overhead, without going behind the head. You can also do it lying on your back, or do fewer reps.
remediation: If your lower back arches, your head pushes forward or one arm lags, you are past your range. Stop the lift where the ribs stay down. Practise Wall Angel until overhead reach is comfortable.

name: Scapular Squeeze
desc: Sit tall, squeeze your shoulder blades together as if pinching a pencil between them. Hold 5 seconds, release. Repeat 10 times.

phases.label: Sit tall, squeeze your shoulder blades together...

progression: Add arms in a W position for more activation

pairs_with.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen the back while opening the front

pairs_with.name: Chin Tuck
pairs_with.reason: Both fight desk posture from different areas

form_cue: Drive it from the shoulder blades pulling DOWN and together (retraction + depression), not from shrugging up. Think 'blades toward your back pockets'; chest stays soft, and don't arch the low back to fake range.
stop_condition: Stop if your shoulders rise toward your ears, if you feel pinching in the front of the shoulder, or any neck strain. The work belongs between the shoulder blades, not in the neck or upper traps.
regression: Reduce the squeeze to a gentle ~30% effort with a brief hold, or do it lying on your back so the floor gives feedback and gravity assists.
remediation: If the upper traps dominate (shoulders rise), the lower traps / scapular depressors need work first: practice slow scapular depressions (slide the blades down without squeezing) before adding the squeeze.

name: Thoracic Extension

phases.label: Sit on a chair, clasp hands behind your head, a...

progression: Small range over a thick cushion on the chair
Use a foam roller under the upper back on the floor
Add deep breathing in the extended position

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow

form_cue: Arch the UPPER back over the chair edge to open the chest — the movement is in the mid-back, not the low back. Support the head with the hands; don't crank the neck.
stop_condition: Keep it gentle and in the mid-back. Stop with low-back pinching (you're arching too low), sharp pain, or dizziness.
regression: Reduce the arch, or do it without clasping the head — just open the arms and lift the chest.
remediation: If the low back takes over, brace the core lightly and keep the ribs down so the motion stays in the thoracic spine.

name: Thoracic Rotation
desc: Sit tall with arms crossed over your chest. Rotate your torso to the right, hold 5 seconds, then to the left. Repeat 8 times each side.
progression: Add arms extended forward for more lever
Exhale into the rotation for deeper range

pairs_with.name: Thoracic Extension
pairs_with.reason: Rotation plus extension covers all upper back motion

pairs_with.name: Seated Twist
pairs_with.reason: Different positions for thoracic rotation

form_cue: Rotate from the mid-back with arms crossed, keeping the hips and pelvis facing forward — turn the ribcage, not the whole body. Sit tall throughout.
stop_condition: Gentle rotation only; stop with sharp back pain or anything radiating.
regression: Reduce the turn; small controlled range beats forcing depth.
remediation: If the hips swivel, plant the feet and squeeze the seat to keep the base still, isolating the mid-back.

name: Cat-Cow
desc: On all fours, arch your back up (cat), then dip it down (cow). Move slowly with your breath. Flow smoothly for 10 reps.

phases.label: 10 cycles — arch up, dip down, breathe

progression: Exaggerate the arch and the drop
Add a side bend component by looking at your hip

pairs_with.name: Child's Pose
pairs_with.reason: Cat-cow mobilizes, child's pose rests the spine

pairs_with.reason: Both work spinal extension/flexion

form_cue: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips. Round the whole spine up toward the ceiling, then let the chest and belly sink, moving slowly with your breath. Spread the movement along the whole back instead of hinging at one spot.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching back pain, tingling down an arm or leg, dizziness, or wrist or knee pain that does not ease. A gentle stretch along the spine is normal; pain is not.
regression: Make both the arch and the dip much smaller and do fewer reps. If your wrists or knees object, kneel on a folded towel or do the same rounding and arching sitting on a chair with hands on your thighs.
remediation: If the movement all comes from your low back or your elbows keep bending, slow down and shrink the range. Keep the arms straight and think of moving one section of the spine at a time.

name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
desc: Lie on a foam roller placed across your upper back. Support your head with hands, and gently extend over the roller. Roll up and down the upper back.

phases.label: Lie on a foam roller placed across your upper back

progression: Place roller at mid-back, small extensions
Move roller to different segments of upper back
Hold extensions for 10 seconds at each level
Add arms overhead while extending for deeper stretch

pairs_with.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Foam roller opens the back, doorway opens the front

pairs_with.name: Wall Angel
pairs_with.reason: Use improved mobility from rolling in wall angels

form_cue: Roller sits across the upper back, never the low back or neck. Knees bent, feet flat, hips down, head cradled in your hands. Lean back gently over the roller so the bend comes from between the shoulder blades, and keep your ribs from flaring.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching spine pain, rib pain, dizziness, neck strain, or tingling into the arms. Pressure and a stretch across the upper back are normal. Check with a clinician first if you have osteoporosis or a past spinal fracture.
regression: Keep your hips on the floor and only lean back a little without rolling, or use a rolled towel in place of the roller. A shorter time is fine.
remediation: If your low back arches or your neck drops back, lower the ribs, tuck the chin slightly and take a smaller lean. If it still feels uncontrolled, practise Thoracic Extension first.

name: Thread the Needle
desc: From hands and knees, reach one arm under your body toward the opposite side, rotating your upper back. Hold 10 seconds, return. 5 each side.
progression: Let your shoulder and ear rest on the ground
Reach the top arm toward the ceiling for an active twist

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow
pairs_with.reason: Warm up with cat-cow before threading the needle

pairs_with.name: Open Book Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both are thoracic rotation exercises in different positions

form_cue: Start on hands and knees with hips over knees. Slide one arm, palm up, under your chest and let the upper back turn to follow it while the hips stay put. You should feel a stretch across the back of the shoulder and between the shoulder blades.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp shoulder or neck pain, pinching in the low back, numbness or tingling in the arm, or dizziness with your head lowered. A pulling stretch in the upper back is normal.
regression: Reach only a short way under and keep your head up off the floor, with a shorter hold or fewer reps. Put a folded towel under your knees if they are sore.
remediation: If your hips swing sideways or you collapse onto the shoulder, reduce the reach and keep pressing the floor away with the supporting hand. Practise Thoracic Rotation first if the twist feels stuck.

name: Open Book Stretch
desc: Lie on your side with knees bent. Open your top arm across your body like a book opening, following it with your eyes. Hold 15 seconds each side.
progression: Rotate only as far as comfortable
Try to get both shoulders flat on the floor
Hold for 30 seconds with deep breathing
Add a pec stretch by sliding the top arm overhead

pairs_with.name: Thread the Needle
pairs_with.reason: Both are thoracic rotation in different planes

pairs_with.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Open book also stretches the chest

form_cue: Lie on your side, knees bent and stacked, arms straight out in front with palms together. Lift the top arm up and over to open your chest toward the ceiling, eyes following the hand, knees staying together. Feel it across the chest and upper back.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching pain in the shoulder, back or neck, or numbness or tingling down the arm. A stretch across the chest and mid-back is normal; do not force the arm toward the floor.
regression: Open only partway and rest the arm on a pillow placed behind you. Put a pillow under your head and another between your knees, and use a shorter hold.
remediation: If your top knee lifts or your hips roll back with you, the twist has moved to the low back. Pin the knees together, make the opening smaller, or practise Thoracic Rotation first.

name: Prone Y Raise
desc: Lie face down with arms in a Y position. Lift both arms a few inches off the floor by squeezing your mid-back. Hold 3 seconds, lower. 10 reps.

phases.label: Lie face down with arms in a Y position

pairs_with.name: Prone T Raise
pairs_with.reason: Y and T raises together hit all mid-back muscles

pairs_with.name: Band Pull-Apart
pairs_with.reason: Standing and prone versions of similar muscle work

form_cue: Lie face down, forehead on a small towel, arms overhead in a Y with thumbs up. Draw the shoulder blades down and back, then lift the arms just a few inches. The work belongs between and below the shoulder blades, not in the neck.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching at the top or front of the shoulder, neck strain, low-back pain, or tingling in the arms. Muscle effort and mild tiredness in the mid-back are normal.
regression: Lower the arms to a wider, lower V and make the lift tiny, or lift one arm at a time. A shorter hold and fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your shoulders shrug toward your ears or your chin lifts, lower the arms and reset the shoulder blades down before each lift. If that keeps happening, go back to Scapular Squeeze.

name: Prone T Raise
desc: Lie face down with arms out to the sides in a T position. Lift both arms by squeezing shoulder blades. Hold 3 seconds, lower. 10 reps.

phases.label: Lie face down with arms out to the sides in a T...

pairs_with.name: Prone Y Raise
pairs_with.reason: T and Y together build complete mid-back strength

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Same muscles, different position

form_cue: Lie face down, forehead on a small towel, arms straight out to the sides with thumbs up. Squeeze the shoulder blades together to lift the arms a little, keeping the neck long. Feel it between the shoulder blades.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching in the front of the shoulder, neck strain, low-back pain, or tingling in the arms. Muscle effort between the shoulder blades is normal.
regression: Bend your elbows so the arms are shorter, lift only an inch, or lift one arm at a time. A shorter hold and fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your shoulders hike up, your chin lifts or your low back arches, make the lift smaller and keep your forehead down. If you still cannot feel the shoulder blades working, go back to Scapular Squeeze.

name: Sphinx Pose
desc: Lie face down, prop up on your forearms with elbows under shoulders. Gently press your chest forward and up. Hold 30 seconds.

phases.label: Lie face down, prop up on your forearms with el...

progression: Progress to cobra with straight arms

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow
pairs_with.reason: Both work spinal extension

pairs_with.name: Child's Pose
pairs_with.reason: Sphinx extends, child's pose flexes — good pair

form_cue: Lie face down with elbows under shoulders and forearms flat. Draw the chest gently forward and up while the hips and legs stay heavy on the floor. Keep the shoulders away from your ears and your gaze slightly ahead, neck long.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching low-back pain, pain or tingling running into the buttock or leg, or neck pain. A mild feeling of compression or stretch in the back and front of the trunk is normal.
regression: Slide your elbows further forward so the chest is lower, or rest on a pillow under your chest. Hold for a shorter time.
remediation: If you sink between your shoulders or clench your buttocks, press the forearms lightly into the floor and relax the legs. If the low back still pinches, lower the chest until it eases.

name: Seated Twist
desc: Sit tall, place your right hand on your left knee and twist your torso to the left. Hold 15 seconds, repeat on the other side.
progression: Use the hand on the knee to deepen the twist slightly
Exhale into the twist for more range

pairs_with.name: Thoracic Rotation
pairs_with.reason: Both target seated thoracic rotation

pairs_with.name: Side Bend Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Twist and side bend cover all seated spinal movements

form_cue: Sit tall and rotate the ribcage, using the hand on the knee only as a light gauge — not a lever to wrench yourself around. Grow taller as you turn; don't collapse.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching back pain, or anything shooting down a leg. This is mobility, not a max stretch.
regression: Use less rotation and don't pull on the knee; a gentle turn is enough.
remediation: Keep the spine long — rotation on a tall spine is safer than cranking on a slumped one.

name: Standing Back Extension
desc: Place hands on your lower back and gently lean backward, arching your spine. Hold 5 seconds, return upright. Repeat 5 times.

phases.label: Place hands on your lower back and gently lean ...

progression: Small lean, hands supporting lower back
Add a deep inhale while extended

pairs_with.name: Standing Forward Fold
pairs_with.reason: Extension and flexion balance the lower back

pairs_with.name: Pelvic Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Both address lower back mobility

form_cue: Stand with feet hip-width, knees soft, hands on the back of your pelvis for support. Lean back slowly from the spine, hips staying over your feet, eyes forward instead of tipping the head back. It should feel like mild pressure in the low back.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness, unsteadiness, sharp back pain, or pain or tingling spreading into the buttock or leg. Stand with a counter or sturdy chair within reach in case you lose balance.
regression: Lean back only a little, with a shorter hold and fewer reps, and keep the back of your thighs against a counter for support.
remediation: If your knees bend, your hips push far forward or your head drops back, you are swaying instead of arching. Shorten the lean, look straight ahead, and keep your weight over the middle of your feet.

name: Pelvic Tilt
desc: Lie on your back with knees bent. Flatten your lower back into the floor by tilting your pelvis. Hold 5 seconds, release. Repeat 10 times.

phases.label: Lie on your back with knees bent

progression: Small tilts, find the neutral position
Add a march (alternating foot lifts) while holding tilt
Progress to pelvic tilts with feet on a wall

pairs_with.name: Bridge
pairs_with.reason: Pelvic tilts teach the motion, bridges add strength

pairs_with.name: Dead Bug
pairs_with.reason: Both build supine core control

form_cue: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Gently tip your pelvis so the low back flattens into the floor, using the lower belly, not by pushing with your feet or squeezing your buttocks. Keep breathing; this is a small movement.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp back pain, pain or tingling down a leg, or cramping that does not settle. Light effort in the lower belly is normal; your breath should never be held.
regression: Make the tilt smaller and hold it more briefly, with fewer reps. A pillow under your head and a slow rock between a little arch and a little flattening is enough.
remediation: If your hips lift or your buttocks grip hard, you are bridging instead of tilting. Put a hand under your low back and practise pressing it lightly, then releasing, until the motion feels easy.

name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
desc: Lie on your back, pull one knee toward your chest with both hands. Hold 20 seconds, switch sides. Finish with both knees together.
progression: Gently pull knee to comfortable range
Rock gently side to side with knees pulled in
Add a chin tuck while pulling knee in

pairs_with.name: Pelvic Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Both decompress the lower back

pairs_with.name: Supine Twist
pairs_with.reason: Knee-to-chest then twist for complete lower back relief

form_cue: Lie on your back and draw one knee toward your chest with both hands, keeping your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor. Pull gently and steadily. You should feel a stretch in the low back and buttock.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching in the front of the hip, sharp back pain, knee pain, or tingling down the leg. A gentle pulling stretch is normal. After a hip replacement, check with your surgeon or physical therapist before doing this.
regression: Hold behind the thigh instead of over the shin and pull only partway, keeping the other knee bent with the foot flat. Skip the both-knees finish, or use a shorter hold.
remediation: If your head and shoulders lift or you tug with your arms, ease off and rest your head on a pillow. If your hands cannot reach comfortably, loop a towel behind the thigh.

name: Supine Twist
desc: Lie on your back, drop both knees to one side while keeping shoulders on the floor. Arms in a T. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Knees bent at 90 degrees, gentle drop to each side
Extend the top leg for a deeper stretch
Look in the opposite direction from your knees

pairs_with.name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Flexion then rotation for full lower back release

pairs_with.name: Open Book Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both are rotational stretches in supine/side-lying

form_cue: Lie on your back with arms out in a T and knees bent. Lower both knees slowly to one side, letting gravity do the work, while both shoulders stay heavy on the floor. Feel the stretch through the low back and outer hip.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching back pain, pain or tingling down a leg, or pain in the hip. A gentle twisting stretch is normal; do not push the knees down with your hand.
regression: Lower the knees only partway and rest them on a pillow or cushion beside you. A shorter hold is fine.
remediation: If the opposite shoulder lifts off the floor, you have gone further than your back can twist. Bring the knees back up until the shoulder settles, and stay there.

name: Bird Dog
desc: From hands and knees, extend your right arm and left leg simultaneously. Hold 5 seconds, switch sides. 8 reps per side.
progression: Just extend the arm, then just the leg
Extend arm and leg together, 5-second holds
Add slow elbow-to-knee crunch between reps
Hold for 10 seconds, 10 reps per side

pairs_with.name: Dead Bug
pairs_with.reason: Bird dog and dead bug are complementary core stabilizers

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow
pairs_with.reason: Warm up with cat-cow, then challenge with bird dog

form_cue: From hands and knees, brace your belly lightly, then slide one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your trunk, no higher. Keep your back flat and hips square to the floor, eyes down.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp back pain, pain or tingling into a leg or arm, wrist or shoulder pain, or if you wobble and cannot steady yourself. Muscle effort around the trunk and hip is normal.
regression: Move just the arm, then just the leg, or keep the toes of the moving leg touching the floor as you slide it back. A shorter hold and fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your low back sags or your hips tip to one side, do not lift the leg as high and reach long instead. If you cannot keep the trunk still, practise Pelvic Tilt first to find a steady low back.

name: Bridge
desc: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat. Press hips toward the ceiling, squeezing your glutes at top. Hold 5 seconds, lower. 10 reps.

phases.label: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat

progression: Full lift to one straight line, 5-second holds
Single-leg bridge (extend one leg at the top)
Add a resistance band above knees

pairs_with.name: Pelvic Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Pelvic tilts teach the movement, bridges build strength

pairs_with.name: Clamshell
pairs_with.reason: Both strengthen the glutes that support the lower back

form_cue: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width. Press through your heels and lift the hips until shoulders, hips and knees make a line, no higher. The work belongs in the buttocks, with ribs down and the low back not arched.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp back pain, knee pain, pain or tingling down a leg, or a hamstring cramp that does not ease. Muscle effort in the buttocks and back of the thighs is normal.
regression: Lift the hips only a couple of inches, with a shorter hold and fewer reps.
remediation: If you feel it mostly in the low back or the hamstrings cramp, lower the hips slightly and bring the feet a little closer. Start each rep with a Pelvic Tilt, then lift.

name: Child's Pose
desc: Kneel and sit back on your heels, reaching arms forward on the floor. Let your forehead rest down. Breathe deeply for 60 seconds.

phases.label: Kneel and sit back on your heels, reaching arms...

Walk hands to one side for a lateral stretch
Hold for 2 minutes with focused breathing

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow
pairs_with.reason: Active mobility then passive rest for the spine

pairs_with.name: Sphinx Pose
pairs_with.reason: Child's pose flexes, sphinx extends — balance the spine

form_cue: Kneel, sit your hips back toward your heels and walk your hands forward, letting the chest sink and the forehead rest. Breathe slowly into your back. You should feel a gentle stretch along the low back, hips and shoulders.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp knee, hip or ankle pain, pinching in the front of the hips, dizziness with your head down, or tingling in the feet. A gentle stretch is normal. Skip it after a knee or hip replacement unless you have been cleared.
regression: Put a pillow between your heels and buttocks and rest your forehead on stacked fists or a cushion, with a shorter hold. If kneeling is not possible, sit on a chair and fold forward over your thighs.
remediation: If your hips will not go back or your shoulders tense up, do not force them. Widen the knees a little, shorten the reach, and let the weight rest on your props.

name: Seated Lower Back Flexion
desc: Sit at the edge of your chair. Slowly round forward, letting your hands hang toward the floor between your knees. Hold 15 seconds, sit back up slowly.

progression: Round forward gently, hands on thighs
Hang toward the floor, hold 15 seconds
Alternate between rounding forward and sitting tall 5 times

pairs_with.reason: Flexion and extension balance the lower back

pairs_with.name: Seated Twist

form_cue: Slowly round forward and let the head and arms hang heavy, one segment at a time — a gentle flexion, not a fast flop. Come up slowly, stacking the spine.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp pain or any tingling/numbness down the legs. If flexion is your provocative direction, skip it. Rise slowly to avoid dizziness.
regression: Round only partway, or rest the hands on the thighs to support some weight on the way down and up.
remediation: If standing up makes you lightheaded, pause halfway. If flexion aggravates the back, favor extension-biased moves instead.

name: Prone Press-Up

form_cue: Lie face down with hands under shoulders. Press the chest up with your arms while the hips, buttocks and legs stay relaxed and heavy on the floor. Keep the shoulders away from the ears and go only as high as is comfortable.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching low-back pain, or pain, numbness or tingling that spreads into the buttock or leg. Mild pressure in the low back that eases when you lower is normal.
regression: Press up only onto your forearms, or move your hands further forward so the lift is lower. A shorter hold and fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your hips lift or you clench your buttocks, you have gone too high. Lower until the hips rest again, and practise Sphinx Pose until that position is comfortable.

name: Side-Lying Trunk Rotation

form_cue: Lie on your side with knees bent and stacked, arms out in front. Turn your top arm, chest and head open toward the ceiling while the knees stay together on the floor. Feel the stretch through the trunk and chest.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching back pain, shoulder pain, or pain or tingling into an arm or leg. A stretch through the waist and chest is normal; do not force the shoulder toward the floor.
regression: Turn only partway and rest the arm on a pillow behind you, with a pillow under your head and a shorter hold.
remediation: If your top knee slides back or lifts, hold it down with your lower hand and turn less. If the twist still feels stuck or uncomfortable, return to Supine Twist.

name: Superman Hold

form_cue: Lie face down, forehead toward the floor and neck long. Squeeze your buttocks and reach arms and legs long, lifting them only an inch or two. Feel the muscles along the spine and buttocks working, with no sharp pressure in the low back.
stop_condition: Safety: this loads the low back strongly. Stop at once with sharp or pinching back pain, pain or tingling into a leg, or neck strain. Skip it and ask a clinician first if you have osteoporosis or a known back condition.
regression: Lift only your arms, or only your legs, or one arm with the opposite leg, and barely clear the floor. A shorter hold and fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If you jerk up, crane your neck or hold your breath, the lift is too high. Reach long and low instead, and go back to Bird Dog until you can hold that steadily.

name: Doorway Pec Stretch

Try arm higher (120 degrees) and lower (60 degrees)

form_cue: Forearm upright on the frame with the elbow at shoulder height. Step through with the foot on the same side and let your chest turn slightly away from the arm. Keep the shoulder down. Feel the stretch in the chest and front of the shoulder.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the front of the shoulder, or numbness or tingling in the arm or hand. A steady pull across the chest is the normal stretch feeling.
regression: Take a smaller step so the stretch is lighter, set the elbow a little below shoulder height, or use a shorter hold.
remediation: If the shoulder hikes toward your ear or your back arches, you have stepped too far. Step back, draw the shoulder blade gently down and back, then ease forward again with your ribs down.

name: Chest Opener on Wall
desc: Stand facing a wall, place one palm on the wall at shoulder height. Rotate your body away from the wall hand until you feel a chest stretch. Hold 20 seconds each side.

pairs_with.name: Doorway Pec Stretch

form_cue: Palm flat on the wall at shoulder height with the elbow soft, not locked. Turn your feet and chest away from that hand slowly, keeping the shoulder down. Feel the stretch across the chest, front of the shoulder and sometimes the upper arm.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the front of the shoulder, pain at the elbow or wrist, or numbness or tingling in the arm or hand. A broad pull across the chest is normal.
regression: Turn away only a little, place the hand slightly lower than shoulder height, bend the elbow more, or use a shorter hold.
remediation: If the shoulder rolls forward or shrugs up as you turn, you have gone too far. Come back, set the shoulder blade gently back and down, and turn only as far as it stays there.

name: Chest Expansion Stretch
desc: Clasp hands behind your back, straighten your arms and lift them up while squeezing shoulder blades together. Hold 15 seconds.

phases.label: Clasp hands behind your back, straighten your a...

Use a towel between hands if clasping is difficult

form_cue: Stand tall, clasp the hands behind you, draw the shoulder blades together and lift the hands only as far as you can without tipping forward. Chin level, ribs down. Feel the stretch across the chest and the front of the shoulders.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the front of the shoulder, pain at the elbows or wrists, numbness or tingling in the hands, or neck strain. A stretch across the chest is the normal feeling.
regression: Hold a towel between your hands instead of clasping, keep the elbows slightly bent, and lift the hands less, or simply squeeze the shoulder blades together without lifting.
remediation: If your shoulders roll forward, your head juts out or you bend at the waist to lift higher, lower the hands. Squeeze the shoulder blades together first, then lift only while your chest stays open.

name: Floor Angel
desc: Lie on your back with knees bent. Arms in a goalpost position, try to keep arms flat on the floor while sliding them overhead and back down. 10 reps.

phases.label: Lie on your back with knees bent

progression: Focus on keeping lower back flat
Try to keep wrists on the floor throughout
Slow to 5 seconds up, 5 seconds down
Place a foam roller lengthwise under your spine for added stretch

pairs_with.reason: Both open the chest in a supine position

form_cue: On your back with knees bent and your lower back resting easily on the floor. Slide the arms slowly along the floor overhead and back, keeping your ribs down. Feel a chest stretch and gentle work in the upper back.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching at the top or front of the shoulder, sharp pain, numbness or tingling in the arms, or neck strain. A stretch across the chest and mild upper-back effort are normal.
regression: Slide only part of the way up, let the wrists lift off the floor and keep just the elbows down, put a small pillow under your head, or do fewer reps.
remediation: If your ribs flare or your lower back arches off the floor as the arms rise, stop the slide just before that happens. If getting up and down from the floor is hard, do Wall Angel instead.

name: Prone Chest Lift

form_cue: Face down, fingertips resting lightly behind your head and elbows wide. Lift the chest a little by squeezing the shoulder blades back and down, looking at the floor so your neck stays long. Feel it in the upper and mid back.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching pain in the lower back, pain or tingling into the legs, neck pain, or dizziness. Tired upper-back muscles are normal effort. Do not pull on your head with your hands.
regression: Rest your hands on your lower back or by your sides instead of behind your head, lift only an inch or so, use a shorter hold, or do fewer reps.
remediation: If you feel it mostly in your lower back or your chin pokes up, the lift is too high. Lower it, tighten your buttocks gently and keep your eyes on the floor. Practise Sphinx Pose first if lying face down and lifting is uncomfortable.

name: Foam Roller Chest Opener

stop_condition: Stop with numbness or tingling in the arms or hands, sharp pain in the shoulder or back, neck strain, or dizziness. Get on and off slowly by sitting on one end and rolling to your side. A gentle chest stretch is normal.

name: Wall Push-Up
desc: Stand arm's length from a wall, place palms on it at shoulder height. Do push-ups against the wall, 12-15 reps. Great for building chest strength safely.

phases.label: Stand arm's length from a wall, place palms on ...

progression: Step further from wall for more difficulty
Slow to 3 seconds down, 3 seconds up
Progress to incline push-ups on a countertop

pairs_with.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen then stretch the chest

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Push-up works the front, squeeze works the back

form_cue: Hands on the wall at shoulder height, a little wider than your shoulders. Keep your body in one straight line from head to heels and bend the elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, then press away. Feel it in the chest, shoulders and arms.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp pain in the shoulder, elbow or wrist, pinching in the front of the shoulder, chest pain or pressure, or dizziness. Muscle effort is normal. Stand on a non-slip floor so your feet cannot slide.
regression: Stand closer to the wall, bend the elbows only part of the way, or do fewer reps and rest.
remediation: If your hips sag or stick out, or your head leads toward the wall, step closer and tighten your stomach and buttocks. Move as one plank, with elbows angled down and back rather than flared straight out.

name: Dead Bug
desc: Lie on your back, arms pointing up, knees bent 90 degrees. Slowly extend one arm overhead and the opposite leg out straight, then return. Alternate for 10 reps per side.

phases.label: Lie on your back, arms pointing up, knees bent ...

progression: Move just the arms, keep legs still
Opposite arm and leg, 8 reps each side
Slow the movement to 3 seconds out, 3 seconds back
Add a resistance band around feet

pairs_with.name: Bird Dog
pairs_with.reason: Dead bug and bird dog are the front/back core duo

pairs_with.name: Pelvic Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Pelvic tilts teach the flat-back position dead bugs need

form_cue: Keep your lower back gently in contact with the floor the whole time and move slowly. Only reach the arm and leg as far as you can without your back arching or ribs flaring. You should feel your belly working, not your back.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel sharp or pinching pain in your lower back, hip or shoulder, or if your back keeps arching off the floor. Steady effort in the belly is normal; pain or strain in the back is not.
regression: Move just the arms and keep both feet resting on the floor, or slide one heel along the floor instead of lifting the leg. A smaller reach and fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your back arches as the leg goes out, the reach is too long: shorten it and keep the knee bent. Practise Pelvic Tilt first to learn how to hold your lower back steady.

name: Pallof Press (Band)
desc: Anchor a band at chest height and stand SIDEWAYS to it — that side-on position is what creates the twisting force. Hold the band with both hands at the center of your chest, brace your core, and press it straight out in front of you without letting your shoulders or hips rotate toward the anchor. Bring it back slowly, then turn around and do the other side. Hold 5 seconds, return. 8 reps each side.
progression: Add a step away from the anchor for more resistance
Try single-leg Pallof press for balance challenge

pairs_with.name: Bird Dog
pairs_with.reason: Both train anti-rotation core stability

pairs_with.name: Side Plank
pairs_with.reason: Both resist lateral forces on the core

form_cue: Stand tall with feet about hip width and knees soft, and press the band straight out from the middle of your chest. Hips and shoulders stay facing forward. You should feel the muscles around your waist working to stop the twist.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your lower back or shoulder, or if the band pulls you off balance. Check that the anchor is secure before every set. Effort around the waist is normal; a pinch or pull in the back is not.
regression: Use a lighter band or stand closer to the anchor, and press only part of the way out with a shorter hold. You can also do it sitting tall on a sturdy chair.
remediation: If you twist toward the anchor or your shoulders shrug up, there is too much tension: step closer and shorten the press. Practise Dead Bug to build steady trunk control first.

name: Plank Hold
desc: Hold a forearm plank position with your body in a straight line from head to heels. Keep your core braced. Hold as long as you can up to 60 seconds.

phases.label: Hold a forearm plank position with your body in...

progression: Start on knees if needed, hold 20 seconds
Add shoulder taps while holding plank

pairs_with.name: Side Plank
pairs_with.reason: Front and side planks for complete core stability

pairs_with.name: Bird Dog
pairs_with.reason: Dynamic and static core challenges

form_cue: Elbows under your shoulders, body in one line from head to heels, eyes on the floor so your neck stays long. Gently tighten your belly and buttocks and keep breathing. You should feel it across the front of your trunk.
stop_condition: Stop as soon as your hips sag or you feel pain in your lower back, shoulders or neck, or if you catch yourself holding your breath. Shaking from effort is normal; a pinch or ache in the lower back means the hold is over.
regression: Do it with your knees on the floor, or with your forearms on a sturdy bench, counter or wall. Take a shorter hold and rest when your form starts to slip.
remediation: The usual faults are hips sagging or lifting high in the air. End the hold when that happens rather than pushing on; a shorter hold in good form counts for more. Practise Dead Bug to build the control.

name: Side Plank
desc: Lie on your side, prop up on your forearm, lift your hips to make a straight line. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Add hip dips (lower and lift hips 10 times)

pairs_with.name: Plank Hold
pairs_with.reason: Front and side planks together for full core stability

pairs_with.name: Pallof Press (Band)
pairs_with.reason: Both build anti-lateral-flexion strength

form_cue: Elbow directly under your shoulder, hips stacked one above the other, and lift until your body is one straight line. Keep your neck in line with your spine and keep breathing. You should feel the side of your waist nearest the floor.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel sharp or pinching pain in the supporting shoulder, your lower back or your neck, or if your hips drop and you cannot lift them again. Effort in the side of the waist is normal.
regression: Keep the bottom knee bent and resting on the floor and lift from knees to shoulders. Take a shorter hold if you need to.
remediation: If your hips sag, roll forward or back, or the shoulder sinks toward your ear, lower down and rest. Use the bent-knee version and a shorter hold, and build your Plank Hold first.

name: Seated Core Brace
desc: Sit tall, tighten your core as if bracing for a light punch to the stomach. Hold 10 seconds while breathing normally. Repeat 5 times.

phases.label: Sit tall, tighten your core as if bracing for a...

progression: Brace while lifting one foot slightly off the floor
Brace while slowly rotating side to side

pairs_with.name: Pelvic Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Both teach core activation in simple positions

pairs_with.name: Seated Marching
pairs_with.reason: Brace the core, then add limb movement

form_cue: Firm the whole trunk to a moderate 30-40% brace — as if expecting a light poke — and KEEP BREATHING. Don't suck the belly in or hold your breath.
stop_condition: Stop if you hold your breath and get lightheaded, or with any sharp back pain. It's a gentle brace, not a max clench.
regression: Lighter brace, shorter hold; even a soft co-contraction counts.
remediation: If you can't brace and breathe at once, practice diaphragmatic breathing first, then add a light brace on top.

name: Seated Marching
desc: Sit tall with core braced. Slowly lift one knee, lower it, then lift the other. Alternate for 20 marches total. Keep your torso still.
progression: Lift knees higher, maintain tall posture
Add a 3-second hold at the top of each lift
Add opposite arm reach while lifting knee

pairs_with.name: Seated Core Brace
pairs_with.reason: Brace first, then challenge with movement

pairs_with.name: Standing March
pairs_with.reason: Seated then standing progression

form_cue: Keep the core lightly braced and the spine tall, and lift each knee without rocking the pelvis or leaning back — the trunk stays quiet while the legs move.
stop_condition: Stop with low-back pain, or if you have to swing or lean to lift the knee. Keep it controlled.
regression: Lift the knee less high, or slide the heel forward instead of lifting.
remediation: If the pelvis rocks, master the Seated Core Brace first so the trunk can stay still.

name: Bicycle Crunch
desc: Lie on your back, hands behind head. Bring right elbow to left knee while extending right leg, then switch. Alternate for 20 reps total.

phases.label: Lie on your back, hands behind head

progression: Add a hold on each side for 2 seconds

pairs_with.name: Dead Bug
pairs_with.reason: Dead bug builds control, bicycle crunch adds intensity

pairs_with.name: Plank Hold
pairs_with.reason: Rotational and anti-extension core work

form_cue: Rest your head lightly in your hands with elbows wide and turn from the ribs so the shoulder moves toward the opposite knee. Do not pull on your neck. Keep your lower back heavy on the floor and move slowly; feel it in the belly.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel neck pain or strain, sharp lower back pain, or pain in the front of the hip. If you have been told to avoid bending or twisting your spine, check with a clinician before doing this one.
regression: Keep your head and shoulders resting on the floor and just pedal the legs slowly, or keep the straight leg higher off the floor. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If you are tugging on your head or your back is arching off the floor, slow down, make the twist smaller and do fewer reps. Practise Dead Bug to learn to keep your back steady first.

name: Standing Anti-Rotation Hold
desc: Anchor a band at chest height and stand SIDEWAYS to it, both hands holding the band straight out in front of your chest. The band will try to twist you toward the anchor — hold still and resist that pull for 15 seconds, keeping your hips and shoulders square. Release briefly and repeat for 4 rounds, then turn around and do 4 rounds facing the other way.

phases.label: Turn around to face the other way

pairs_with.name: Pallof Press (Band)
pairs_with.reason: Both train anti-rotation

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Balance and core stability together

form_cue: Stand tall with feet about hip width and knees soft, hands in line with the middle of your chest. Nothing should move: hips and shoulders face straight ahead. Keep breathing. You should feel the muscles around your waist.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your lower back or shoulder, if you are holding your breath, or if the band pulls you off balance. Check the anchor is secure first. Effort around the waist is normal.
regression: Use a lighter band or stand closer to the anchor, and keep your elbows bent with your hands near your chest. A shorter hold is fine.
remediation: If you turn toward the anchor, lean away from it or shrug your shoulders, there is too much tension: step closer and bend your elbows. Practise Seated Core Brace to find the bracing feeling first.

name: Hollow Body Hold
desc: Lie on your back and press your lower back FIRMLY into the floor (tuck your tailbone slightly to do it). Keeping that contact, lift your shoulder blades, arms, and legs off the floor — only as high as you can WITHOUT letting your lower back arch up. Hold and breathe normally; if your back lifts off the floor, lower your arms and legs until it presses down again. Hold 20 seconds.
progression: Rock gently back and forth (hollow body rock)

pairs_with.name: Superman Hold
pairs_with.reason: Hollow body and superman train opposite sides of the core

pairs_with.name: Dead Bug
pairs_with.reason: Dead bug builds the control hollow body demands

form_cue: Your lower back stays pressed into the floor from start to finish; that contact is the exercise. Lift only as high as you can keep it, chin gently tucked, and keep breathing. You should feel the front of your belly working hard.
stop_condition: This is a hard exercise. Stop at once if your lower back lifts or hurts, if your neck strains, or if you are holding your breath. Strong effort and shaking in the belly is normal; back or neck pain is not.
regression: Keep your knees bent over your hips and your arms by your sides, or leave your head and shoulders resting on the floor and lift only the legs. A shorter hold is fine.
remediation: The usual fault is the lower back arching up. When that happens, bend your knees, bring arms and legs higher, or lower down and rest. Build a steady Plank Hold before returning to this.

name: Bear Crawl Hold
desc: From hands and knees, lift your knees just 2 inches off the floor. Hold this position for 20 seconds, keeping your back flat.

phases.label: From hands and knees, lift your knees just 2 in...

pairs_with.name: Bird Dog
pairs_with.reason: Both are quadruped core challenges

pairs_with.name: Plank Hold
pairs_with.reason: Different angles of core stability

form_cue: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, toes tucked. Lift your knees only a little and keep your back flat like a table, pushing the floor away. Keep breathing. You should feel your belly, shoulders and thighs working.
stop_condition: This is a hard exercise. Stop if you feel sharp pain in your wrists, shoulders, knees or lower back, or if you are holding your breath. Come down to your knees to rest. Effort and shaking are normal; joint pain is not.
regression: Stay on hands and knees and simply press down through your hands and toes as if about to lift, without your knees leaving the floor. Or lift for a shorter hold.
remediation: If your hips shoot up, your back rounds or sags, or your knees drift high, lower your knees and reset. Make fists or use a folded towel under your hands if your wrists complain, and build Plank Hold first.

name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
desc: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward in a lunge. Push your hips gently forward until you feel a stretch in the front of your back hip. Hold 30 seconds each side.
progression: Add a same-side arm reach overhead
Add a gentle twist toward the front leg
Elevate the back foot on a chair for a deeper stretch

pairs_with.name: Glute Bridge
pairs_with.reason: Stretch the hip flexors, activate the glutes

pairs_with.name: Standing Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both stretch the front of the hip/thigh

form_cue: Stay tall, tuck your tailbone under slightly and squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg, then ease the hips forward. You should feel the stretch in the front of the back hip and upper thigh, not a pinch in the low back.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp pain in the kneeling knee, pinching in the front of the hip or low-back pain. A steady pull in the front of the hip is normal; pain or numbness is not. Keep a chair beside you if you feel unsteady.
regression: Put a folded towel or cushion under the knee, hold a chair for balance and push the hips forward only a little. If kneeling is not comfortable, try it standing in a short split stance with the back heel lifted.
remediation: If your low back arches as you push forward, you have gone past the hip. Come back, tuck the tailbone and squeeze the glute first, then move forward a smaller distance.

name: Figure Four Stretch
desc: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Pull the bottom thigh toward your chest. Hold 30 seconds each side.
progression: Gentle pull, stop at first stretch
Hold 30 seconds, pull a bit closer
Deepen only by drawing the bottom thigh closer to your chest — let the crossed knee relax open, don't push it
Progress to pigeon stretch on the floor

pairs_with.name: Pigeon Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Figure four is the beginner version of pigeon

pairs_with.name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both decompress the hip while lying down

form_cue: The stretch comes from pulling the BOTTOM thigh toward your chest — that's what opens the crossed hip/glute. Keep head, shoulders and low back relaxed on the floor and your hips square (don't let the pelvis twist toward the crossed side). Let the crossed knee fall open on its own — do NOT push it away to force more; that just torques the knee without deepening the hip stretch.
stop_condition: Stop with any KNEE pain in the crossed leg (this belongs in the hip, never the knee), sharp groin pain, or low-back strain. Extra caution if you've ever had knee problems or knee surgery: the crossed knee is on a long lever, so pushing it open loads the joint hard — let it relax open and back off at the first knee sensation. IMPORTANT: after a hip replacement this crossed-leg position can violate hip precautions — skip it unless a surgeon or PT has cleared this range.
regression: Don't cross fully — rest the ankle lower on the shin, or skip the cross and just hug one knee toward the chest. Pull the bottom thigh in less far.
remediation: If crossing pinches in the front of the hip, stay with a simple single-knee-to-chest hug and don't force the cross.

name: Seated Figure Four
desc: Sit tall, cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Gently lean forward keeping your back straight until you feel a stretch in the crossed hip. 20 seconds each side.
progression: Deepen only by hinging further from the hips, knee relaxed — don't press or shift the knee down
Progress to floor figure four for deeper stretch

pairs_with.name: Seated Twist
pairs_with.reason: Both are seated mobility exercises for desk breaks

pairs_with.name: Figure Four Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Seated version is quicker, floor version is deeper

form_cue: Cross the ankle over the opposite knee and hinge forward from the HIPS with a flat back — the stretch belongs in the outer hip/glute of the crossed leg, not the knee or low back. Keep your weight even on both sit bones (don't collapse or shift toward the stretching side). Keep the crossed knee relaxed and let it hang where it wants — do NOT chase depth by driving the knee toward the floor. Forcing the knee down doesn't deepen the hip stretch; it just torques the knee.
stop_condition: Stop with any KNEE pain (this should be felt in the hip, never the knee), sharp groin pain, or low-back pain from rounding. Extra caution if you've ever had knee problems or knee surgery: the crossed knee sits on a long lever, so shifting weight or forcing it down loads the joint hard — keep the knee relaxed and back off at the first knee sensation. IMPORTANT: after a hip replacement this crossed-leg position can violate hip precautions — skip it unless a surgeon or PT has cleared this range.
regression: Don't cross fully — rest the ankle lower on the shin, or hold the shin and hug the knee gently toward the opposite shoulder for a milder version. Hinge less far.
remediation: If crossing the leg is limited or pinches in the front of the hip, stay with the gentler knee-hug version and don't force the cross.
