name: Hip CARs
desc: Stand on one leg (hold something for balance). Lift your knee, rotate it out to the side, then extend it behind you in a big circle. 3 circles each direction, each leg.
progression: Add a pause at tight spots

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: CARs require and build single-leg balance

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: CARs explore full hip range including flexor length

form_cue: Keep the standing leg, pelvis and trunk still while only the lifted hip moves: knee up, out to the side, then round behind you. Go slowly and make the circle as big as you can without your body leaning or twisting.
stop_condition: Keep a firm hold on a counter or sturdy chair throughout. Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the hip or groin, low-back pain or unsteadiness. If you have had a hip replacement, check with your surgeon or PT before doing this.
regression: Make the circle much smaller and keep both hands on the support. You can also do the same circle lying on your side so balance is not a factor.
remediation: If your trunk leans or your pelvis twists to get the leg round, the circle is too big. Shrink it until the body stays still, and loosen the hip first with Figure Four Stretch.

name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
desc: Sit with one leg bent 90 degrees in front and the other bent 90 degrees behind. Lean forward over the front leg. Hold 30 seconds, switch sides.
progression: Lean forward over front shin, hold 30 seconds
Switch to leaning over the back leg
Transition between front and back leans smoothly

pairs_with.name: Pigeon Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both open the hip in external rotation

pairs_with.name: Hip CARs
pairs_with.reason: 90/90 builds the range that CARs explore

form_cue: Sit tall with both sit bones as grounded as you can, then hinge forward from the hips over the front shin with a long back. You should feel the stretch in the outer hip and glute of the front leg, not in either knee.
stop_condition: Stop with any knee pain, pinching in the front of the hip or groin, or sharp low-back pain. A strong pull in the outer hip is normal. After a hip replacement, skip this unless your surgeon or PT has cleared it.
regression: Sit on a folded blanket or cushion, rest your hands on the floor beside you and stay upright instead of leaning forward. Let the knee angles be wider than 90 degrees if that eases the knees.
remediation: If you tip onto one hip or round your back to lean forward, sit up taller on a cushion and lean less. If the position itself is out of reach, practise Figure Four Stretch first.

name: Standing Hip Circle
desc: Stand on one leg and swing the other in a circle from the hip, 10 circles each direction, then switch legs. Hold something for balance.

pairs_with.name: Hip CARs
pairs_with.reason: Hip circles are the warm-up, CARs are the progression

pairs_with.name: Leg Swing (Front-Back)
pairs_with.reason: Both are standing dynamic hip mobility

form_cue: Stand tall on the supporting leg and let the other leg circle from the hip socket, keeping the trunk upright and the pelvis fairly level. Keep the circles smooth and only as big as you can control.
stop_condition: Keep one hand on a wall, counter or sturdy chair the whole time. Stop if you feel unsteady or dizzy, or get pinching or sharp pain in the hip, groin or low back. A light warming feeling around the hip is normal.
regression: Make the circles small and slow, keep the toes close to the floor and hold the support with both hands. Do fewer circles if the standing leg tires.
remediation: If your whole body sways or your trunk leans to throw the leg round, slow down and shrink the circle until only the leg moves. Rest the foot down between circles if you need to reset your balance.

name: Leg Swing (Front-Back)
desc: Hold a wall for balance. Swing one leg forward and backward like a pendulum, 15 swings each leg. Keep your torso upright.
progression: Add a brief hold at end ranges

pairs_with.name: Leg Swing (Side-to-Side)
pairs_with.reason: Front-back and lateral swings together warm up all hip directions

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Dynamic and static hip flexor work

form_cue: Stand tall beside the wall and let the leg swing loosely from the hip, like a pendulum, with the trunk still. The swing should be relaxed and rhythmic, with only a light pull at the front or back of the thigh at each end.
stop_condition: Keep hold of the wall and never force the height of the swing. Stop with sharp or pulling pain in the hamstring, groin or low back, or if you feel unsteady or dizzy. A light stretch at the end of the swing is fine; a sudden tug is not.
regression: Keep the swings small and slow, well short of your end range, and hold a counter or sturdy chair with a firm grip. Do fewer swings if the standing leg tires.
remediation: If your back arches as the leg goes behind or your trunk rocks to gain height, the swing is too big. Tighten your belly gently, shorten the swing and let the range grow on its own.

name: Leg Swing (Side-to-Side)
desc: Face a wall, hold it for balance. Swing one leg side to side across your body, 15 swings each leg. Keep hips facing forward.
progression: Add a pause at end range

pairs_with.name: Leg Swing (Front-Back)
pairs_with.reason: Lateral and sagittal swings for complete hip warm-up

pairs_with.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Dynamic and static inner thigh work

form_cue: Face the wall with both hands on it and keep your hips and chest square to it while the leg swings across in front of the standing leg and back out to the side. Keep it loose and controlled, with a light pull in the inner or outer thigh.
stop_condition: Keep both hands on the wall and never force the swing. Stop with sharp or pulling pain in the groin, outer hip or low back, twinges in the standing knee, or any unsteadiness or dizziness. A light stretch at each end is normal.
regression: Use small, slow swings that stay well inside your comfortable range, and stand a little further from the wall so the leg has room. Do fewer swings if the standing leg tires.
remediation: If your hips turn or your trunk tips side to side with each swing, the swing is too big or too fast. Slow down and shrink it until the pelvis stays facing the wall.

name: Standing Adductor Stretch
desc: Take a wide stance, shift your weight to one side and bend that knee while keeping the other leg straight. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Add a gentle bounce at end range

pairs_with.name: Leg Swing (Side-to-Side)
pairs_with.reason: Dynamic and static inner thigh work

pairs_with.name: Sumo Squat
pairs_with.reason: Both work inner thigh flexibility and strength

form_cue: Keep both feet flat and pointing forward, sit the hips back a little as you bend one knee, and keep that knee in line with its toes. The stretch belongs along the inner thigh of the straight leg.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pulling pain in the groin, pain in the bent knee, or if your feet start to slide. A steady pull along the inner thigh is normal. Hold the stretch still without bouncing, and do it on a non-slip floor.
regression: Narrow your stance, bend the knee only a little and rest your hands on a counter or the back of a sturdy chair in front of you. Use a shorter hold.
remediation: If the bent knee drops inward or your chest folds forward, the stance is too wide. Bring the feet in, keep the knee over the toes and shift across only until you first feel the inner thigh.

name: Pigeon Stretch
desc: From hands and knees, bring one knee forward and lay the shin across in front of you. Extend the other leg behind. Fold forward and hold 45 seconds each side.
progression: Hold for 90 seconds per side with deep breathing

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Pigeon opens the back, hip flexor stretch opens the front

pairs_with.name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both are deep external rotation stretches

form_cue: The stretch is deep in the glute/outer hip of the FRONT leg. Keep your hips square to the floor (don't let the back hip roll open), and keep the front shin at a comfortable angle — the closer it is to parallel with the front of the mat, the more intense, so build up gradually. Fold forward from the hips over the front leg with a flat back, only as far as the hip allows.
stop_condition: Felt in the outer hip/glute, NOT the knee. Stop with any pain on the inside or front of the FRONT knee (common here — draw the shin back toward you and reduce the angle), sharp groin pain, or low-back strain from rounding. Extra caution with any knee history: the bent front knee is vulnerable in this position. After a hip replacement, deep flexion + external rotation can violate precautions — skip unless a surgeon or PT has cleared it.
regression: Do the figure-four version lying on your back instead — same muscles, far gentler on the knee. Or stay tall and skip the forward fold, and keep the front shin closer to your body rather than parallel to the mat.
remediation: If the front knee complains or the hip pinches, switch to the supine figure-four — it targets the same glute without loading the knee.

name: Deep Squat Hold
desc: Lower into a deep squat with feet shoulder-width apart, heels on the ground. Hold for 30 seconds. Hold onto something for balance if needed.

phases.label: Lower into a deep squat with feet shoulder-widt...

progression: Hold a doorframe for support, 20 seconds
Add gentle shifting side to side in the bottom

pairs_with.name: Ankle Circles
pairs_with.reason: Ankle mobility supports the deep squat position

pairs_with.name: Hip CARs
pairs_with.reason: CARs warm up the range the deep squat demands

form_cue: Keep your heels down, knees tracking over your toes and chest lifted as you sink between your hips. You should feel a stretch through the hips, groin and ankles, with weight spread across the whole foot.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp knee pain, pinching in the front of the hip or groin, or low-back pain, and come up slowly in case you feel lightheaded. If you have had a knee or hip replacement, check with your surgeon or PT before squatting this deep.
regression: Hold a doorframe or sturdy counter and go only as low as you can with heels down and no pain, or sit back onto a low stool. A rolled towel under the heels can help, and a shorter hold is fine.
remediation: If your heels lift or your knees cave in, you are lower than your ankles and hips allow yet. Hold a support, stay higher and widen your feet a little, and practise Standing Adductor Stretch first.

name: Frog Stretch
desc: From hands and knees, spread your knees wide and lower your hips toward the floor between them. Keep feet turned out. Hold 45 seconds.

phases.label: From hands and knees, spread your knees wide an...

progression: Keep hips high, light stretch on inner thighs
Add gentle rocking forward and back

pairs_with.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Standing version is easier, frog is deeper

pairs_with.name: Deep Squat Hold
pairs_with.reason: Both require and build significant hip mobility

form_cue: Keep knees in line with hips, shins and feet turned out, and your back flat as you ease the hips down and slightly back. Support your weight on your hands or forearms. The stretch belongs in the inner thighs and groin.
stop_condition: This is a strong stretch, so go slowly and never force or bounce. Stop with sharp groin pain, pinching in the hip, knee pain or low-back pain. After a hip replacement or groin injury, skip this unless a clinician has cleared it.
regression: Kneel on a folded blanket, bring the knees closer together and keep the hips high so the stretch is light. Use a shorter hold and come out by walking the knees in slowly.
remediation: If your low back sags or you feel it in the knees instead of the inner thighs, narrow the knees and lift the hips higher. If that still does not work, build the range with 90/90 Hip Stretch first.

name: Glute Bridge
desc: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Lift your hips toward the ceiling, squeeze glutes at the top. Hold 5 seconds at top. 12 reps.
progression: Hold at top for 5 seconds, 12 reps
Add a resistance band above knees

pairs_with.name: Clamshell
pairs_with.reason: Bridge works glute max, clamshell works glute med

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Stretch the front, strengthen the back

form_cue: Press through your heels and lift until shoulders, hips and knees make a straight line, no higher. Ribs stay down and knees stay hip-width apart. You should feel the work in your glutes more than in your low back.
stop_condition: Stop with low-back pain, sharp knee pain, or a hamstring cramp that does not ease when you lower. Muscle effort in the glutes and backs of the thighs is normal. Keep breathing through the hold.
regression: Lift only a few inches and lower straight away without the hold, or do fewer reps. Resting between reps is fine.
remediation: If your hamstrings cramp, bring your heels a little closer to your hips. If you feel it in your low back, tuck your tailbone slightly before lifting and stop the lift lower.

name: Clamshell
desc: Lie on your side with knees bent and stacked. Keep feet together and open the top knee like a clamshell. 15 reps each side.
progression: Add a resistance band above knees
Hold the open position for 3 seconds
Progress to standing clamshell with band

pairs_with.name: Glute Bridge
pairs_with.reason: Clamshell hits glute med, bridge hits glute max

pairs_with.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
pairs_with.reason: Both are side-lying glute exercises

form_cue: Keep hips stacked one above the other and your feet touching while the top knee opens. The movement is small and slow, and you should feel it in the side and back of the top hip.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching in the front of the hip or groin, sharp pain in the outer hip you are lying on, or low-back pain. A tired, warm feeling in the side of the hip is normal effort.
regression: Open the knee only part way, do fewer reps and rest your head on a pillow. Lying with your back against a wall helps you stay stacked with less effort.
remediation: If the top hip rolls backward as the knee opens, you are borrowing range from your back. Put your top hand on that hip to keep it still and open only as far as the pelvis stays put.

name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
desc: Lie on your side with legs straight. Lift the top leg about 12 inches, hold 2 seconds, lower slowly. 12 reps each side.
progression: Add a resistance band around ankles
Hold at the top for 5 seconds
Add small pulses at the top

pairs_with.name: Clamshell
pairs_with.reason: Both target glute medius from different angles

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Leg raises build the hip stability single-leg stance needs

form_cue: Keep hips stacked and the top leg straight, in line with your body or slightly behind it, toes pointing forward. Lift with control and lower slowly. You should feel it in the side of the top hip.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the hip or groin, low-back pain, or pain in the hip you are lying on. A working, tired feeling in the side of the hip is normal.
regression: Bend the bottom knee for a steadier base, lift the leg only a few inches without the hold, and do fewer reps.
remediation: If the leg drifts forward or the toes turn up to the ceiling, the front of the hip is taking over. Lie with your back and heel against a wall and slide the heel up it.

name: Standing Glute Squeeze
desc: Stand tall and squeeze your glutes as hard as you can for 5 seconds, then release. Repeat 8 times. Activates dormant glutes from sitting.

phases.label: Stand tall and squeeze your glutes as hard as y...

progression: Squeeze one side at a time

pairs_with.name: Glute Bridge
pairs_with.reason: Squeeze activates, bridge strengthens

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Stretch tight hip flexors, wake up the glutes

form_cue: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft, then tighten both buttocks without tucking your pelvis hard or leaning back. Keep breathing normally. The effort belongs in the glutes, not the low back or thighs.
stop_condition: Stop with low-back pain, a cramp that does not ease, or lightheadedness. Do not hold your breath while you squeeze. A firm working feeling in the buttocks is normal.
regression: Squeeze at about half effort for a shorter time, with a hand on a counter for steadiness, or do it lying on your back with knees bent.
remediation: If your low back arches or your thighs do most of the work, soften the knees, ease the effort and place your hands on your buttocks to feel them tighten.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
desc: Place a resistance band around your ankles. Take 10 side steps to the right, then 10 to the left. Stay low in a quarter squat.

phases.label: Place a resistance band around your ankles

progression: Add a pause and squeeze after each step

pairs_with.name: Clamshell
pairs_with.reason: Clamshell isolates, lateral walk integrates the movement

pairs_with.name: Sumo Squat
pairs_with.reason: Both work the glute medius in a functional pattern

form_cue: Keep toes pointing forward, knees over toes and the band lightly taut the whole time. Step out with the lead foot, then follow with a small step so the feet never touch. You should feel it in the sides of the hips.
stop_condition: Clear the floor and step alongside a counter or wall, because a band at the ankles can trip you. Stop with knee pain, pinching in the hip, low-back pain or unsteadiness. Burning in the sides of the hips is normal effort.
regression: Move the band above your knees or do the steps with no band, stand taller and take smaller steps alongside a counter. Fewer steps each way is fine.
remediation: If your knees cave in, your feet drag or your trunk rocks side to side, the band is too strong or the steps too big. Go lighter and smaller, and build hip strength with Clamshell first.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
desc: Lie on your back, extend one leg. Drive through the grounded foot to lift your hips. Hold 3 seconds at top. 8 reps each side.
progression: Foot close to hips, 6 reps each side
Extend the free leg straight up
Add a resistance band above knees

pairs_with.name: Glute Bridge
pairs_with.reason: Bilateral builds base, unilateral builds balance

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Both challenge unilateral stability

form_cue: Keep your hips level as you lift, pressing through the heel of the grounded foot, and stop when shoulder, hip and knee are in line. You should feel it in the glute of the working leg, not the low back.
stop_condition: Stop with low-back pain, sharp knee pain or a hamstring cramp that does not ease when you lower. Lower under control rather than dropping. Strong effort in the glute and back of the thigh is normal.
regression: Keep both feet down and lift with most of your weight on one leg, or lift lower without the hold. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your hips tilt or drop to one side, or the hamstring cramps, bring the working foot closer to your hips and lift less high. If it still breaks down, go back to Glute Bridge.

name: Donkey Kick
desc: On hands and knees, drive one bent knee up toward the ceiling, squeezing the glute at top. 12 reps each side.
progression: Add a resistance band around thighs
Extend the leg straight at the top

pairs_with.name: Fire Hydrant
pairs_with.reason: Both are quadruped glute exercises targeting different angles

pairs_with.name: Bird Dog
pairs_with.reason: Similar position, different focus

form_cue: Keep the knee bent and press the sole of the foot toward the ceiling until the thigh is about level with your body, no higher. Your back stays flat and hips square to the floor. You should feel it in the glute of the lifting leg.
stop_condition: Stop with low-back pain, wrist pain, sharp pain in the knee you are kneeling on, or pinching in the hip. Glute effort is normal. Use a mat or folded towel under your knees.
regression: Lift the leg lower and do fewer reps, or rest on your forearms if your wrists complain. You can also do it standing, leaning on a counter and pressing one heel back.
remediation: If your low back arches or your hips twist open as the leg rises, you are lifting too high. Tighten your belly gently and stop the lift where the back stays flat.

name: Fire Hydrant
desc: On hands and knees, lift one bent knee out to the side, keeping it at 90 degrees. 12 reps each side.
progression: Add small circles at the top
Add a resistance band above knees

pairs_with.name: Donkey Kick
pairs_with.reason: Fire hydrant and donkey kick hit different glute angles

pairs_with.name: Clamshell
pairs_with.reason: Both target glute medius/external rotation

form_cue: Keep your arms straight, back flat and weight even on both hands while the bent knee lifts out to the side. Only the hip moves. Lift as high as you can without the pelvis tipping, and feel it in the outer hip and glute.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching in the hip or groin, low-back pain, wrist pain or sharp pain in the supporting knee. A working feeling in the outer hip is normal. Pad your knees with a mat or folded towel.
regression: Lift the knee only a few inches and do fewer reps, or rest on your forearms to spare the wrists. You can also do the same knee-opening movement lying on your side.
remediation: If you lean away or your trunk rotates to get the knee higher, the lift is too high. Keep your weight centred and stop the knee where both hips still face the floor.

name: Pistol Squat Progression
desc: Hold a doorframe, lower into a single-leg squat on one leg with the other extended forward. Go as low as you can. 5 reps each leg.
progression: Sit to a high chair on one leg
Sit to a low chair on one leg
Hold a doorframe for balance, go deeper

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Balance foundation for pistol squats

pairs_with.name: Deep Squat Hold
pairs_with.reason: Bilateral deep squat prepares for unilateral

form_cue: Keep the standing heel down and the knee tracking over the toes as you sit back and down under control, holding the doorframe. Go only as low as you can stand back up from smoothly. Feel it in the thigh and glute of the standing leg.
stop_condition: Keep a firm grip on a solid doorframe and never drop into the bottom. Stop with any knee pain, pinching in the hip, low-back pain or loss of balance. If you have knee problems or a joint replacement, check with a clinician first.
regression: Sit down to a high, sturdy chair on one leg and stand up using both legs, keeping hold of a support. Use a smaller depth and fewer reps.
remediation: If the knee caves inward, the heel lifts or you fall into the bottom, the depth is too much for now. Stay higher and use a chair as a target, and build strength with Single-Leg Glute Bridge first.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
desc: Stand on one leg, pull the other foot toward your glute. Use a wall for balance. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Hold 30 seconds with no balance support

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Both stretch the front of the thigh/hip

pairs_with.name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Front and back of thigh for balance

form_cue: Stand tall with one hand on the wall, knees side by side, and draw the heel toward your glute without arching your low back. You should feel the stretch down the front of the thigh, not in the knee.
stop_condition: A firm pull in the front of the thigh is normal. Stop with sharp or pinching knee pain, a cramp in the back of the thigh, low-back pain, or if you feel unsteady. Keep the wall or a sturdy chair within reach the whole time.
regression: Hold your ankle or trouser leg with a smaller knee bend, or loop a towel around the ankle so you do not have to reach as far. A shorter hold is fine.
remediation: If your back arches or the knee drifts out to the side, ease the pull, gently tuck your tailbone and bring the knees level. If balance is the problem, try Lying Quad Stretch instead.

name: Couch Stretch
desc: Kneel with your back shin flat up against a wall (toes pointing up), and step your other foot forward into a lunge. Keeping your torso tall, gently ease your hips forward and down until you feel a strong stretch in the front of the back thigh and hip. Ease off if it turns sharp, then switch sides. 30 seconds each side.
progression: Lean back slightly for more stretch
Rise up to full-kneeling against the wall

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Couch stretch is the deeper version

pairs_with.name: Standing Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Standing version is the warm-up, couch is the deep stretch

form_cue: Keep your torso tall, ribs down and tailbone gently tucked as you ease the hips forward. The stretch belongs in the front of the back thigh and hip, not in the low back or the kneecap.
stop_condition: A strong stretch is expected. Stop with sharp or pinching pain in the back knee, pain on the kneecap from the floor, low-back pinching, or numbness or tingling in the leg. Come out slowly, using your hands.
regression: Pad the knee with a folded towel and move it further from the wall so the knee bends less, or keep your hands on the floor or a chair and stay leaning forward.
remediation: If your low back arches or you cannot get upright, you are too close to the wall. Move the knee away, tuck the tailbone first, then ease forward. Standing Quad Stretch is a good place to practise first.

name: Lying Quad Stretch
desc: Lie on your side, grab your top foot and pull your heel toward your glute. Keep knees together. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Push hip forward to add hip flexor stretch

pairs_with.name: Standing Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Same stretch, different position for stability

pairs_with.name: Lying Hamstring Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Front and back of thigh in a lying position

form_cue: Lie on your side with knees together and hips stacked, then draw the top heel toward your glute. Keep your low back from arching; the stretch should be in the front of the top thigh.
stop_condition: A steady pull in the front of the thigh is normal. Stop with sharp or pinching knee pain, a cramp in the back of the thigh, or low-back pain.
regression: Use a towel or strap looped around the ankle so you do not have to reach back as far, and pull less. A shorter hold is fine.
remediation: If your back arches or the top knee lifts and drifts forward, ease the pull and bend the bottom knee up in front of you to steady the pelvis before trying again.

name: Wall Sit
desc: Lean against a wall and slide down until your thighs are parallel to the floor, knees at 90 degrees. Hold as long as you can up to 45 seconds.

phases.label: Lean against a wall and slide down until your t...

progression: Slide down only partway, hold 20 seconds
Add a ball squeeze between knees

pairs_with.name: Standing Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen then stretch the quads

pairs_with.name: Sumo Squat
pairs_with.reason: Both build lower body strength in different patterns

form_cue: Keep your whole back flat on the wall, feet far enough out that your knees stay over your ankles, and weight through your heels. You should feel the effort in the thighs. Keep breathing.
stop_condition: Burning, tired thighs are normal. Stop with sharp pain in or behind the kneecap, back pain, dizziness, or if your legs shake so much you might slide. Stop before your legs give out, and never hold your breath.
regression: Slide down only partway, well above a 90-degree bend, and hold for a shorter time. Place a chair beside you so you have something to push up from.
remediation: If your knees move past your toes or fall inward, walk your feet further from the wall and press the knees gently out in line with the toes. If your back lifts off the wall, come up higher.

name: Step-Up
desc: Step up onto a sturdy step or low chair with one foot, straighten the leg, then step down slowly. 10 reps each leg.
progression: Hold at the top for 3 seconds each rep

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Both challenge single-leg stability

pairs_with.name: Standing Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Stretch after strengthening

form_cue: Put the whole foot on the step, lean slightly forward, and push through that heel to stand up straight. Keep the knee in line with your toes and lower yourself down slowly instead of dropping.
stop_condition: Working thighs are normal. Stop with sharp or pinching knee pain, a knee that buckles or gives way, dizziness, or unsteadiness. Use a step that cannot slide or tip, and keep a rail, wall or counter within reach.
regression: Use the lowest step you have, such as the bottom stair with a hand on the rail, and do fewer reps. Tap the other foot on the step at the top for balance.
remediation: If you push off the bottom foot or the knee caves inward, the step is too high. Lower it, hold a support, and slow the step-down. Wall Sit can be used to build thigh strength first.

name: Sumo Squat
desc: Stand with feet wider than shoulders, toes turned out. Squat down keeping knees tracking over toes. 12 reps.

phases.label: Stand with feet wider than shoulders, toes turn...

progression: Add a 3-second hold at the bottom
Add a calf raise at the top

pairs_with.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both work inner thigh flexibility

pairs_with.name: Wall Sit
pairs_with.reason: Both build quad and hip strength

form_cue: Feet wider than shoulders with toes turned out, and knees pointing the same way as your toes all the way down. Sit the hips back and down with your chest up. Feel it in the thighs, inner thighs and glutes.
stop_condition: Muscle effort in the thighs is normal. Stop with sharp knee pain, pinching in the hip or groin, low-back pain, dizziness, or unsteadiness.
regression: Do a quarter squat only, with a hand on a counter or chair back, and narrow your stance or turn the toes out less. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your knees fall inward, turn the toes out a little less and gently press the knees out over them. If your heels lift or your chest drops, shorten the depth until you can hold the position.

name: Seated Knee Extension
desc: Sit tall, straighten one leg until it's parallel to the floor. Hold 5 seconds, lower slowly. 10 reps each leg. Builds quad strength gently.

pairs_with.name: Seated Marching
pairs_with.reason: Both are seated lower body exercises

pairs_with.name: Wall Sit
pairs_with.reason: Seated extension builds toward more loaded positions

form_cue: Straighten the knee to about parallel with the floor, squeezing the thigh at the top — slow up, slow down, thigh staying on the seat.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp knee pain (a mild working effort in the thigh is fine). Ease off if the knee clicks painfully.
regression: Straighten only partway, or do fewer reps; a partial extension still works the quad.
remediation: If the knee aches at full lock, stop just short of straight and hold there.

name: Bodyweight Squat
desc: Stand with feet shoulder width apart. Lower into a squat as if sitting into a chair, then stand up. 12 reps. Keep chest up and knees over toes.

phases.label: Stand with feet shoulder width apart

progression: Slow to 3 seconds down, 3 seconds up
Add a pause at the bottom

pairs_with.name: Standing Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen then stretch

pairs_with.name: Deep Squat Hold
pairs_with.reason: Bodyweight squat builds strength, deep squat builds mobility

form_cue: Send your hips back first as if sitting into a chair, keep your chest up, heels down and knees in line with your toes. You should feel the work in your thighs and glutes, not in the knees or low back.
stop_condition: Muscle effort in the thighs is normal. Stop with sharp or pinching knee pain, pinching in the front of the hip, low-back pain, dizziness, or unsteadiness.
regression: Squat down to a sturdy chair, touch the seat lightly and stand back up, holding a counter or chair back if you need it. A quarter squat with fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your knees cave in, heels lift or back rounds, shorten the depth and slow down. Practise sitting down to a chair and standing up until the hips-back pattern feels steady.

name: Split Squat
desc: Stand in a stagger stance, one foot forward. Lower your back knee toward the floor, then push up. 10 reps each side.
progression: Full range, knee near the floor, 10 reps
Add a 2-second pause at the bottom
Elevate the back foot on a step (Bulgarian split squat)

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Same position for strength and flexibility

pairs_with.name: Step-Up
pairs_with.reason: Both are unilateral lower body strengtheners

form_cue: Feet stay hip-width apart side to side, like standing on train tracks. Lower straight down with your torso upright and front heel flat. Feel it in the front thigh and glute, with the front knee in line with the toes.
stop_condition: Working thighs are normal. Stop with sharp or pinching pain in either knee, a knee that buckles, dizziness, or unsteadiness. Keep a wall, counter or sturdy chair within reach.
regression: Hold a chair or counter and lower only partway, doing fewer reps. Put a cushion under the back knee so there is no worry about touching down.
remediation: If you wobble or the front knee caves in, widen your stance side to side, hold a support and shorten the range. If it still feels unsteady, go back to Bodyweight Squat first.

name: Terminal Knee Extension
desc: Anchor a band behind your knee. Stand facing away, bend knee slightly, then straighten it against the band resistance. 12 reps each leg.
progression: Add a 3-second hold at full extension

pairs_with.name: Wall Sit
pairs_with.reason: Both strengthen the quad's role in knee stability

pairs_with.name: Standing Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen then stretch around the knee

form_cue: With the band behind the knee, keep your heel down and hips level, then straighten the knee by tightening the front of the thigh. Finish straight but not snapped back. Feel it just above the kneecap.
stop_condition: Effort in the thigh is normal. Stop with sharp knee pain, pain behind the knee where the band presses, or unsteadiness. Check the band and its anchor are secure before each set, and keep a wall or chair within reach.
regression: Use the lightest band or stand closer to the anchor so there is less pull, and hold a chair for balance. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your hips swing or you lock the knee hard to finish, the band is too strong. Lighten it and straighten slowly. You can practise the thigh squeeze first with Seated Knee Extension.

name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
desc: Place one heel on a low step or the floor in front of you. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until you feel a stretch behind the thigh. 20 seconds each side.
progression: Place foot higher for more range

pairs_with.name: Standing Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Front and back of thigh for balance

pairs_with.name: Standing Forward Fold
pairs_with.reason: Both stretch the posterior chain

form_cue: Front leg nearly straight with the heel down, hips square, and tip forward from the hips with a long flat back. You should feel the stretch behind the thigh, not in your low back.
stop_condition: A firm pull behind the thigh is normal. Stop with sharp pain behind the knee, low-back pain, numbness or tingling down the leg, or unsteadiness. Have a wall or chair within reach.
regression: Keep the heel on the floor instead of a step, bend the front knee a little, and hinge only slightly. Rest a hand on a chair or counter.
remediation: If your back rounds to reach further, you have gone past your range. Come up, put your hands on your hips, lengthen your spine and tip forward only as far as your back stays flat.

name: Standing Forward Fold
desc: Stand with feet hip width. Hinge at the hips and let your upper body hang toward the floor. Bend knees slightly if needed. Hold 20 seconds.
progression: Grab opposite elbows and sway gently

pairs_with.name: Standing Back Extension
pairs_with.reason: Forward fold and extension balance each other

pairs_with.name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both stretch the posterior chain

form_cue: Fold from the hips, not the waist, with knees soft, and let your head, neck and arms hang heavy. Feel the stretch along the backs of the thighs. Roll or hinge up slowly when you finish.
stop_condition: A pull behind the thighs is normal. Stop with dizziness, pressure in the head or eyes, sharp low-back pain, or tingling down a leg. Come up slowly, and skip this if hanging head-down makes you lightheaded.
regression: Bend your knees generously and rest your hands on your thighs, a chair seat or a counter so you fold only partway. A shorter hold is fine.
remediation: If your low back takes the strain or you cannot relax, bend the knees more and support your hands. Standing Hamstring Stretch gives a similar stretch one leg at a time with your head up.

name: Lying Hamstring Stretch
desc: Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot flat on the floor. Loop a towel or strap around the other foot, then gently draw that leg up toward you and straighten the knee until you feel a comfortable stretch up the back of the thigh. Hold, then switch legs. Hold 30 seconds each side.
progression: Straighten the leg more, hold 30 seconds
Pull the leg closer, keep it straight
Add ankle circles while holding the stretch

pairs_with.name: Lying Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Front and back of thigh in a lying position

pairs_with.name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both are supine lower body stretches

form_cue: Keep your head, shoulders and both hips resting on the floor and let the towel do the work. Straighten the lifted knee only as far as is comfortable; the stretch should sit in the back of the thigh.
stop_condition: A comfortable pull up the back of the thigh is normal. Stop with sharp pain behind the knee, low-back pain, or numbness or tingling down the leg or into the foot.
regression: Keep the lifted knee slightly bent and the leg lower. If your arms tire or shoulders tense, use a longer strap or belt. A shorter hold is fine.
remediation: If your hips lift, your back flattens hard into the floor or your shoulders strain, you are pulling too far. Lower the leg, soften the knee and relax your grip before easing back in.

name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
desc: Sit on the edge of your chair, extend one leg straight with heel on the floor. Hinge forward at the hips keeping back flat. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Deeper hinge with flat back, 20 seconds

pairs_with.name: Seated Figure Four
pairs_with.reason: Both are desk-friendly lower body stretches

pairs_with.name: Seated Knee Extension
pairs_with.reason: Stretch and strengthen at the desk

form_cue: Hinge forward from the HIPS with a long, flat back — lead with the chest, don't round the spine. Feel it in the back of the thigh, not the low back. Knee soft, not locked.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel it in your low back (you're rounding — reset the flat back) or any sharp pain or nerve-like tingling down the leg. Gentle thigh tension only.
regression: Keep a bigger knee bend, hinge less far, or rest the leg on a low stool instead of straightening fully. Less range, same flat-back form.
remediation: If tight hamstrings pull you into rounding, reduce range until you can keep a flat back — protecting the low back matters more than reach. Practice the hip hinge (sit tall, tip the pelvis forward slightly) to build the pattern.

name: Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight)
desc: Stand on one leg, hinge at the hip and reach hands toward the floor while the free leg extends behind you. 8 reps each leg.
progression: Partial hinge with fingertip touch on wall
Full hinge, hands reach toward floor
Slow to 3 seconds down, 3 seconds up
Hold a light weight for added challenge

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Both challenge single-leg balance

pairs_with.name: Glute Bridge
pairs_with.reason: Both strengthen the posterior chain

form_cue: Soften the standing knee, then tip forward from the hip so your chest goes down as the free leg goes back, keeping the back flat and hips level. Feel it in the hamstring and glute of the standing leg.
stop_condition: A stretch and effort behind the standing thigh is normal. Stop with low-back pain, sharp pain behind the knee, dizziness, or loss of balance. This is single-leg work: stay within reach of a wall or sturdy chair.
regression: Keep fingertips on a wall or chair and hinge only partway, or keep the back toes resting lightly on the floor as a kickstand. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your back rounds, your hip opens out to the side or you wobble, shorten the hinge and use the support. Practise the flat-back hip hinge with Standing Hamstring Stretch first.

name: Good Morning Stretch
desc: Stand with hands behind your head, feet hip width. Hinge at the hips pushing your butt back until you feel a hamstring stretch. Return upright. 10 reps.

phases.label: Stand with hands behind your head, feet hip width

progression: Add a 3-second hold at the bottom

pairs_with.name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Dynamic and static hamstring work

pairs_with.name: Standing Back Extension
pairs_with.reason: Good mornings and extensions are complementary hinge patterns

form_cue: Soften your knees and push your hips straight back, keeping your back flat and elbows wide. Do not pull on your head. Feel the stretch in the backs of the thighs, then squeeze your glutes to stand tall.
stop_condition: A stretch behind the thighs is normal. Stop with low-back pain, neck strain, dizziness, or tingling down a leg. Rise at a steady pace, not quickly.
regression: Cross your arms over your chest or put your hands on your hips instead of behind your head, and hinge only a little. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your back rounds or your knees bend into a squat, the hinge is too deep. Stand a short step in front of a wall and reach your hips back to touch it, keeping the back flat.

name: Hamstring Walkout
desc: Start in a glute bridge — on your back, knees bent, feet flat, hips lifted. KEEPING YOUR HIPS OFF THE FLOOR the whole time, take small steps to walk your feet away from you. As your legs straighten, your body lowers into a long line from shoulders to heels (hips stay up, just lower) and your hamstrings work to hold you there. Then walk your feet back in to the tall bridge. The farther out your feet go, the harder the hamstrings work. 6 reps.

phases.label: Bridge up, then walk feet out and back — hips stay off the floor

progression: Slow the walkout to 5 seconds out, 5 seconds back

pairs_with.name: Glute Bridge
pairs_with.reason: Bridge builds the base, walkout adds challenge

pairs_with.name: Lying Hamstring Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen then stretch the hamstrings

form_cue: Drive the hold from your HAMSTRINGS and glutes, not your low back. Keep your ribs down and core gently braced so the lower back doesn't arch as the legs straighten. Only walk out as far as you can keep your hips lifted — if the hips start sagging to the floor, that's your range for today.
stop_condition: Stop with any low-back pinching or pain (this belongs in the backs of the thighs and glutes, not the back), or hamstring cramping. Come down if your hips can't stay off the floor. If you feel it in the lower back instead of the hamstrings, shorten the range.
regression: Walk out only halfway with the knees more bent, or hold a plain glute bridge first. Shorten the distance your feet travel.
remediation: If the hamstrings cramp or tire fast, build the base with glute bridges and short walkouts before extending the range — cramping usually means going too far too soon.

name: Nordic Curl Eccentric
desc: Kneel tall with your ankles anchored (under a loaded barbell or heavy couch, or held by a partner) and something padded under your knees. Keeping your body in ONE straight line from knees to head — hips open, no bending at the waist — slowly lower your whole body toward the floor, resisting the fall with your hamstrings for as long as you can. When you can't hold any longer, catch yourself with your hands (into a push-up position) and push back up to kneeling. The slow lowering IS the exercise. 5 reps.

phases.label: Lower your straight body slowly, catch with hands, push back up

progression: Lean forward just a few inches, push back up with hands
Lean further forward with slow control
Lower to the ground over 5 seconds, push up with hands

pairs_with.reason: Both are advanced hamstring strengtheners

pairs_with.name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Stretch after intense strengthening

form_cue: Keep a rigid straight line from knees to head the ENTIRE time — hips stay open, no hinging at the waist (bending at the hips takes the hamstrings out of it and defeats the move). Go slow and stay in control; the instant you lose it, catch with your hands. Keep your hands ready in front of you the whole way down.
stop_condition: This is an advanced, very demanding exercise. Stop with any sharp hamstring pain or a pulling sensation (hamstring strain is a real risk here), knee pain from the kneeling load, or low-back pain from letting the hips pike. If you can only control the first few inches, that IS your range — do NOT free-fall the rest. Expect significant muscle soreness for a few days, especially the first time; that soreness is normal, sharp pain during the move is not.
regression: Only lower a few inches and push straight back up with your hands, 2-3 reps. Better yet, build the base first with the easier eccentric hamstring moves (Hamstring Walkout, bodyweight Romanian deadlift) — this needs that foundation.
remediation: If your hamstrings can't control even a small range, you're not ready for Nordics yet — spend several weeks on hamstring walkouts and glute bridges first. Any cramp or 'pull' means stop immediately.

name: Sciatic Nerve Floss
desc: A gentle nerve GLIDE for the sciatic nerve — not a stretch. Sit tall with both feet on the floor. Straighten one leg out in front of you while you look UP toward the ceiling; then bend that knee back down while you tuck your chin to your chest. The leg and head move together in opposition, smooth and rhythmic — you're sliding the nerve back and forth, not stretching it. Keep the tension light and never hold it at the end. Alternate smoothly 10 times each leg.
progression: Add ankle dorsiflexion for more nerve tension

form_cue: This is a nerve GLIDE, not a stretch: as the knee straightens look UP, as it bends tuck the chin — the two ends move in opposition, smooth and rhythmic. You should feel gentle tension that comes and goes, never a hard stretch you hold.
stop_condition: Nerve tissue must not be forced. Stop with any sharp, shooting, or burning pain or increasing numbness/tingling down the leg — that means too much, not 'good stretch.' Keep it gentle and brief; never hold at the tension end.
regression: Reduce the range at both ends (less knee straightening, smaller head movement) and do fewer, slower reps. Small and gentle is the whole point of flossing.
remediation: If even a small glide provokes shooting leg symptoms, stop and flag it — that pattern wants a clinician's eyes before continuing, not more reps.

name: Toe Yoga
desc: Lift your big toe while keeping the other four down, then switch — lift the four toes and press the big toe down. Alternate 10 times each foot.

name: Eyes-Closed Balance

form_cue: Get steady on one foot with eyes open first, standing knee soft and fingertips touching or hovering by the wall. Then close your eyes. Stand tall and breathe. You will feel the foot and ankle working much harder.
stop_condition: High fall risk: only do this within arm's reach of a wall or counter, on a clear floor. Open your eyes and put your foot down the moment you sway, feel dizzy or have pain. Do not try to save a wobble with your eyes shut.
regression: Keep both feet on the floor and close your eyes, with a hand on the wall or counter. Or stay on one foot and just soften your gaze rather than closing your eyes. Shorter holds are fine.
remediation: If you tip as soon as your eyes close, that is your answer for today: open them. Go back to Single-Leg Stand with eyes open and get a steady hold before trying again.

regression: Stand closer so the reach is short, or keep the toes of the back foot resting on the floor as a kickstand. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your back rounds, the standing knee wobbles inward, or you fall onto the table, shorten the reach and use the kickstand. Practise Single-Leg Stand until you can hold it steadily first.

form_cue: Keep both feet on the floor with knees soft and let the shake start from a gentle bounce through the legs. Jaw, shoulders and hands stay loose. It should feel easy and relaxed, not forced.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness, unsteadiness, shortness of breath that feels unusual, or any joint pain. Stand next to a chair or counter you can hold if your balance is unsure.
regression: Shake more gently and for a shorter time, hold a chair with one hand, or do it sitting and shake just your arms and legs.
remediation: If you feel tense or jarred, make it smaller and softer: keep your heels down and your knees unlocked, and let your arms hang instead of throwing them about.

name: Desk Reset Sequence
desc: Chin tuck (10 sec), shoulder shrug release (5 reps), wrist circles (10 each way), seated twist (10 sec each side), ankle circles (10 each way). A 2-minute desk break.
progression: Add standing components between seated ones
Customize the sequence for your tightest areas

pairs_with.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Add breathing to the desk reset for more benefit

pairs_with.name: Standing Full Body Shake
pairs_with.reason: Desk reset then stand and shake

form_cue: Move through each mini-exercise gently and in order — it's a mobility reset, not a workout. Follow each component's own gentle, controlled form.
stop_condition: Stop any single component that provokes pain, dizziness, or tingling — skip it and continue with the rest.
regression: Do fewer of the components, or fewer reps of each.
remediation: See each individual exercise's cues if any part feels off.

name: Morning Wake-Up Flow
desc: Overhead reach (10 sec), side bend each way (10 sec), forward fold (15 sec), standing back extension (5 sec), shoulder rolls (10 each way), neck rotations (5 each way).

phases.label: Overhead reach (10 sec), side bend each way (10...

progression: Create your own personalized morning routine

pairs_with.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Start the morning with breath then movement

pairs_with.name: Standing March
pairs_with.reason: Flow then march to fully wake up

form_cue: Move slowly from one position to the next and keep breathing. Keep your knees soft in the fold, keep the back bend small with your hands on your hips, and keep neck movements slow. Each stretch should feel mild.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness or light-headedness, especially coming up from the fold or leaning back, sharp or pinching pain, or tingling. Rise slowly and stand near a support. A mild stretch is normal; pain is not.
regression: Shorten the holds, fold only halfway with your hands on your thighs or a chair, skip the back bend, or do the whole sequence seated.
remediation: If you lose balance or rush, take one normal breath between positions and make each one smaller. Leave out any position that is uncomfortable today.

name: Windmill Stretch
desc: Stand with feet wide, arms out in a T. Rotate and reach one hand to the opposite foot while the other arm points up. Alternate 8 reps each side.
progression: Reach to the shin, small rotation
Reach to the foot, full rotation
Keep both legs straight for a deeper hamstring stretch

pairs_with.name: Side Bend Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both stretch the lateral and rotational chains

pairs_with.name: Standing Forward Fold
pairs_with.reason: Windmill adds rotation to the fold

form_cue: Hinge from your hips with a long back and soft knees, then turn your chest so the top arm reaches up. Come all the way back up to the T between sides. Feel it in the back of the legs and through the trunk.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness as your head goes down or comes up, sharp low-back pain, or pain or tingling down a leg. Move slowly and do not swing. A stretch in the back of the thighs is normal.
regression: Reach only to the opposite knee or shin, bend your knees more, do fewer reps, or put the lower hand on a chair seat.
remediation: If your back rounds or you bounce to get lower, shorten the reach and slow down. Practise Standing Forward Fold first to get comfortable hinging at the hips.

name: Downward Dog
desc: From hands and knees, push hips up and back to form an inverted V. Press heels toward the floor, straighten legs. Hold 30 seconds.

phases.label: From hands and knees, push hips up and back to ...

progression: Knees bent, focus on spine length
Pedal the feet alternately for dynamic calf stretch

pairs_with.name: Cobra/Upward Dog
pairs_with.reason: Down dog and up dog flow together

pairs_with.name: Wall Calf Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Down dog also stretches the calves

form_cue: Spread your fingers, press the floor away and send your hips up and back so your back feels long. Bend your knees if that keeps your back straight; heels need not touch. Feel it in the shoulders, hamstrings and calves.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness, pressure in your head or eyes, sharp wrist or shoulder pain, or tingling in the hands. Come down to hands and knees and rise slowly. If head-down positions are a problem for you, check with a clinician first.
regression: Keep your knees well bent and shorten the hold, or do it with your hands on a sturdy chair seat or a wall so your head stays above your hips.
remediation: If your back rounds or your shoulders hunch to your ears, bend your knees more and push your hips back. Practise Standing Forward Fold first for hamstring length.

name: Cobra/Upward Dog
desc: From prone, push up through your hands lifting your chest while keeping hips on or near the floor. Open your chest and look slightly upward. Hold 20 seconds.

phases.label: From prone, push up through your hands lifting ...

progression: Press hips slightly off the floor (upward dog)
Flow between cobra and down dog

pairs_with.name: Downward Dog
pairs_with.reason: Cobra and down dog are the classic yoga pair

pairs_with.name: Child's Pose
pairs_with.reason: Extension then flexion for spinal balance

form_cue: Hands under your shoulders, press up only as far as your hips stay heavy and your low back feels comfortable. Draw your shoulders down away from your ears and keep your neck long. Feel a gentle arch and an open chest.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching low-back pain, pain or tingling into the buttocks or legs, or wrist pain. Mild pressure in the low back and a stretch across the tummy are normal. Do not crank your head back.
regression: Stay on your forearms, or press up only a little with your elbows bent and hips on the floor, and shorten the hold.
remediation: If your shoulders shrug up or you feel it all in one spot in the low back, lower down and lift less. Practise Sphinx Pose until it is comfortable.

name: Warrior II Pose
desc: Step wide, turn one foot out 90 degrees. Bend the front knee over the ankle, extend arms parallel to the floor. Hold 30 seconds each side.
progression: Transition to triangle pose by straightening the front leg

pairs_with.name: Side Bend Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Warrior II into extended side angle is a natural flow

pairs_with.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both open the hips in a wide stance

form_cue: Keep the front knee stacked over the ankle and pointing the same way as the toes, with your back leg straight and the outer edge of that foot pressed down. Trunk upright, shoulders relaxed. Feel the front thigh working.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching knee, hip or groin pain, or if you feel unsteady. Burning effort in the front thigh is normal; joint pain is not. Have a chair or wall within reach.
regression: Take a narrower stance with a shallower knee bend and a shorter hold, rest your hands on your hips, or hold a chair back with one hand.
remediation: If the front knee drifts inward or past your toes, come up higher and press the knee gently out over the foot. Practise Sumo Squat first to build strength in this wide stance.

name: Walking Lunge with Twist
desc: Step into a lunge, then rotate your torso toward the front leg. Return and step into a lunge on the other side. 8 lunges total (4 each side).
progression: Walking lunge with rotation, 4 each side
Add an overhead reach in the rotated position

pairs_with.name: Split Squat
pairs_with.reason: Split squat builds strength, walking lunge adds dynamics

pairs_with.name: Thoracic Rotation
pairs_with.reason: Both involve torso rotation

form_cue: Finish the lunge and feel steady before you turn. Front knee stays over the ankle and in line with the toes, trunk tall, and the turn comes from your ribs and chest. Feel the legs working and a gentle twist mid-back.
stop_condition: Stop at once with sharp or pinching knee, hip or back pain, or if you wobble or feel dizzy. Do this beside a wall or counter you can grab, on a clear, non-slip floor. Thigh effort is normal; joint pain is not.
regression: Stay in one spot: step back into a shallow split stance with a hand on a chair, and make the turn small. Do fewer lunges.
remediation: If your front knee caves in or you tip as you twist, lunge less deep and make the twist smaller, or leave it out. Practise World's Greatest Stretch first for the rotation.

name: Burpee (Modified)
desc: Stand, place hands on the floor, step or jump feet back to plank, lower to the floor, push up, step or jump feet forward, stand up. 8 reps.

phases.label: Stand, place hands on the floor, step or jump f...

progression: Step back to plank, step forward, 5 reps
Step back, push-up from knees, 6 reps
Add a small jump at the top

pairs_with.name: Inchworm
pairs_with.reason: Inchworm is the slower version of a burpee

pairs_with.name: Standing Full Body Shake
pairs_with.reason: Shake out after intense effort

form_cue: Step, do not jump, unless stepping is already easy. Bend your knees to get your hands down, hold a straight line from head to heels in the plank, and lower with control. Stand all the way up each rep. Steady pace.
stop_condition: Stop at once with chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual breathlessness, or sharp wrist, shoulder, back or knee pain. Hard breathing and effort are normal. Rise slowly. Check with a clinician first if you have a heart or blood pressure condition.
regression: Step back and step forward only, leaving out the lowering and push-up, with your hands on a sturdy chair seat or bench instead of the floor. Do fewer reps.
remediation: If your hips sag in the plank or you start to collapse to the floor, slow down, rest between reps and drop your knees for the push-up. Practise Inchworm first.

name: Turkish Get-Up (Half)
desc: Lie on your back with your RIGHT arm reaching straight up at the ceiling, your right knee bent and that foot flat, and your left arm and leg relaxed out to the side. Keeping your right arm pointing up the whole time, roll onto your left forearm, then your left hand, and press your hips up off the floor. Sweep your left leg back underneath into a kneeling position, then reverse the steps to lie back down. Switch sides. 3 each side.
progression: Just the roll to elbow and back, each side
Add a light weight in the raised hand

pairs_with.name: Sit-to-Stand
pairs_with.reason: Both train getting up from the floor/chair

pairs_with.name: Bird Dog
pairs_with.reason: Both require coordinated full-body stability

form_cue: Keep your eyes on the raised hand and that arm straight up the whole time. Press through the bent-leg foot to roll up, one step at a time, with a pause at each stage, and reverse just as slowly.
stop_condition: Stop at once with sharp or pinching shoulder pain in either arm, wrist or back pain, dizziness on coming up or lying down, or if the supporting arm feels shaky. Use no weight, and have a clear floor around you.
regression: Do only the roll to your forearm and back down, without lifting your hips or sweeping the leg, and do fewer reps each side.
remediation: If the raised arm drifts or the supporting shoulder sinks toward your ear, go back to the last stage you can do smoothly and push the floor away with the supporting hand. Practise Sit-to-Stand for leg strength.

name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
desc: Tense each muscle group for 5 seconds then release: feet, calves, thighs, glutes, core, hands, arms, shoulders, face. Focus on the contrast between tension and relaxation.

phases.label: Tense each muscle group for 5 seconds then rele...

progression: 5-second tense, quick release, move through body
5-second tense, slow release, savor the relaxation
Focus on the groups where you hold the most tension

pairs_with.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Breathing and muscle relaxation together

pairs_with.name: Jaw Release
pairs_with.reason: Jaw is often the most tension-holding muscle

form_cue: Tense each group to a MODERATE (not maximal) level for about 5 seconds, then fully release and notice the contrast. Keep breathing; never clench hard enough to cramp or strain a joint.
stop_condition: Stop tensing any area that's injured or wants to cramp, and don't hold the breath.
regression: Use lighter tension, or skip any sore/injured group and just relax it.
remediation: If a group cramps (calves and feet are common), use gentler tension there.

name: Jaw Release
desc: Let your jaw hang open. Place your tongue on the roof of your mouth. Move your jaw gently side to side 10 times, then open and close slowly 10 times.
progression: Press tongue to roof of mouth while opening jaw
Massage jaw muscles with fingertips for 30 seconds

pairs_with.name: Suboccipital Release
pairs_with.reason: Jaw and suboccipital muscles are neurologically linked

pairs_with.name: Neck Side Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Jaw and neck tension often go together

form_cue: Let the jaw hang loose and rest the tongue lightly on the roof of the mouth behind the teeth — a passive release into a neutral, relaxed position.
stop_condition: Stop with any jaw-joint (TMJ) pain or clicking that hurts. It should feel like a release, not a stretch.
regression: Just soften the jaw without any specific tongue placement.
remediation: If the jaw is painful or clicky (TMJ issues), keep it very gentle and see a clinician if it persists.

name: Eye Circles
desc: Without moving your head, trace a large circle with your eyes — look up, right, down, left. 5 circles each direction. Relieves eye strain from screens.

phases.label: Without moving your head, trace a large circle ...

progression: Focus on a near object then a far object (20-20-20 rule)
Combine with palming (cover closed eyes with warm palms)

pairs_with.name: Desk Reset Sequence
pairs_with.reason: Eye circles fit into any desk break routine

pairs_with.name: Chin Tuck
pairs_with.reason: Eye and neck work together for screen-related tension

form_cue: Keep the head still and move ONLY the eyes in slow full circles — up, out, down, in — smooth tracking, without straining to the very corners.
stop_condition: Stop with eye strain, headache, or dizziness — reduce the range and slow down; rest if the eyes feel tired.
regression: Smaller circles, fewer reps, blink between sets.
remediation: If it triggers dizziness, do fewer and slower, and look at a far point to reset.

name: Lunge Matrix
desc: Do one forward lunge, one lateral lunge, and one reverse lunge on each leg. That's one round. Do 3 rounds. Hits every hip and leg angle.
progression: Slow each lunge to 3 seconds down, 3 seconds up
Add a medicine ball or light weight

pairs_with.name: Walking Lunge with Twist
pairs_with.reason: Add rotation to the lunge matrix

pairs_with.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Stretch after the lateral lunges

form_cue: In every lunge the bending knee follows the line of the toes and the foot stays flat. Keep your trunk tall; for the side lunge, sit your hips back with the other leg straight. Feel the thighs and buttocks working.
stop_condition: Stop at once with sharp or pinching knee, hip or groin pain, or if you lose your balance. Keep a sturdy chair or counter within reach and use a non-slip floor. Muscle burn is normal; joint pain is not.
regression: Make each lunge shallow and take a shorter step, hold a chair or counter with one hand, and do fewer rounds.
remediation: If your knee caves inward or you push off with a lurch, shorten the step and reduce the depth. Practise Split Squat first until you can lower and rise under control.

name: Wall Squat with Calf Raise
desc: Hold a wall sit position. Rise up onto your toes and hold 3 seconds, then lower heels. 10 calf raises while holding the wall sit.
progression: 5 calf raises in a high wall sit
10 calf raises in a 90-degree wall sit
Hold the calf raise for 5 seconds each
Single-leg calf raises in wall sit position

pairs_with.name: Wall Sit
pairs_with.reason: Wall sit alone, then add the calf raise challenge

pairs_with.name: Calf Raise
pairs_with.reason: Combines two exercises for efficiency

form_cue: Keep your back and head on the wall and knees over your ankles, in line with your toes. Rise onto the balls of both feet without your hips sliding up or down, then lower your heels slowly. Feel thighs and calves working.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp pain in or around the kneecap, calf cramp, or if your feet start to slip. Burning effort in the thighs and calves is normal. Wear non-slip shoes and slide up the wall to stand if you feel unsteady.
regression: Sit higher on the wall with only a slight knee bend, do fewer raises, or lower your heels straight away without the hold.
remediation: If your knees fall inward or your hips creep up the wall as you tire, stop the set and rest. Practise Wall Sit on its own first, with heels down.

name: Stork Stand with Hip Hinge
desc: Stand on one leg, hinge at the hip reaching one arm to the floor while the free leg extends behind you, then return to standing. 6 reps each leg.
progression: Touch a chair or bench in front of you
Slow to 3 seconds down, 3 seconds up
Hold a light weight in the reaching hand

pairs_with.name: Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight)
pairs_with.reason: Same pattern with arm reach added

pairs_with.name: Clock Reach
pairs_with.reason: Both are advanced single-leg balance exercises

form_cue: Tip forward from the hip like a seesaw: as your chest goes down the back leg goes up, back flat, hips level and facing the floor. Keep the standing knee slightly soft. Feel the back of the standing thigh and buttock.
stop_condition: Stop at once if you start to lose balance, or with sharp low-back, hip or knee pain or dizziness. Do this beside a sturdy chair or counter you can grab. Wobbling at the ankle and hamstring stretch are normal.
regression: Reach to a chair seat instead of the floor, keep the back toes lightly touching the ground, or hold a counter with your free hand. Do fewer reps.
remediation: If your back rounds or your hip opens out to the side, hinge less far and slow down. Practise Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight) on two legs until the hinge feels natural.

name: Squat to Overhead Press
desc: Hold light weights at shoulder height. Squat down, then as you stand, press the weights overhead. 10 reps. A compound movement for the whole body.

phases.label: Hold light weights at shoulder height

progression: Bodyweight squat to overhead reach, 8 reps
Slow the squat, fast press, 10 reps
Add a 2-second hold at the bottom and top

pairs_with.name: Bodyweight Squat
pairs_with.reason: Build squat strength before adding the press

pairs_with.name: Overhead Reach
pairs_with.reason: Mobility for the overhead position

form_cue: Sit your hips back and down with heels flat and knees in line with your toes, then stand up fully before the weights finish overhead. Keep your ribs down so your low back does not arch. Legs and shoulders share the work.
stop_condition: Stop at once with sharp or pinching shoulder, knee or back pain, dizziness, or if you cannot control the weights overhead. Keep weights light and do not hold your breath. Muscle effort is normal; joint pain is not.
regression: Use no weights and simply reach your arms overhead, squat only part of the way or down to a chair seat, and do fewer reps.
remediation: If your back arches as you press or your heels lift as you squat, put the weights down and reduce the depth. Practise Bodyweight Squat first until it is steady.

name: Reverse Lunge to Knee Drive
desc: Step one foot back into a reverse lunge, then drive that knee up in front of you as you stand. 8 reps each leg. Builds balance, strength, and coordination.
progression: Slow reverse lunge, gentle knee lift
Full lunge, high knee drive, 8 reps
Add a brief pause on the knee drive
Hold a light weight at chest

pairs_with.name: Split Squat
pairs_with.reason: Static lunge builds base for dynamic lunge

pairs_with.name: Standing March
pairs_with.reason: March is the warm-up for knee drives

form_cue: Step back softly onto the ball of the foot, lower with your front knee over the ankle, then push through the front heel to stand tall and bring the back knee up. Finish upright, not leaning back. Move with control.
stop_condition: Stop at once with sharp or pinching knee or hip pain, dizziness, or if you cannot stay balanced. Do this beside a sturdy chair or counter and hold it if you need to. Thigh and buttock effort is normal.
regression: Hold a chair or counter with one hand, take a shallow step back, and lift the knee only a little, or tap the foot down beside the other. Do fewer reps.
remediation: If you wobble at the top or the front knee caves inward, slow down and put the foot down between the lunge and the knee lift. Practise Split Squat first.

name: Pelvic Floor Elevator
desc: Sitting tall and breathing normally, find your pelvic floor muscles - the ones you would use to stop yourself passing gas - and keep your buttocks and thighs relaxed. Gently lift them a little (first floor), then more (second floor), then to a strong-but-comfortable squeeze (third floor). Then lower back down floor by floor and fully relax before the next rep. Hold 5 seconds at each floor. 5 reps. Relaxing fully matters as much as the squeeze — some pelvic-floor specialists find urinary symptoms come as much from muscles that cannot relax properly as from weak ones.

phases.label: Imagine your pelvic floor is an elevator

progression: Find the contraction, hold at floor 1
Quick flicks: contract and release rapidly 10 times

pairs_with.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Pelvic floor and diaphragm work together

pairs_with.name: Pelvic Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Both engage the deep core system

form_cue: Gently lift the pelvic floor in graded stages (like a slow elevator up), then fully RELAX back down between reps — a lift-and-let-go. Keep breathing; don't clench the glutes or hold your breath.
stop_condition: Stop if you can't fully relax between reps, feel pain, or find yourself bearing DOWN instead of lifting. Over-gripping is counterproductive.
regression: Use just the first 'floor' (a light lift) and focus on the full release, which matters as much as the lift.
remediation: If you're unsure you're finding the right muscles, this is worth checking with a pelvic-health PT — cueing it as a bear-down is a common mistake.
