name: Standing Hip Abduction
desc: Stand on one leg, hold a wall for balance. Lift the other leg out to the side about 12 inches, hold 2 seconds, lower slowly. 12 reps each side.

pairs_with.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
pairs_with.reason: Same muscle group, different position

pairs_with.name: Banded Lateral Walk
pairs_with.reason: Both strengthen hip abductors

form_cue: Stand tall and lift the leg straight out to the side with toes pointing forward, keeping your trunk upright. The lift is modest. You should feel it in the outer hip of the lifting leg and also in the standing hip.
stop_condition: Keep a hand on the wall or a sturdy chair. Stop if you feel unsteady or dizzy, or get sharp or pinching pain in either hip, the groin or the low back. A tired feeling in the outer hips is normal.
regression: Lift the leg only a few inches without the hold, keep both hands on the support and do fewer reps. Tap the foot down between reps to reset your balance.
remediation: If you lean your trunk away or the toes turn out to get the leg higher, lower the lift. Stay tall and lift only as far as you can with the body still.

name: Seated Ankle Pumps
desc: Sit with feet flat on the floor. Alternate pointing toes down then pulling toes up, pumping the ankle joint. 20 pumps each foot. Boosts circulation.

phases.label: Sit with feet flat on the floor

progression: Add toe curls at the bottom
Press toes into the floor at the bottom for resistance

pairs_with.name: Ankle Circles
pairs_with.reason: Both are seated ankle mobility exercises

pairs_with.name: Calf Raise
pairs_with.reason: Pumps are the seated warm-up for standing calf raises

form_cue: Alternate pointing the toes down and pulling them up, pumping through the full ankle range — smooth and rhythmic, feet near the floor.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp pain or cramping. (Great for circulation and very low risk.)
regression: Smaller, slower pumps; even a little movement aids circulation.
remediation: If the calf cramps on the point, favor the pull-up (dorsiflexion) direction.

name: Standing Chest Fly
desc: Hold a band behind your back with both arms extended. Bring arms forward in a hugging motion, squeezing your chest. 12 reps.

phases.label: Hold a band behind your back with both arms ext...

progression: Add a 2-second squeeze at the front

pairs_with.name: Band Pull-Apart
pairs_with.reason: Push and pull for balanced shoulder/chest work

pairs_with.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen then stretch the chest

form_cue: With the band across your upper back and an end in each hand, keep a slight bend in the elbows and sweep the arms forward as if hugging a wide tree, then open slowly. Stand tall with shoulders down. Feel it in the chest.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the front of the shoulder, chest pain or pressure, or numbness or tingling in the arms. Muscle effort in the chest is normal. Check the band for nicks and keep it flat across your back, not on your neck.
regression: Use a lighter band, hold it with more slack, open the arms only part of the way back, or do fewer reps.
remediation: If your shoulders round forward or shrug, or your elbows lock, the band is too strong or you are opening too far. Lighten it and shorten the range. Go back to Wall Push-Up if the movement stays hard to control.

name: Neck Retraction (Wall)
desc: Stand with your back against a wall. Push the back of your head into the wall, making a double chin. Hold 5 seconds, release. 10 reps.

phases.label: Stand with your back against a wall

progression: Add wall angels while maintaining the retraction

pairs_with.name: Chin Tuck
pairs_with.reason: Wall version gives tactile feedback for chin tucks

pairs_with.name: Wall Angel
pairs_with.reason: Both use the wall for posture feedback

form_cue: Slide your head straight back as if along a shelf, eyes and chin level, until the back of your head presses the wall. Do not tip your head back or chin down. Feel a stretch at the base of the skull.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness, sharp or pinching neck pain, headache, or numbness or tingling into an arm. A stretch at the back of the neck and gentle effort in front are normal. Press lightly; never force it.
regression: Press more gently, shorten the hold and do fewer reps. If your head does not reach the wall comfortably, place a small folded towel behind it.
remediation: If your chin lifts or your low back arches off the wall, step your feet a little forward, soften your knees and press less hard. Practise Chin Tuck sitting down first.

name: Scapular Push-Up
desc: In a plank position, keep arms straight and push your upper back toward the ceiling by protracting your shoulder blades. Then let them squeeze together. 10 reps.

phases.label: In a plank position, keep arms straight and pus...

progression: Add a hold at full protraction for 3 seconds

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Squeeze is retraction, scapular push-up is protraction

pairs_with.name: Plank Hold
pairs_with.reason: Both are done from plank position

form_cue: Hold a plank with elbows locked and body in one line. Without bending the arms, push the floor away so the upper back rises, then let the chest sink between the shoulders. Only the shoulder blades move.
stop_condition: Stop with wrist pain, pinching in the shoulder, low-back pain from sagging hips, or neck strain. Effort around the shoulder blades and trunk is normal.
regression: Do it from your knees, or standing with your hands on a wall or counter. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your elbows bend, your hips sag or your head pokes forward, move to the knees or the wall. If you cannot feel the shoulder blades moving, practise Scapular Squeeze first.

name: Hip Hike
desc: Stand on a step with one foot hanging off the edge. Let that hip drop, then hike it up by squeezing the standing-side hip. 12 reps each side.
progression: Hold at the top for 3 seconds
Add light ankle weight on the hanging leg

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Hip hikes build the stability for single-leg activities

pairs_with.name: Banded Lateral Walk
pairs_with.reason: Both target glute medius for hip stability

form_cue: Keep both knees straight and your trunk tall. The movement comes only from the pelvis tilting: let the free side lower a little, then lift it by working the hip of the standing leg. Feel it in the side of the standing hip.
stop_condition: Use a low, stable step next to a wall or rail and keep a hand on it. Stop if you feel unsteady or dizzy, or get sharp pain in the standing hip, knee or low back. A tired feeling in the side of the hip is normal.
regression: Do it on flat ground beside a counter, lifting one foot just off the floor and hiking that hip, with a smaller movement and fewer reps.
remediation: If you bend the standing knee or lean your trunk sideways, you are not using the hip. Shrink the movement and watch your belt line in a mirror, and practise Standing Hip Abduction first.

name: Hamstring Curl (Standing)
desc: Stand holding a wall for balance. Bend one knee, bringing your heel toward your glute. Lower slowly. 12 reps each leg.
progression: Hold at top for 3 seconds, 12 reps

pairs_with.name: Standing Quad Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Hamstring curl strengthens, quad stretch stretches — balance

pairs_with.name: Seated Knee Extension
pairs_with.reason: Quad extension and hamstring curl pair for knee health

form_cue: Stand tall holding the wall, thighs side by side, and bend one knee to bring the heel up behind you without the thigh swinging forward or the back arching. Feel it in the back of the thigh. Lower slowly.
stop_condition: Effort behind the thigh is normal. Stop with a hamstring cramp, sharp pain in or behind the knee, low-back pain, or unsteadiness. Keep hold of the wall or a sturdy chair throughout.
regression: Bend the knee only partway, hold a counter with both hands and do fewer reps.
remediation: If your thigh swings forward or your back arches, you are using the hip instead of the knee. Stand closer to the wall, keep the knees level, and curl through a smaller range slowly.

name: Wall Sit with Ball Squeeze
desc: Hold a wall sit position with a ball or pillow between your knees. Squeeze the ball while holding the sit. Hold 20 seconds, rest, repeat 3 times.

phases.label: Hold a wall sit position with a ball or pillow ...

progression: Pulse squeeze (quick squeeze-release) 20 times while sitting

pairs_with.name: Wall Sit
pairs_with.reason: Wall sit is the base, ball squeeze adds adductor work

pairs_with.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen then stretch the inner thighs

form_cue: Back flat on the wall, knees over ankles and in line with your hips, and squeeze the ball evenly with both knees while you keep breathing. Feel the thighs and inner thighs working.
stop_condition: Burning, shaking thighs are normal effort. Stop with sharp pain in or behind the kneecap, groin pain, back pain, dizziness, or if you feel you may slide. Stop before your legs give out, and do not hold your breath.
regression: Sit higher on the wall with a lighter squeeze and a shorter hold, or do fewer repeats. Keep a chair beside you to push up from.
remediation: If your feet creep in, your back peels off the wall or you hold your breath, come up higher and squeeze more gently. Go back to plain Wall Sit until that hold feels steady.

name: Heel Drop (Eccentric Calf)
desc: Stand on the edge of a step on your toes. Slowly lower one heel below the step over 5 seconds. Push back up with both feet. 10 reps each side.
progression: Hold a light weight for added load

pairs_with.name: Wall Calf Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Eccentric strengthening and stretching for calf health

pairs_with.name: Soleus Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Heel drops work both gastrocnemius and soleus

form_cue: Balls of the feet on the step, hold a rail, rise on both feet, then shift onto one leg and lower that heel slowly and smoothly below the step. Push back up with both feet. Feel it in the calf and behind the ankle.
stop_condition: A strong calf stretch and effort is normal. Stop with sharp pain in the heel, the cord behind the ankle or the calf, a sudden pull or pop, or unsteadiness. Always hold a rail or wall, on a step that will not slip.
regression: Lower both heels together instead of one, drop only to step level instead of below it, and do fewer reps. Or do the slow lowering on flat floor.
remediation: If you drop quickly, bounce at the bottom or cannot control the lowering, it is too much load for now. Use both feet and practise Single-Leg Calf Raise on flat ground first.

name: Wrist Roller
desc: Hold a light weight on a string tied to a dowel. Roll the dowel to wind the string up, then slowly unwind. 3 reps. Builds forearm and grip endurance.

phases.label: Hold a light weight on a string tied to a dowel

pairs_with.name: Grip Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Both build grip and forearm strength

pairs_with.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Stretch after intense wrist strengthening

form_cue: Keep your elbows bent at your sides and wrists level, and turn the dowel one hand at a time with small, steady wrist movements. Unwind as slowly as you wind. The effort belongs in the forearms; shoulders stay relaxed.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp wrist, elbow or thumb pain, numbness or tingling in the hand, or if your grip starts to fail. Forearm burn is normal. Keep the weight very light and over a clear floor, away from your feet.
regression: Use a lighter weight or none at all, wind the string only part of the way, rest your forearms on a table edge, and do fewer reps.
remediation: If your shoulders hunch or you start to jerk the dowel, lower the weight to the floor and rest. Practise Grip Squeeze first to build hand and forearm endurance.

name: Tree Pose
desc: Stand on one foot, place the other foot on your inner calf or thigh (never on the knee). Bring hands to chest or overhead. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Foot on inner calf, hands at chest
Foot on inner thigh, hands at chest

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Tree pose is the yoga progression of single-leg stand

pairs_with.name: Warrior II Pose
pairs_with.reason: Both are standing yoga balance poses

form_cue: Press the foot and the inner calf or thigh gently into each other, well away from the knee joint. Keep the standing knee soft, hips level and facing forward, and eyes on a fixed point. Feel the standing leg and outer hip.
stop_condition: Stand beside a wall or counter. Put your foot down and stop if you feel dizzy, very unsteady, or have pain in the standing knee, hip or ankle, or pinching in the bent hip. Small ankle wobbles are normal.
regression: Rest the heel on the inside of your standing ankle with the toes still on the floor, and keep one hand on a wall. Take a shorter hold if you need to.
remediation: If your hip hikes up, you lean to the side, or the foot keeps sliding, lower the foot and keep your hands at your chest. Practise Single-Leg Stand until you can hold it steadily first.

name: Deep Breathing with Arm Raise
desc: Breathe in while slowly raising arms overhead. Breathe out while lowering arms. 8 breaths. Coordinates breath with movement.

phases.label: Breathe in while slowly raising arms overhead

progression: Add a side bend at the top
Rise onto toes at the top of the inhale

pairs_with.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Seated breathing then standing with movement

pairs_with.name: Overhead Reach
pairs_with.reason: Both involve reaching overhead, one static, one with breath

form_cue: Let the breath set the pace: your arms rise for the whole inhale and lower for the whole exhale. Keep your shoulders away from your ears and your ribs from flaring. Breathe quietly and comfortably, not as deeply as possible.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel light-headed or dizzy, or have pinching pain in a shoulder. Return to normal breathing and rest. Stand near a support if your balance is unsure.
regression: Raise your arms only to shoulder height, or out to the sides, and take fewer breaths. You can do this seated.
remediation: If you run out of breath before your arms get there, move your arms a little faster or raise them less high. Do not stretch the breath to fit the movement.

name: Resistance Band Row
desc: Anchor a band at waist height. Hold with both hands, pull toward your body squeezing shoulder blades. 12 reps. Strengthens the mid-back.

phases.label: Anchor a band at waist height

progression: Add a 2-second hold at full contraction

pairs_with.name: Band Pull-Apart
pairs_with.reason: Both use bands for upper back strengthening

pairs_with.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen the back, stretch the front

form_cue: Stand tall with feet hip-width and knees soft. Pull your elbows straight back close to your sides, squeezing the shoulder blades together and down, then return slowly. Chest stays up, shoulders stay away from your ears.
stop_condition: Check that the band is undamaged and firmly anchored before each set. Stop with pinching in the front of the shoulder, neck strain, low-back pain from leaning back, or tingling in the arms. Mid-back effort is normal.
regression: Step closer to the anchor so the band is slacker, use a lighter band, or do it seated on a sturdy chair. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If you shrug, lean back or let the band snap you forward, the resistance is too much. Lighten it and slow down, or practise Scapular Squeeze first to find the movement.

name: Seated Spinal Wave
desc: Sit at the edge of your chair with both feet flat. Starting from the bottom, slowly tuck your pelvis and round your lower back, then mid-back, then upper back into a gentle slouch. Then reverse it - tilt your pelvis forward and un-curl from the bottom up until your chest lifts and your back gently arches. Flow slowly back and forth between the two. 8 waves.

phases.label: Sit at the edge of your chair

progression: Round and extend in one movement
Segment the wave from bottom to top
Add a gentle twist at the top of extension

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow
pairs_with.reason: Spinal wave is the seated version of cat-cow

pairs_with.name: Seated Twist
pairs_with.reason: Wave (flexion/extension) plus twist (rotation) for full seated spine mobility

form_cue: Roll into a slouch one segment at a time — low back, then mid, then upper — a smooth wave of flexion, then reverse to stack back up tall. Controlled, not a collapse.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp back pain or any tingling down the legs. If forward-rounding is your provocative direction, keep it small or skip it.
regression: Move through a smaller range, or just alternate a gentle slouch and sit-tall without the segmental detail.
remediation: If segmenting is hard, practice a simple pelvic tilt (rocking the pelvis) to find low-back movement first.
review_note: PT APPROVED 2026-09-15 by FaithPT (StretchSmart's PT cofounder), answering the 09-10 queue review, verbatim (19:05Z): "Spinal wave is excellent EXCEPT- I know what you are getting at re: complex movement patterns and dementia, but I am not sure this qualifies as a true “complex movement pattern”. name: Wall Hamstring Stretch
desc: Lie on your back with your hips close to a wall and your legs straight up resting against it. Scoot your hips closer to the wall until you feel a gentle stretch up the backs of your thighs - the closer you are, the stronger it is. Relax and breathe; bend your knees to come out. Hold 45 seconds.

phases.label: Lie on your back with hips near a wall

progression: Bend knees, hips away from wall
Straighten legs, hips closer to wall
Hips against the wall, legs straight
Open legs into a V for inner thigh stretch

pairs_with.name: Lying Hamstring Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Wall version is more passive and restorative

pairs_with.name: Supine Twist
pairs_with.reason: Both are restorative floor stretches

form_cue: Lie on your back with your tailbone and low back resting on the floor and legs relaxed up the wall, knees soft if needed. The stretch should be a gentle pull up the backs of the thighs.
stop_condition: A gentle pull behind the thighs is normal. Stop with low-back pain, sharp pain behind the knees, or numbness, tingling or cold feet. Bend your knees, roll to your side and rest before getting up slowly.
regression: Move your hips further from the wall and keep your knees bent. A shorter hold is fine.
remediation: If your tailbone lifts off the floor or your knees will not stay comfortably straight, you are too close. Slide back from the wall until your hips rest flat and the legs can relax.

name: Thoracic Spine Windmill
desc: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent and both arms stretched out in front of you, palms together (rest your top knee on a foam roller, pillow or cushion to keep your hips from rolling). Keeping your knees down, sweep your top arm up and over in a big arc to the other side, following your hand with your eyes as your upper back rotates open. Slowly sweep it back, then switch sides. 8 reps each side.
progression: Hold at tight spots for 5 seconds
Add a light weight in the moving hand

pairs_with.name: Open Book Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Open book is simpler, windmill adds range and load

pairs_with.name: Thread the Needle
pairs_with.reason: Both are thoracic rotation exercises on the floor

form_cue: Keep the top knee pressed onto its cushion throughout. Sweep the top arm in a slow arc up past your head and over, eyes following the hand, so the turn comes from the upper back. Feel it across the chest, shoulder and mid-back.
stop_condition: Safety: move slowly and never force the arm toward the floor. Stop with sharp or pinching shoulder pain, a slipping or catching feeling in the shoulder, back pain, dizziness, or tingling down the arm.
regression: Make a small arc and stop when the arm points to the ceiling, bending the elbow if that is easier. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your top knee lifts off the cushion or your hips roll back, the low back is doing the twisting. Shrink the arc and pin the knee, or go back to Open Book Stretch.

name: Single-Leg Deadlift to Row
desc: Hold a light weight. Hinge on one leg (Romanian deadlift), then pull the weight to your hip in a row. Stand back up. 6 reps each side.
progression: Add a 2-second hold in both hinge and row positions

pairs_with.name: Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight)
pairs_with.reason: Build the hinge pattern first, then add the row

pairs_with.name: Resistance Band Row
pairs_with.reason: Both include a rowing component

form_cue: Hinge from the hip with a flat back and hips level, standing knee slightly soft. Get steady first, then pull your elbow back toward your hip without twisting your trunk. Feel the standing thigh, buttock and upper back.
stop_condition: Stop at once if you start to lose balance, or with sharp low-back, hip or shoulder pain or dizziness. Do this beside a sturdy chair or counter you can grab, and keep the weight light. Muscle effort is normal.
regression: Use no weight, keep the back toes on the floor as a kickstand, and rest your free hand on a chair or counter. Do fewer reps.
remediation: If your back rounds or your trunk twists as you row, set the weight down and hinge less far. Practise Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight) on two legs first.

name: Standing Calf Stretch on Step
desc: Stand on a step with your heels hanging off the edge. Let your heels drop below the step level. Hold 20 seconds. Switch to bent-knee for 20 more seconds.

phases.label: Stand on a step with your heels hanging off the...

progression: Full drop, 20 seconds straight and bent knee
One leg at a time for deeper stretch

pairs_with.name: Wall Calf Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Two positions for the same stretch

pairs_with.name: Calf Raise
pairs_with.reason: Step stretch and step raise use the same setup

form_cue: Balls of both feet on the step, hold a rail, and let the heels sink slowly under control with knees straight, then with knees slightly bent. Feel the stretch in the calves, lower down with the knees bent.
stop_condition: A steady pull in the calves is normal. Stop with sharp pain in the heel or behind the ankle, a cramp in the arch, or unsteadiness. Hold a rail or wall the whole time and use a step that will not slip.
regression: Let the heels drop only to step level, or do one foot at a time with the other foot fully on the step. If the step feels unsafe, do Wall Calf Stretch on the floor.
remediation: If you bounce, grip with your toes or cannot relax into it, come up a little and hold more firmly. If your feet slide on the step, switch to Wall Calf Stretch instead.

name: Breath Hold Walk
desc: Take a normal breath in, exhale normally, then hold your breath and walk until you feel a moderate urge to breathe. Resume breathing and walk normally for 1 minute. Repeat 3 times.

phases.label: Take a normal breath in, exhale normally, then ...

progression: Practice nose-only breathing during recovery walks

pairs_with.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Calm breathing before and after breath holds

pairs_with.name: Standing March
pairs_with.reason: Both are walking-based exercises

form_cue: Start the hold after a normal, relaxed breath out, not a big one, and walk at an easy pace. Start breathing again at the first clear urge to breathe; your next breath in should be calm and through the nose, not a gasp.
stop_condition: Stop at once and breathe normally with dizziness, light-headedness, tingling, chest tightness, headache or a pounding heart. Never push the hold. Skip this and ask a clinician first if you have a heart, lung or blood pressure condition or are pregnant.
regression: Hold for only a few steps, do fewer repeats, or try the short breath hold sitting down before doing it while walking.
remediation: If you gasp or need several big breaths to recover, the hold was too long: shorten it. Practise Diaphragmatic Breathing until calm nose breathing is easy.

name: Prone Hip Extension
desc: Lie face down. Squeeze one glute and lift that leg straight up a few inches off the floor. Hold 3 seconds, lower. 10 reps each side.

pairs_with.name: Donkey Kick
pairs_with.reason: Both are prone glute exercises with different leverage

pairs_with.name: Superman Hold
pairs_with.reason: Prone hip extension is the single-leg version of superman legs

form_cue: Keep both hip bones pressed into the floor and the knee straight, and lift the leg from the glute just a few inches. Rest your forehead on your hands. Feel it in the buttock, with only light effort in the low back.
stop_condition: Stop with low-back pain or pinching, a hamstring cramp that does not ease, or tingling down the leg. Glute effort is normal. Height does not matter here, so never force the leg higher.
regression: Put a pillow under your hips and belly, lift the leg barely off the floor and skip the hold. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your pelvis rolls or your low back arches to lift the leg, the lift is too high. Squeeze the glute first, then lift only an inch or two. If it stays hard, go back to Donkey Kick.

name: Standing Piriformis Stretch
desc: Stand facing a sturdy table about hip height and rest one shin across it, knee bent and turned out, so the outer shin and knee are supported. Hold the table for balance, keep your back long, and hinge forward from your hips until you feel a comfortable stretch deep in that buttock. Hold, then switch legs. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Add a gentle torso rotation toward the stretched side

pairs_with.name: Figure Four Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Same stretch pattern, standing vs lying

pairs_with.name: Pigeon Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Standing version for when floor isn't available

form_cue: Rest the outer ankle/lower shin on the surface with the knee bent open — the stretch is in the outer hip/glute of that leg. Keep your standing leg soft (slight bend), hips square, and hinge forward from the hips with a flat back to deepen. Hold the table for balance the whole time.
stop_condition: Feel it in the outer hip/glute, not the knee. Stop with pain in either knee, the groin, or low back. This is a single-leg balance position — hold something stable, and if you feel unsteady at all, do the seated or floor version instead. Extra caution with knee history or hip-replacement precautions (crossed-leg external rotation) — skip unless cleared.
regression: Lower the surface (a chair seat instead of a table), keep more weight on the standing leg and hinge less, or switch to the seated Figure Four or supine version for full stability.
remediation: If balance is the limiter, do the seated Figure Four or the supine version — same target muscle without the balance demand.
review_note: FaithPT 2026-09-16, verbatim: "Ok so working on standing Piriformis stretch and the technique looks fine but I have problems with the intro and rationale. Relating it to low back pain is questionable, and  the importance of movement is not necessarily what this addresses, if you follow me. One can refer to excess sitting as a cause for tightness and relate it to hip alignment and/or sciatic compression but Piriformis tightness and lower back pain is reaching I think" ACTIONED: removed the 'back pain' concern tag — it made the app assert the link she calls reaching, AND it served this stretch to users who selected back pain in onboarding. TECHNIQUE UNCHANGED (she said it looks fine); no clinical copy added. Her acceptable framing (excess sitting -> tightness -> hip alignment / sciatic compression) is already carried by the remaining tags 'hip tightness' + 'sitting recovery' — no new vocabulary invented. STILL OPEN WITH HER: the research-insight card. Removing the tag does NOT change it (insight 27 still scores top on 'glutes'/'sitting'), the next candidate (21) makes the low-back claim harder, and the matcher's last tier is the whole pool so id 31 ('80% of adults experience low back pain... movement is the medicine') can surface on repeat views.

name: Wrist Push-Up Position Stretch
desc: In a push-up position on your knees, rock gently forward and backward over your wrists. Then flip hands so fingers point toward knees and rock back. 30 seconds each position.

phases.label: In a push-up position on your knees, rock gentl...

progression: Mostly on knees, light weight on wrists
More weight on wrists, rock gently

pairs_with.name: Tabletop Wrist Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Same concept with more body weight

pairs_with.name: Wall Push-Up
pairs_with.reason: Build wrist tolerance for push-up positions

form_cue: Keep your knees down, palms flat and elbows straight but not locked. Rock slowly and only as far as you feel a stretch in the forearm and wrist, with your shoulders over or just past your hands.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching wrist pain, or numbness or tingling in the hand or fingers. A firm stretch in the forearm is normal; pain in the joint is not. Take weight off your hands at once if it pinches.
regression: Sit back toward your heels to take weight off your hands, rock a smaller distance, shorten the time, or do it with your hands on a table or chair seat.
remediation: If the heels of your hands lift or your elbows bend, you have gone too far: back off until the palms are flat. Practise Tabletop Wrist Stretch first.

name: Seated Hip Flexor Stretch
desc: Sit at the edge of your chair, scoot one hip off the side and let that leg drop back and down. You'll feel the hip flexor stretch on the dropped side. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Reach the same-side arm overhead for more stretch

pairs_with.name: Seated Figure Four
pairs_with.reason: Both are seated hip stretches for desk breaks

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Seated version for when you can't get on the floor

form_cue: Let the leg drop back and down off the chair edge, tucking the pelvis slightly (posterior tilt) so the stretch lands in the FRONT of the hip/thigh, not the low back. Sit tall and stay stable on the seat.
stop_condition: Stop with low-back pinching (tuck the pelvis more), sharp groin pain, or if you feel unstable on the edge of the chair.
regression: Let the leg drop back only slightly; a small range still reaches the hip flexor, and hold the chair for stability.
remediation: If the low back arches to 'fake' the stretch, add a light core brace and tuck the pelvis so the hip does the work.

name: Lateral Neck Flexion with Resistance
desc: Place your hand on the side of your head. Push your head into your hand, resisting the motion with your hand so there's no movement. Hold 8 seconds each side, 5 reps.
progression: Strong resistance, 8-second holds, 5 reps each side

pairs_with.name: Isometric Neck Strengthening
pairs_with.reason: Isometrics in all directions for full neck strength

pairs_with.name: Neck CARs
pairs_with.reason: Strength and mobility together

form_cue: Press the head sideways INTO the hand while the hand fully resists so NOTHING moves — a pure isometric. Build the push gradually and keep the chin neutral, not poking forward.
stop_condition: Stop immediately with dizziness, sharp/shooting pain, or any tingling/numbness into the arm. Keep the force moderate — never a maximal strain on the neck. Skip it entirely if you have current neck pain or nerve symptoms.
regression: Use light pressure and short holds; the goal is control, not strength.
remediation: Master the gentle Chin Tuck and the forehead Isometric first — those build the base control before adding side-load.

name: Prone Neck Retraction
desc: Lie face down, forehead on a folded towel. Tuck your chin and lift your head 1 inch off the towel while maintaining the tuck. Hold 5 seconds, 8 reps.

phases.label: Lie face down, forehead on a folded towel

progression: Just the chin tuck, no lift

pairs_with.name: Neck Flexor Strengthening
pairs_with.reason: Supine and prone neck strengthening together

pairs_with.name: Prone Y Raise
pairs_with.reason: Both are prone upper body exercises

form_cue: Tuck your chin first, then float your head just off the towel with your eyes still looking at the floor and the back of your neck long. Keep your shoulders relaxed. The effort is in the back of the neck and between the shoulder blades.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp neck pain, headache, dizziness, or numbness or tingling into an arm. Mild muscle effort at the back of the neck is normal. Do not look forward or tip your head back.
regression: Do the chin tuck only with your forehead resting on the towel, or lift for a shorter hold and do fewer reps.
remediation: If your chin juts forward or you look up as you lift, the tuck has gone: rest, reset and lift less. Practise Neck Flexor Strengthening first.

name: Thoracic Foam Roller Rotation
desc: Sit on the floor with a foam roller behind you under your upper back. Hug yourself and rotate over the roller to one side, then the other. 8 reps each side.
progression: Hold at end range for 5 seconds
Move the roller to different thoracic levels

pairs_with.name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
pairs_with.reason: Extension and rotation on the roller for complete mobility

pairs_with.name: Thread the Needle
pairs_with.reason: Both are deep thoracic rotation exercises

form_cue: Knees bent, feet flat, roller across the upper back only. Arms hugged across your chest, chin slightly tucked. Turn your shoulders and ribs slowly to one side over the roller, then the other, keeping the hips still and the low back off the roller.
stop_condition: Safety: go slowly and stay in a small range. Stop with sharp spine or rib pain, neck strain, dizziness, or tingling into the arms. Skip it and ask a clinician first if you have osteoporosis or a past spinal fracture.
regression: Leave the roller out and make the same small hugging rotations lying on your back with knees bent, or sitting tall on a chair. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your hips roll with you, your neck strains or the roller slides, reduce the turn and reset your feet. If you cannot stay steady on the roller, go back to Foam Roller Thoracic Extension.

name: Jefferson Curl
desc: Stand on a low step. Tuck your chin and slowly round your spine one vertebra at a time, reaching toward the floor. Reverse to stand tall. 5 very slow reps. No weight needed.
progression: Standing on flat ground, small range
Standing on a step for more range
Aim to touch the step surface below your feet

pairs_with.name: Standing Forward Fold
pairs_with.reason: Forward fold is passive, Jefferson curl is active and controlled

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow
pairs_with.reason: Both work segmental spinal control

form_cue: Tuck your chin, then let the neck, upper back, mid back and low back round in turn, arms hanging heavy and knees straight but not locked. Uncurl from the bottom up, head last. Feel a stretch along the spine and backs of the legs.
stop_condition: Safety: use a low, stable step next to a wall or rail. Stop with dizziness, unsteadiness, sharp back pain, or pain or tingling down a leg. Skip it and ask a clinician if you have osteoporosis, disc problems or blood pressure concerns.
regression: Do it standing on the flat floor, rounding down only as far as your thighs or knees, with a hand on a counter or chair back. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If you hinge at the hips with a flat back, drop quickly or lose balance, shorten the range and slow down. Practise Standing Forward Fold first until rounding down and up feels controlled.

name: Side Plank Clamshell
desc: Hold a side plank with knees bent. Open the top knee like a clamshell while maintaining the plank. 10 reps each side.
progression: Side plank on knees, small clamshell opening
Full side plank (straight legs) with hip abduction

pairs_with.name: Side Plank
pairs_with.reason: Side plank is the base, adding clamshell increases difficulty

pairs_with.name: Clamshell
pairs_with.reason: Clamshell lying down builds toward the side plank version

form_cue: Elbow under your shoulder, knees bent, hips lifted and pushed forward so you are straight from knees to shoulders. Keep your feet together and open only the top knee without rolling back. Feel the side of both hips and waist.
stop_condition: This is a hard exercise. Stop if you feel sharp or pinching pain in the supporting shoulder, hip or lower back, or if your hips drop and you cannot keep them up. Burning effort in the side of the hip is normal.
regression: Lie on your side with your hips resting on the floor and do the knee opening without the plank. Or hold the bent-knee side plank without opening the knee. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your hips sag or your body rolls backward as the knee opens, make the opening smaller or rest. Build a steady Side Plank first, then add the knee movement.

name: Quadruped Hip Extension with Band
desc: Loop a band around one foot and hold the other end under your hands. From hands and knees, kick the banded leg straight back. 10 reps each side.
progression: Add a 3-second hold at full extension
Add a pulse at the top, 3 pulses per rep

pairs_with.name: Donkey Kick
pairs_with.reason: Bodyweight first, then add band resistance

pairs_with.name: Banded Lateral Walk
pairs_with.reason: Both use bands for glute strengthening

form_cue: Keep your back flat and hips square to the floor as you press the banded foot straight back until the leg is in line with your body, no higher. Return slowly against the band. Feel it in the glute of the kicking leg.
stop_condition: Check the band is not worn and is pinned firmly under your hands, since it can snap back toward your face. Stop with low-back pain, wrist pain, sharp pain in the supporting knee or pinching in the hip. Glute effort is normal.
regression: Use the lightest band or no band, kick back only part of the way and do fewer reps. Pad your knees with a mat or folded towel.
remediation: If your back arches or your hips twist as the leg goes back, the band is too strong or the kick too high. Drop the band and get Donkey Kick smooth first.

name: Eccentric Single-Leg Squat
desc: Stand on one leg in front of a chair. Slowly lower yourself onto the chair over 5 seconds, then stand up on both legs. 6 reps each leg.
progression: Hover above the seat without sitting

pairs_with.name: Sit-to-Stand
pairs_with.reason: Sit-to-stand is bilateral, this is unilateral

pairs_with.name: Pistol Squat Progression
pairs_with.reason: Eccentric squat builds toward pistol squat

form_cue: Send your hips back and lower slowly on one leg, keeping the knee in line with the toes and the heel down, until you are seated. Do not drop the last part. Feel it in the thigh and glute.
stop_condition: Hard thigh effort is normal. Stop with sharp or pinching knee pain, a knee that buckles, or loss of balance. Use a sturdy chair that cannot slide, placed against a wall, and keep a counter or second chair within reach.
regression: Use a higher seat or add a firm cushion, keep the toes of the other foot lightly on the floor, and lower for a shorter time. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If you drop onto the seat or the knee caves inward, the load is too much. Raise the seat, hold a support, or lower on both legs slowly. Step-Up is the exercise to build strength with first.

name: Hamstring Bridge March
desc: Hold a bridge position with feet further from hips (more hamstring emphasis). March by lifting one foot at a time while maintaining hip height. 8 marches each side.
progression: Feet closer to hips, small foot lifts
Slow each march to 3 seconds up, 3 seconds down
Add a resistance band above knees

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
pairs_with.reason: Both challenge unilateral bridge stability

pairs_with.name: Hamstring Walkout
pairs_with.reason: Both are advanced hamstring bridge variations

form_cue: Press through your heels to hold the hips up, then lift one foot just off the floor without the pelvis dropping or twisting. Keep your ribs down. Feel it in the hamstring and glute of the supporting leg.
stop_condition: Strong effort in the hamstrings is normal. Stop with a hamstring cramp, low-back pain, or sharp knee pain. Lower your hips to the floor to rest whenever you need to, and do not hold your breath.
regression: Bring your feet closer to your hips and make the lifts tiny, or just lift one heel while the toes stay down. Fewer marches is fine.
remediation: If your hips sag or rock side to side, or the hamstring cramps, move the feet closer and hold a steady two-foot bridge. Glute Bridge is the one to get solid before marching.

name: Ankle Inversion/Eversion
desc: Sit with feet flat. Roll your feet to the outside edges (inversion), hold 3 seconds, then roll to inside edges (eversion), hold 3 seconds. 10 reps.
progression: Stand and do gentle rolling with balance support
Add a resistance band for inversion/eversion against resistance

pairs_with.name: Ankle Circles
pairs_with.reason: Circles for general mobility, inversion/eversion for specific

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Ankle stability supports balance

form_cue: Roll the soles gently toward each other (inversion) then apart (eversion), moving from the ankle with the heel fairly still — controlled and small, since this is the direction ankles sprain.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp pain, especially on the OUTER ankle (inversion is the classic sprain direction). Gentle range only.
regression: Very small movements; if recovering from a sprain, work the pain-free direction only.
remediation: Build tolerance with pain-free pumps and circles before loading inversion/eversion.

name: Finger Abduction with Band
desc: Wrap a small rubber band around all five fingers at the middle knuckle. Spread fingers apart against the resistance. 12 reps, 3 sets each hand.
progression: Hold the open position for 3 seconds

pairs_with.name: Rubber Band Finger Extension
pairs_with.reason: Fingertip band vs knuckle band for different grip angles

pairs_with.name: Grip Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Open and close patterns for hand strength balance

form_cue: Spread the fingers apart against the band at the middle knuckles, then control the return — it trains the small hand muscles. Slow and deliberate.
stop_condition: Stop with joint pain; moderate effort only.
regression: Looser band, fewer reps, or plain finger spreads first.
remediation: Build with unresisted Finger Spread before adding the band.

name: Backward Walking
desc: Walk slowly backward in a straight line for at least 20 steps. Keep a wall or railing nearby for safety. This challenges balance in an unfamiliar direction.

phases.label: Walk slowly backward in a straight line for 20 ...

pairs_with.name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
pairs_with.reason: Forward and backward walking for complete balance

pairs_with.name: Grapevine Walk
pairs_with.reason: Multi-directional walking challenges

form_cue: Stand tall, reach back with your toes first and roll down to the heel, taking small slow steps. Keep your chest up rather than leaning forward. Check the path behind you is clear before you start.
stop_condition: Clear the floor behind you and keep a hand near a wall, railing or counter. Stop if you feel dizzy, stumble, or have sharp pain in your knees, hips or back. Feeling unsure at first is normal; losing your balance is not.
regression: Slide one hand along a counter or wall as you go, take shorter steps and fewer of them. Stop and look over your shoulder whenever you need to.
remediation: If you shuffle, lean forward or keep twisting to look behind, make the steps smaller and keep a hand on the support. Practise Heel-to-Toe Walk going forward until it feels steady.

name: Extended Exhale Breathing
desc: Breathe in for 3 counts, breathe out for 6 counts. The extended exhale activates your parasympathetic nervous system. 10 breaths.

phases.label: Breathe in for 3 counts, breathe out for 6 counts

progression: Use before bed as a sleep onset tool

pairs_with.name: 4-7-8 Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Both emphasize extended exhale for calming

pairs_with.name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
pairs_with.reason: Breathing plus muscle relaxation for complete calming

form_cue: In for 3, out for 6 — the exhale about double the inhale, which is what down-shifts the nervous system. Smooth and belly-led.
stop_condition: Ease off with any lightheadedness and return to natural breathing.
regression: Any in:out ratio where the exhale is longer works — scale it to comfort.
remediation: None; this is a gentle, high-value pattern.

name: Seated Shoulder Blade Pinch
desc: While seated at your desk, pull your shoulder blades down and together, as if putting them in your back pockets. Hold 5 seconds, release. 8 reps.

phases.label: While seated at your desk, pull your shoulder b...

progression: Maintain the position while typing for 30 seconds

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Same muscles, slightly different cue

pairs_with.name: Chin Tuck
pairs_with.reason: Shoulder blades down and chin back together fix desk posture

form_cue: Pull the shoulder blades DOWN and together — 'into the back pockets' — not shrugging up. Chest stays soft; the work is between the blades.
stop_condition: Stop if the shoulders rise toward the ears, or with front-of-shoulder pinching or neck strain.
regression: A lighter squeeze and a briefer hold.
remediation: If the upper traps dominate, practice scapular depression (blades down without squeezing) first.

name: Doorway Lat Stretch
desc: Hold a doorframe overhead with both hands. Step forward and let your body hang slightly to stretch the lats and side body. Hold 20 seconds.

phases.label: Hold a doorframe overhead with both hands

progression: Shift to one side then the other

pairs_with.name: Overhead Reach
pairs_with.reason: Both open up the overhead range and lat length

pairs_with.name: Side Bend Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both stretch the lateral chain

form_cue: Hold the frame with both hands as high as you comfortably can, feet planted, and sit your hips back so your arms lengthen and your chest drops gently. Keep your feet on the floor the whole time. Feel the stretch under the arms and along your sides.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching at the top of the shoulder, sharp pain, numbness or tingling in the arms or hands, or dizziness. Only use a solid frame you can grip securely and never take your feet off the floor. A long pull down your sides is normal.
regression: Hold the sides of the frame at chest or shoulder height instead of overhead and sit the hips back only a little. Use a shorter hold.
remediation: If your lower back arches sharply or your shoulders jam up by your ears, you are hanging too heavily. Take more weight through your feet, bend the knees and let the stretch come from sitting the hips back.

name: Standing IT Band Stretch
desc: Cross one foot behind the other. Lean your hip toward the side of the back foot and reach the same-side arm overhead. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Lean further and add a forward hinge

pairs_with.name: Side Bend Stretch
pairs_with.reason: IT band stretch adds a hip component to the side bend

pairs_with.name: Banded Lateral Walk
pairs_with.reason: Stretch the IT band, strengthen the glute med

form_cue: Keep both feet flat and your chest facing forward, then push the hip of the back leg out to its side while that arm reaches up and over. Do not twist or bend forward. Feel the stretch along the outer hip and side of the body.
stop_condition: Stand beside a wall or counter you can touch, since crossed feet make you less steady. Stop with unsteadiness, sharp pain in the outer hip or knee, or pinching in the low back. A gentle pull down the side is normal.
regression: Keep one hand on a wall or counter, cross the feet only slightly and lean a small amount. Leave the arm down if reaching overhead is uncomfortable, and use a shorter hold.
remediation: If you twist, bend forward or lose balance, uncross the feet a little and lean less. Practise the side lean on its own with Side Bend Stretch first.

name: Incline Push-Up
desc: Place hands on a counter or sturdy table, body in a straight line at an angle. Do push-ups. 10-12 reps. Harder than wall push-ups, easier than floor.

phases.label: Place hands on a counter or sturdy table, body ...

progression: Progress to knee push-ups on the floor

pairs_with.name: Wall Push-Up
pairs_with.reason: Wall push-up is the easier progression

pairs_with.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen then stretch the chest

form_cue: Hands on the edge of the surface a little wider than your shoulders, feet back, body in one straight line from head to heels. Lower your chest toward the edge and press away. Feel it in the chest, shoulders and arms.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp pain in the shoulder, elbow or wrist, chest pain or pressure, or dizziness. Muscle effort is normal. Use only a heavy, fixed surface that cannot slide or tip, and make sure your feet will not slip.
regression: Use a higher surface, stand with your feet closer to it, lower only part of the way, or do fewer reps.
remediation: If your hips sag, your bottom lifts or your head drops forward, the angle is too hard. Tighten your stomach and buttocks, or go back to Wall Push-Up until you can keep a straight line.

name: Lying Hip Flexor Stretch
desc: Lie on the edge of a bed or bench. Pull one knee to your chest while letting the other leg hang off the edge. The hanging leg should feel a hip flexor stretch. 30 seconds each side.
progression: Let the hanging leg relax, 20 seconds
Add gentle knee bend on the hanging leg

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Lying version is more passive and supported

pairs_with.name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both are supine hip and back stretches

form_cue: Lie on your back with your buttocks near the edge. Hug one knee to your chest so the low back stays flat, and let the other leg hang relaxed off the edge. Feel the stretch at the front of the hanging hip and thigh.
stop_condition: Use a firm, stable bed and stay well supported so you cannot slide off. Stop with sharp back pain, pinching in the front of either hip, groin pain, or tingling in the leg. A pulling stretch at the front of the hip is normal.
regression: Lie a little further onto the bed so the leg hangs less, or rest the hanging foot on a low stool or stack of books. Use a shorter hold.
remediation: If your low back arches up off the bed, the stretch has moved to your back. Hug the knee in closer, or raise the hanging foot on a support until the back stays flat.

name: Neck Lateral Flexion with Overpressure
desc: Tilt your head to one side. Place the same-side hand on your head and add very gentle additional pressure. Hold 15 seconds each side. Be very gentle.
progression: Add slight rotation (look at floor) for different fibers

pairs_with.name: Neck Side Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Basic tilt first, then add gentle overpressure

pairs_with.name: Upper Trap Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both deepen the lateral neck stretch

form_cue: Tilt the head to the side, then let the hand add only VERY gentle extra pressure — a light assist, never a pull. The stretch should feel mild along the opposite side of the neck.
stop_condition: Overpressure on the neck is the higher-risk part — stop the instant you feel pinching, sharp pain, dizziness, or any tingling into the arm. When in doubt, remove the hand.
regression: Drop the overpressure entirely and do a plain active tilt (like Neck Side Tilt) — most of the benefit, far less risk.
remediation: If your active tilt range is already limited or symptomatic, stay with the gentle active version and skip overpressure until a clinician clears it.

name: Quadruped Rock Back
desc: On hands and knees, slowly rock your hips back toward your heels while keeping your hands in place. Return to start. 10 reps. A gentle lower back mobilizer.

phases.label: On hands and knees, slowly rock your hips back ...

progression: Hold at the back position for 5 seconds
Shift to one side on the rock back

pairs_with.name: Child's Pose
pairs_with.reason: Quadruped rock back is the dynamic version of child's pose

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow
pairs_with.reason: Both are quadruped spinal mobility exercises

form_cue: Start with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Keeping your back long and hands planted, ease your hips back toward your heels, then return. Feel a gentle stretch in the low back, hips and shoulders.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp back pain, pinching in the front of the hips, knee or wrist pain, or tingling in the legs. A gentle stretch is normal; do not push into pain to reach your heels.
regression: Rock back only partway and do fewer reps. Kneel on a folded towel, and widen your knees slightly if the hips feel blocked.
remediation: If your low back rounds early or your hips pinch, stop the rock just before that point and work in that smaller range. Keep the movement slow and even.

name: Belly Breathing with Weight
desc: Lie on your back, place a light book or small weight on your belly. Breathe so the object rises on inhale and falls on exhale. 10 breaths. The weight provides feedback.

phases.label: Lie on your back, place a light book or small w...

progression: Extend exhale to twice inhale length
Add a 2-second pause between inhale and exhale

pairs_with.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Weight adds tactile feedback to belly breathing

pairs_with.name: Crocodile Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Both use position to enhance breathing awareness

form_cue: Let the object rise as you breathe in and sink as you breathe out, while your chest and shoulders stay quiet. Breathe gently through your nose; do not push your belly out or force the breath.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel light-headed or short of breath, or if the weight is uncomfortable on your belly. Return to normal breathing. Check with a clinician first if you are pregnant or have had recent abdominal surgery.
regression: Use your hand instead of an object, bend your knees with your feet flat or put a pillow under them, and take fewer breaths.
remediation: If the object barely moves or your chest lifts first, slow down and breathe more softly. Practise Diaphragmatic Breathing with a hand on your belly first.

name: Zombie Walk
desc: Walk forward kicking each leg straight up while reaching the opposite hand toward the lifted toes. 10 kicks each leg. Dynamic hamstring stretch.
progression: Add a brief hold at the top of each kick

pairs_with.name: Leg Swing (Front-Back)
pairs_with.reason: Both are dynamic hamstring mobility exercises

pairs_with.name: Standing Forward Fold
pairs_with.reason: Dynamic then static hamstring stretching

form_cue: Stand tall and swing one leg up with a nearly straight knee only as high as your back stays upright, reaching the opposite hand toward it. Controlled swing, not a fling. Feel a brief stretch behind the thigh.
stop_condition: A quick stretch behind the thigh is normal. Stop with a sharp or sudden pull in the back of the thigh, low-back pain, or loss of balance. Warm up first, never force the height, and stay near a wall on a clear floor.
regression: Do it in place with one hand on a wall or chair, with small low swings and a soft knee. Fewer kicks is fine.
remediation: If you round your back or lean backward to reach your toes, lower the kick and stop chasing the hand. If the swing feels uncontrolled, use Standing Hamstring Stretch instead.

name: Pallof Hold with Rotation
desc: From a Pallof press position (band at chest height, arms extended), slowly rotate toward and away from the anchor point. 8 reps each side.
progression: Add a step away from anchor for more tension

pairs_with.name: Pallof Press (Band)
pairs_with.reason: Press is anti-rotation, adding rotation increases challenge

pairs_with.name: Standing Anti-Rotation Hold
pairs_with.reason: Both are standing core rotation exercises

form_cue: Stand tall, feet about hip width, knees soft, arms straight out from your chest. Turn your chest, arms and head together as one unit, slowly, through a small range you fully control. Feel the muscles around your waist.
stop_condition: Loaded twisting: check the anchor is secure and keep the band light. Stop with any sharp or pinching lower back pain, if the band jerks you round, or if you lose balance. If you have been told to avoid twisting, skip this.
regression: Use a lighter band or stand closer to the anchor, make the turn smaller, and bend your elbows to bring your hands nearer your chest. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If the band snaps you back toward the anchor, or your arms move while your trunk stays still, reduce the tension and the range. Go back to Pallof Press (Band) until you can hold it without moving.

name: Shoulder Pendulum
desc: Lean forward holding a table with one hand. Let the other arm hang down and swing it gently in small circles. 15 seconds each direction, each arm. Very gentle shoulder mobilizer.
progression: Hold a light weight for traction

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Rolls
pairs_with.reason: Both are gentle shoulder warm-up exercises

pairs_with.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Pendulum warms up, stretch deepens

form_cue: Lean on the table with a flat back and let the other arm hang heavy like a rope. Start the circles with a small sway of your body so the arm follows along; the shoulder muscles stay relaxed. It should feel loose and easy.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or increasing shoulder pain, numbness or tingling in the arm or hand, dizziness or lightheadedness from leaning forward, or back strain. Come up slowly. Easy, painless movement is the goal.
regression: Make the circles tiny, lean forward less, or just let the arm hang still and relax for a moment. You can also sit and lean forward with your free forearm on the table.
remediation: If you find you are lifting or steering the arm with your shoulder muscles, stop and let it hang still, then restart with a smaller body sway. Bend your knees and keep weight on the table hand if your back tires.

name: Forearm Pronation/Supination
desc: Rest forearm on your desk, hand hanging off the edge. Rotate palm down then palm up slowly. 15 rotations each arm. Mobilizes the forearm.
progression: Hold a light weight for resistance
Hold at end ranges for 3 seconds

pairs_with.name: Wrist Circles
pairs_with.reason: Both target forearm and wrist mobility

pairs_with.name: Grip Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Mobility then strength for the forearm

form_cue: Forearm resting on the desk, hand off the edge; rotate slowly palm-down then palm-up, keeping the elbow and forearm still so the motion is at the forearm, not the shoulder.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp wrist or elbow pain. Smooth, controlled rotation only.
regression: Smaller range, or hold a light object for feedback (not weight).
remediation: If the elbow lifts to cheat, pin it to the desk or your side.

name: Resisted Hip Flexion
desc: Loop a band around one foot and anchor it behind you. March the banded leg up against resistance. 12 reps each leg. Strengthens hip flexors for walking.
progression: Add a 2-second hold at the top

pairs_with.name: Standing March
pairs_with.reason: Bodyweight marching builds toward resisted marching

pairs_with.name: Hip Flexor Stretch (Half-Kneel)
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen and stretch the hip flexors

form_cue: Stand tall and lift the banded knee straight up in front toward hip height without leaning back or hiking the hip, then lower slowly. Feel the effort at the front of the lifting hip.
stop_condition: Hold a counter or sturdy chair, and check the band is anchored low and securely so it cannot slip or snap. Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the front of the hip or groin, low-back pain or unsteadiness.
regression: Use the lightest band or no band, lift the knee only part of the way and keep both hands on a support. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If you lean back, sway or hitch the hip up to raise the knee, the band is too strong. Lower the lift or lighten the band, and practise Standing March first.

name: Chest Squeeze Isometric
desc: Press palms together at chest height and squeeze as hard as you can. Hold 10 seconds, release. 5 reps. Activates the chest without any equipment.

phases.label: Press palms together at chest height and squeez...

progression: Move hands to different heights (low, mid, high)
Squeeze and slowly push hands out in front

pairs_with.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Strengthen then stretch the chest

pairs_with.name: Wall Push-Up
pairs_with.reason: Isometric builds awareness, push-up builds dynamic strength

form_cue: Press the palms together hard at chest height and hold, feeling the chest work — keep the shoulders DOWN (not shrugging) and KEEP BREATHING through the hold.
stop_condition: Stop with shoulder or wrist pain, or if the shoulders creep up to the ears. Don't hold the breath (it can spike blood pressure).
regression: Lighter squeeze, shorter hold, hands lower.
remediation: If the shoulders shrug, cue them down first; if the wrists complain, press with loose fists instead of flat palms.

name: Decline Push-Up
desc: Place feet on a step or chair, hands on the floor. Perform push-ups with body angled downward. 8 reps. Emphasizes upper chest.

phases.label: Place feet on a step or chair, hands on the floor

progression: Add a 2-second hold at the bottom

pairs_with.name: Incline Push-Up
pairs_with.reason: Incline for lower chest, decline for upper chest

pairs_with.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Stretch after intense push-ups

form_cue: Hands under the shoulders, feet on the step, body in one rigid line from head to heels. Lower the chest between your hands with elbows angled back, then press up. Feel it in the upper chest, shoulders and arms.
stop_condition: This is an advanced, head-down position. Stop with sharp shoulder, wrist or back pain, chest pain or pressure, dizziness or pressure in the head. Use only a low, fixed step that cannot slide, and skip it if being head-down is a problem for you.
regression: Use a lower step, lower only part of the way, or do fewer reps. If that is still hard, do push-ups with your hands on a counter instead and your feet on the floor.
remediation: If your hips sag, your lower back arches or your head drops, stop the set; form has gone and the load is on your back and shoulders. Go back to Incline Push-Up until a straight line is easy.

name: Chest Fly (Floor)
desc: Lie on your back with light weights (or water bottles) in each hand, arms extended above chest. Lower arms out to the sides with a slight elbow bend, then bring back up. 12 reps.
progression: Add a 2-second squeeze at the top

pairs_with.name: Standing Chest Fly
pairs_with.reason: Standing with band vs floor with weight

pairs_with.name: Foam Roller Chest Opener
pairs_with.reason: Dynamic and passive chest opening

form_cue: On your back with knees bent, weights above the chest and a slight, fixed bend in the elbows. Open the arms slowly until the upper arms lightly touch the floor, then bring them back up in a wide arc. Feel it in the chest.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the front of the shoulder, chest pain or pressure, or numbness or tingling in the arms. Muscle effort is normal. Use weights light enough to control, keep a firm grip and never hold them over your face.
regression: Use lighter weights or none at all, lower the arms only part of the way, bend the elbows more, or do fewer reps.
remediation: If your elbows bend and straighten like a press, your wrists flop or your back arches, the weight is too heavy. Go lighter and slower. Standing Chest Fly trains the same hugging motion with less load.

name: Chest Doorway Stretch (Low Position)
desc: Place forearm on a door frame at waist height with elbow below shoulder. Lean through the doorway. This targets the lower chest fibers. 20 seconds each side.
progression: Combine with the high position for a full pec stretch

pairs_with.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
pairs_with.reason: High and low positions stretch different pec fibers

pairs_with.name: Chest Expansion Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both open the front of the chest

form_cue: Rest the forearm on the frame with the elbow lower than the shoulder, then lean gently forward and let your chest turn slightly away from the arm. Shoulder stays down and back. Feel the stretch in the chest and front of the shoulder.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the front of the shoulder, a slipping or unstable feeling, or numbness or tingling in the arm or hand. A steady pull in the chest is the normal stretch feeling.
regression: Lean less, turn your body away less, or use a shorter hold.
remediation: If the shoulder rolls forward or you bend at the waist to get a stretch, stand up tall and ease off. If you cannot find the position comfortably, stay with Doorway Pec Stretch.

name: Advanced Bird Dog
desc: From a bird dog position (opposite arm and leg extended), draw circles with the extended hand and foot simultaneously. 8 circles each direction, each side.
progression: Add a pause at the most challenging position

pairs_with.name: Bird Dog
pairs_with.reason: Standard bird dog builds toward the advanced version

pairs_with.name: Bear Crawl Hold
pairs_with.reason: Both are advanced quadruped core exercises

form_cue: Hold the bird dog with a flat back and level hips, belly lightly braced. Draw small, slow circles with the lifted hand and foot, moving from the shoulder and hip while the trunk stays completely still.
stop_condition: Safety: keep the circles small and slow. Stop with sharp back pain, pain or tingling into an arm or leg, wrist or shoulder pain, or if you start to tip and cannot steady yourself.
regression: Circle only the hand, or only the foot, with the other limb resting on the floor. Make the circles tiny and do fewer of them.
remediation: If your hips rock, your back sags or you hold your breath, the circles are too big. Shrink them, or go back to Bird Dog until you can hold it without wobbling.

name: Side-Lying Clamshell with Lift
desc: Lie on your side with a band above your knees. Open the top knee and simultaneously lift both feet off the floor. 10 reps each side.
progression: Clamshell without the foot lift first
Add the foot lift, light band, 8 reps
Hold the open-and-lifted position for 3 seconds

pairs_with.name: Clamshell
pairs_with.reason: Standard clamshell builds toward this advanced variation

pairs_with.name: Banded Lateral Walk
pairs_with.reason: Both use bands for glute medius work

form_cue: Keep hips stacked and knees bent. As the top knee opens against the band, let both feet rise together off the floor while the bottom knee stays down. Move slowly and feel it in the side and back of both hips.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching in the front of the hip or groin, sharp pain in the outer hip or low-back pain, or if the band rolls or slips. Control the return so the band does not snap the knees shut. Hip effort is normal.
regression: Take the band off, or leave the feet down and do the plain knee opening, with a smaller range and fewer reps.
remediation: If the top hip rolls backward or you cannot keep the feet together as they lift, you are past your control. Go back to Clamshell without the foot lift until it is smooth.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
desc: Place one foot behind you on a chair or step. Lower into a single-leg squat on the front leg. 8 reps each side. Hold something for balance if needed.
progression: Hold light weights for added challenge

pairs_with.name: Split Squat
pairs_with.reason: Regular split squat builds toward Bulgarian

pairs_with.name: Couch Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Same position for strength and flexibility

form_cue: Most of your weight stays on the front foot. Lower straight down with the front heel flat and the knee in line with the toes, torso leaning slightly forward. Feel it in the front thigh and glute.
stop_condition: Hard thigh effort is normal. Stop with sharp or pinching pain in either knee, pain in the back hip or groin, or loss of balance. Use a chair or step that cannot slide and keep a wall or counter within reach.
regression: Use a lower step for the back foot, hold a support and lower only partway, with fewer reps. Or put the back foot on the floor.
remediation: If the front heel lifts, the knee caves in or you tip sideways, step the front foot further forward and shorten the range. If it stays shaky, go back to Split Squat on the floor.

name: Single-Leg Heel Raise Hold
desc: Stand on one foot on a step edge. Rise to full tiptoe and hold for 10 seconds. Lower slowly. 5 reps each side. Builds calf endurance.
progression: Close your eyes during the hold

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
pairs_with.reason: Dynamic reps build toward static holds

pairs_with.name: Heel Drop (Eccentric Calf)
pairs_with.reason: Both are advanced single-leg calf exercises on a step

form_cue: Ball of the foot on the step, hold a rail, rise straight up as high as you can with the ankle not rolling outward, and stay tall. Lower slowly. Feel the calf working hard.
stop_condition: A burning, tired calf is normal. Stop with a cramp, sharp pain in the heel, behind the ankle or under the ball of the foot, or any wobble. Always hold a rail or wall, on a step that will not slip, eyes open.
regression: Do the hold on flat floor instead of a step, or on both feet, with a firm hold on a counter and a shorter hold. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your heel sinks during the hold or the ankle rolls out, end that rep there and rest. Go back to Single-Leg Calf Raise until you can reach full height with control each time.

name: Wrist CARs
desc: Make a fist. Slowly draw the biggest circle you can with your wrist, moving through full range including flexion, extension, and side-to-side. 5 circles each direction, each wrist.
progression: Add light resistance from the other hand

pairs_with.name: Wrist Circles
pairs_with.reason: Circles are the warm-up, CARs are the controlled progression

pairs_with.name: Tendon Glide Sequence
pairs_with.reason: Both are comprehensive wrist/hand mobility exercises

form_cue: Make a fist and draw the biggest slow circle the wrist can, deliberately reaching full flexion, extension, and both sides — controlled rotation, forearm still. Quality and range over speed.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp pain or painful clicking; work to the edge of comfortable range, not into pain.
regression: Smaller circles; build the range over time.
remediation: Warm up with plain wrist circles before pushing full range.

name: Staggered Stance Balance
desc: Stand with one foot directly in front of the other (heel to toe). Hold this position for 15 seconds, then switch which foot is in front. A beginner balance challenge.

phases.label: Stand with one foot directly in front of the ot...

progression: Arms at sides instead of out

pairs_with.name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
pairs_with.reason: Static staggered stance prepares for heel-to-toe walking

pairs_with.name: Weight Shift
pairs_with.reason: Both are introductory balance exercises

form_cue: Stand tall with your weight shared evenly between both feet, knees soft, and eyes on a fixed point ahead. Arms can be out to the sides. You should feel your feet and ankles making small corrections.
stop_condition: Stand beside a counter or wall you can touch. Step your feet apart and stop if you feel dizzy, cannot steady yourself, or have pain in your feet, ankles or knees. Small wobbles are normal.
regression: Leave a gap between your feet, front to back and a little side to side, instead of lining them up heel to toe. Rest a hand on a counter and take a shorter hold.
remediation: If you sway, lean on one leg or keep stepping out, widen the stance slightly until you can stand still. Bring the feet closer into line only as it gets steady.

name: Nasal Breathing Walk
desc: Walk at a comfortable pace breathing only through your nose. Focus on smooth, rhythmic nasal breathing for 2 minutes. Nasal breathing filters and humidifies air.

phases.label: Walk at a comfortable pace breathing only throu...

progression: Faster pace while maintaining nose breathing
Coordinate steps with breath (4 steps in, 4 steps out)

pairs_with.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
pairs_with.reason: Learn belly breathing seated, then apply while walking

pairs_with.name: Standing March
pairs_with.reason: Both are walking-based exercises

form_cue: Keep your lips gently closed, your jaw relaxed and your pace easy enough that nose breathing stays quiet and smooth. Walk tall with relaxed shoulders.
stop_condition: Stop and breathe normally if you feel light-headed, short of breath or uncomfortably starved of air. If your nose is blocked today, do not strain through it. Walk on a clear, even surface.
regression: Slow your pace, shorten the time, or breathe in through your nose and out through your mouth.
remediation: If you keep needing to open your mouth, you are walking too fast for now: slow down until nose breathing is comfortable. Practise Diaphragmatic Breathing at rest first.

name: Eccentric Hamstring Slide
desc: Lie on your back with heels on a towel on a smooth floor. Lift hips into a bridge, then slowly slide heels away from you until hips drop. Reset and repeat. 6 reps.

phases.label: Lie on your back with heels on a towel on a smo...

pairs_with.name: Hamstring Walkout
pairs_with.reason: Walk-out is the simpler version of the slide

pairs_with.name: Nordic Curl Eccentric
pairs_with.reason: Both are eccentric hamstring strengtheners

form_cue: Lift the hips into a bridge, then slide the heels away slowly, keeping the hips up as long as you can and the ribs down. Lower to the floor before sliding back in. Feel it strongly in the hamstrings.
stop_condition: Strong hamstring effort is normal. Stop with a hamstring cramp, a sharp or sudden pull behind the thigh, low-back pain, or pain behind the knee. Slide slowly and rest fully between reps.
regression: Slide only a short distance, or slide one heel at a time while the other foot stays planted. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your hips drop straight away, your back arches or the hamstrings cramp, shorten the slide and slow down. Hamstring Walkout is the step to practise before this one.

name: Wall Plank
desc: Place forearms on a wall at chest height, step feet back until body forms a straight line at an angle. Hold 30 seconds. A beginner-friendly plank variation.

phases.label: Place forearms on a wall at chest height, step ...

pairs_with.name: Plank Hold
pairs_with.reason: Wall plank is the beginner progression toward floor plank

pairs_with.name: Wall Push-Up
pairs_with.reason: Both use the wall for modified upper body exercises

form_cue: Elbows at about shoulder height, body in one straight line from head to heels, heels can lift. Gently tighten your belly and buttocks and push the wall away. Keep breathing. You should feel your belly and shoulders working.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your shoulders, neck or lower back, or if your feet start to slide. Wear shoes or go barefoot on a floor that grips. Gentle effort in the belly and shoulders is normal.
regression: Stand closer to the wall so you are more upright, and take a shorter hold. Resting between two short holds is fine.
remediation: If your hips sag toward the wall, your bottom sticks out or your shoulders creep up to your ears, step your feet in closer and reset the straight line before holding again.

name: Standing Trunk Rotation
desc: Stand with feet shoulder width, arms bent at 90 degrees. Rotate your torso left and right, letting arms swing naturally. 20 rotations total. A gentle core warm-up.

phases.label: Stand with feet shoulder width, arms bent at 90...

progression: Hold a light weight at chest for resistance
Add a small lunge with each rotation

pairs_with.name: Seated Twist
pairs_with.reason: Standing and seated versions of trunk rotation

pairs_with.name: Thoracic Rotation
pairs_with.reason: Both mobilize the thoracic spine through rotation

form_cue: Stand tall with knees soft and turn from your ribs and chest, letting your head follow. Keep it smooth and easy; let your hips turn a little too, but do not swing or bounce at the end of the range.
stop_condition: Stop if you feel dizzy, sharp or pinching back pain, or pain travelling into a leg. If you have been told to avoid twisting your spine, check with a clinician first. A gentle sense of loosening is normal.
regression: Make the turns smaller and slower, or do them sitting tall on a sturdy chair with your arms crossed over your chest. Fewer rotations are fine.
remediation: If you are flinging your arms and using momentum, slow down and turn only as far as you can control. If your knees twist, let your heels lift a little so the feet can pivot.

name: Shoulder Behind-the-Back Reach
desc: Reach one arm overhead and the other behind your back, trying to touch your fingers. Use a towel to bridge the gap if needed. Hold 15 seconds each way.

phases.label: Reach one arm overhead and the other behind you...

progression: Use a towel, note the gap between hands
Try to close the gap over time

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Flexion with Dowel
pairs_with.reason: Both challenge overhead shoulder range

pairs_with.name: Chest Expansion Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Behind-back reach tests and improves internal rotation

form_cue: Top elbow points to the ceiling beside your head, bottom hand slides up the middle of your back. Stand tall and reach the hands toward each other without arching or leaning. Feel a stretch in the back of the top arm and the front of the lower shoulder.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in either shoulder, a slipping or unstable feeling, numbness or tingling in the arm or hand, or neck strain. Do not yank on the towel. A firm but comfortable stretch is normal.
regression: Hold a towel between your hands and leave a wide gap, pulling only lightly. You can also stretch one arm at a time without trying to join the hands. Use a shorter hold.
remediation: If your back arches, your head pushes forward or the lower shoulder rolls forward, ease off and widen the gap on the towel. Go back to Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch if either arm will not reach its position comfortably.

name: Foam Roller IT Band
desc: Lie on your side with a foam roller under your outer thigh. Roll from hip to just above the knee, pausing on tender spots. 45 seconds each side.
progression: More body weight on the roller
Hold on tender spots for 30 seconds
Add small knee bends while on a tender spot

pairs_with.name: Standing IT Band Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Roll to release, stretch to lengthen

pairs_with.name: Banded Lateral Walk
pairs_with.reason: Release then strengthen the lateral hip

form_cue: Support yourself on your forearm and put the top foot on the floor in front to take some weight. Roll slowly along the fleshy outer thigh only, staying off the bony point of the hip and off the knee joint.
stop_condition: Firm, tolerable pressure is expected; sharp pain, numbness, tingling or pain that makes you hold your breath is not. Stop then, and stop with shoulder or wrist pain from propping. Skip bruised or swollen areas.
regression: Take more weight through the top foot and supporting arm so the pressure is light, roll a shorter stretch of thigh and use a shorter time. A softer roller also helps.
remediation: If you tense up, hold your breath or cannot support yourself, the pressure is too much. Lighten it, or leave the roller today and do Standing IT Band Stretch.

name: Lying Abduction with Band
