desc: Lie on your side with a resistance band above your knees. Lift the top leg against the band resistance, hold 3 seconds at the top. 10 reps each side.
progression: Add small pulses at the top

pairs_with.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
pairs_with.reason: Bodyweight builds base, band adds resistance

pairs_with.name: Banded Lateral Walk
pairs_with.reason: Both use bands for hip abduction

form_cue: Keep hips stacked and the top leg in line with your body, toes forward. Lift against the band without rolling backward, hold, then lower slowly so the band does not pull the leg down. Feel it in the side of the top hip.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching or sharp pain in the hip or groin, low-back pain, pain in the hip you are lying on, or if the band rolls or slips. Lower under control every rep. A strong working feeling in the outer hip is normal.
regression: Use the lightest band or none, lift a shorter distance without the hold and do fewer reps. Bend the bottom knee for a steadier base.
remediation: If you roll back or the leg swings forward to beat the band, the band is too strong. Take it off and get Side-Lying Leg Raise smooth first.

name: Standing Calf Pump
desc: Stand and rapidly rise up on toes then lower, pumping your calves quickly. 30 pumps. Gets blood flowing, especially after sitting.

phases.label: Stand and rapidly rise up on toes then lower, p...

progression: Pumps with a brief hold at the top

pairs_with.name: Calf Raise
pairs_with.reason: Pumps are fast and circulatory, raises are slow and strengthening

pairs_with.name: Standing March
pairs_with.reason: Both get blood moving after sitting

form_cue: Rise onto the balls of both feet and lower in a quick, even rhythm, staying tall with your heels coming down softly each time. Feel the calves warming up. Keep a hand near a wall or chair.
stop_condition: Warm, lightly tired calves are normal. Stop with a calf or foot cramp, sharp pain in the heel or behind the ankle, dizziness, or unsteadiness. Hold a wall or chair back if balance is at all uncertain.
regression: Slow the pace right down, rise only partway and hold a counter. Or do the pumps sitting, lifting and lowering your heels. Fewer pumps is fine.
remediation: If you bounce, bang your heels down or rock forward and back, slow down until each rep is controlled. The slower Calf Raise is the place to practise the movement first.

name: Neck Protraction and Retraction
desc: Slowly push your head forward (protraction) then pull it back (retraction/chin tuck). Move through the full range 10 times. This trains neck positioning awareness.

phases.label: Slowly push your head forward (protraction) the...

progression: Add a 3-second hold at each end
Do against a wall for retraction feedback

pairs_with.name: Chin Tuck
pairs_with.reason: Chin tuck trains retraction, this adds the full range

pairs_with.name: Neck CARs
pairs_with.reason: Both explore full neck range of motion

form_cue: Glide the head forward, then draw it straight back into a gentle chin tuck — a horizontal slide, smooth and controlled, not a nod or a forceful jam backward.
stop_condition: Stop with dizziness, pinching at the base of the skull, or arm symptoms. Keep the range comfortable; retraction is the useful end.
regression: Reduce the range and slow it down; even small glides train the pattern.
remediation: If the retraction end pinches, stick with plain Chin Tucks until it settles.

name: Sphinx to Child's Pose Flow
desc: Flow between sphinx pose (chest up, forearms down) and child's pose (sitting back on heels, arms forward). 8 slow flows. Alternates spinal extension and flexion.

phases.label: Flow between sphinx pose (chest up, forearms do...

progression: Hold each position for 3 seconds, 8 flows
Add a spinal twist in child's pose

pairs_with.name: Sphinx Pose
pairs_with.reason: Uses sphinx as part of the flow

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow
pairs_with.reason: Both alternate between flexion and extension

form_cue: From sphinx, press through your forearms and hands and ease the hips back toward your heels, then slide forward and lower the hips again. Move slowly with your breath and let the spine change shape gradually.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching back pain, pain or tingling into a leg, knee pain when sitting back, or dizziness as your head lowers. A gentle stretch at each end is normal.
regression: Make both ends smaller: a low sphinx and only a partial sit back. Put a pillow between your heels and buttocks, and do fewer flows.
remediation: If you rush or drop into either position, pause on hands and knees between the two. If one direction is uncomfortable, stay with the other shape on its own.

name: Seated Scapular Depression
desc: Place hands on the seat of your chair. Push down to lift your body slightly, focusing on pulling shoulder blades down. Hold 5 seconds, 8 reps.

phases.label: Place hands on the seat of your chair

progression: Press down without fully lifting, 5 reps
Full body lift, hold 5 seconds, 8 reps
Add shoulder blade squeezing while depressed

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Depression and retraction together reset shoulder position

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Shrug Release
pairs_with.reason: Both address elevated-shoulder posture

form_cue: Press the hands into the seat to lightly unweight, driving the shoulder blades DOWN — long neck, ears away from shoulders. A small, controlled lift.
stop_condition: Stop with wrist pain, front-of-shoulder pinching, or if you can't keep the shoulders down. Don't hang on locked, shrugged shoulders.
regression: Skip the lift — just press lightly and focus on drawing the blades down without leaving the seat.
remediation: Build wrist tolerance and the scapular-down pattern before putting body weight through the arms.

name: Wide-Leg Forward Fold
desc: Stand with feet wide apart, toes forward. Hinge at the hips and fold forward, reaching hands toward the floor. Hold 30 seconds. Stretches hamstrings and inner thighs.

phases.label: Stand with feet wide apart, toes forward

progression: Knees slightly bent, hands on shins
Walk hands to one foot then the other

pairs_with.name: Standing Forward Fold
pairs_with.reason: Narrow and wide versions for different muscle emphasis

pairs_with.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both stretch the inner thigh area

form_cue: Feet wide and parallel, knees soft, and fold from the hips with a long back before letting the head hang. Feel the stretch in the backs and insides of the thighs. Bend your knees and come up slowly.
stop_condition: A pull in the hamstrings and inner thighs is normal. Stop with dizziness, pressure in the head, sharp groin or low-back pain, or feet starting to slide. Use a non-slip floor and rise slowly.
regression: Narrow your stance, bend your knees and rest your hands on a chair seat, your thighs or your shins so you fold only partway. A shorter hold is fine.
remediation: If your back rounds, your knees lock or your feet slip outward, step the feet closer and support your hands higher. Standing Forward Fold is the gentler version to practise first.

name: Plank with Leg Lift
desc: Hold a forearm plank. Slowly lift one leg off the floor, hold 5 seconds, switch. 5 lifts each leg while maintaining plank form.
progression: Add a slow side-to-side sweep with the lifted leg

pairs_with.name: Plank Hold
pairs_with.reason: Standard plank builds toward plank with leg lifts

pairs_with.name: Bird Dog
pairs_with.reason: Both challenge core stability with limb movement

form_cue: Set a solid forearm plank first. Lift one straight leg only a few inches by squeezing the buttock, keeping your hips level and square to the floor. Keep breathing. Feel your belly and the buttock of the lifted leg.
stop_condition: This is a hard exercise. Stop if your lower back arches or hurts, your hips twist or sag, or you feel shoulder pain or hold your breath. Lower to your knees to rest. Hard effort is normal; back pain is not.
regression: Lift the foot just an inch with a shorter hold, or do the leg lift from hands and knees instead of a plank. Fewer lifts are fine.
remediation: The usual fault is the hips rolling open or the back sagging as the leg lifts. Lift less high, or take the feet a little wider. Return to Plank Hold until you can hold it steadily first.

name: Ankle Band Strengthening
desc: Sit with your lower leg supported and loop a resistance band around the ball of your foot. You will reposition the band for each of the four directions so it pulls the OPPOSITE way to your movement: pull your toes UP (band anchored in front), point them DOWN (band behind or held), turn the sole INWARD (band out to the side), and turn it OUTWARD (band across your body). Keep your lower leg still and move only at the ankle, slowly. 10 reps each direction per foot.

phases.label: Loop a band around the ball of one foot, anchor...

progression: Add a 3-second hold at end range

pairs_with.name: Ankle Inversion/Eversion
pairs_with.reason: Bodyweight first, then add band resistance

pairs_with.name: Single-Leg Stand
pairs_with.reason: Ankle strength directly supports balance

form_cue: Move the foot slowly through dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, inversion, and eversion against the band — controlled reps, full but pain-free range, moving only the ankle.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp pain (especially outer-ankle on inversion), or if the knee/leg swings to help. Ease the band tension if the movement gets jerky.
regression: Lighter band or less range; start with just the pain-free directions, especially if recovering from a sprain.
remediation: Master the unloaded ankle circles, pumps, and inversion/eversion first; add the band once those are smooth and pain-free.

name: Glute-Focused Squat
desc: Stand with a resistance band above knees, feet wider than shoulders. Squat while pushing knees out against the band. Squeeze glutes hard at the top. 12 reps.

phases.label: Stand with a resistance band above knees, feet ...

progression: Add a 3-second hold at the bottom
Pulse 3 times at the bottom of each rep

pairs_with.name: Sumo Squat
pairs_with.reason: Same stance, band adds glute activation

pairs_with.name: Banded Lateral Walk
pairs_with.reason: Both use bands for glute medius activation

form_cue: Sit the hips back and down with chest lifted and heels down, pressing the knees out so they stay over the toes against the band. Stand up fully and tighten the glutes without leaning back. Feel it in the glutes and outer hips.
stop_condition: Stop with knee pain, pinching in the front of the hip, low-back pain or lightheadedness. Breathe out as you stand rather than holding your breath. Working, burning muscles in the hips and thighs are normal effort.
regression: Take the band off, squat only part of the way or down to a sturdy chair, and keep a hand on a counter. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If your knees cave in against the band or your heels lift, use a lighter band or none and a shallower squat. Get Sumo Squat comfortable first.

name: Wall Sit Abductor Press
desc: Hold a wall sit with a resistance band above your knees. Push knees outward against the band while holding the squat. Hold 15 seconds, rest, repeat 3 times.

phases.label: Hold a wall sit with a resistance band above yo...

progression: Pulse the knees outward 10 times while holding

pairs_with.name: Wall Sit with Ball Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Squeeze works adductors, abductor press works the opposite

pairs_with.name: Banded Lateral Walk
pairs_with.reason: Both use bands for hip abductor strength

form_cue: Keep your whole back and head against the wall, feet flat and far enough out that knees stay over ankles. Press the knees gently outward against the band without the feet rolling. Feel it in the thighs and outer hips.
stop_condition: Stop with knee pain or dizziness, and stand up before your legs give out. Keep breathing steadily and never hold your breath. Wear grippy shoes on a non-slip floor so your feet cannot slide. Burning thighs are normal effort.
regression: Sit higher on the wall with only a small knee bend, use a light band or none and hold for a shorter time. Rest longer between holds.
remediation: If your knees drift in, your back peels off the wall or you hold your breath, slide up higher and ease the press. Get plain Wall Sit steady first.

name: Neck Flexion Stretch
desc: Drop your chin toward your chest. Place both hands behind your head and let the weight of your hands gently deepen the stretch. Hold 15 seconds.

phases.label: Drop your chin toward your chest

progression: Just drop chin, no hand pressure

pairs_with.name: Gentle Neck Nod
pairs_with.reason: Nods warm up the motion, this deepens the stretch

pairs_with.name: Upper Trap Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Both target the back of the neck and upper back

form_cue: Drop the chin toward the chest and let ONLY the weight of the hands (not a pull) gently deepen it — the stretch is along the back of the neck, and it stays mild.
stop_condition: Do NOT pull the head down — just rest the hands. Stop with tingling into the arms, sharp pain, or dizziness. Loaded neck flexion is provocative for some, so go easy.
regression: Take the hands away and just drop the chin under its own weight — plenty for most people.
remediation: If it pulls or tingles, skip the hand weight and work gentle active neck nods first.

name: Lying Knee Drop
desc: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat. Slowly drop both knees a few inches to the right, return to center, then to the left. 10 drops each side.
progression: Full drops with shoulders staying flat

pairs_with.name: Supine Twist
pairs_with.reason: Knee drops are the gentle version of full supine twists

pairs_with.name: Pelvic Tilt
pairs_with.reason: Both are gentle supine lower back exercises

form_cue: Lie on your back with knees bent and together, feet flat. Let both knees sway a few inches to one side and bring them back with control, keeping both shoulders and both feet on the floor. It should feel like easy movement in the low back.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching back pain, hip pain, or pain or tingling down a leg. This should feel like easy movement, not a stretch you have to push into.
regression: Make the drops smaller and do fewer of them. A pillow under your head and a cushion between your knees can make it more comfortable.
remediation: If your shoulders lift or the knees fall instead of lowering, slow down and shorten the drop. Keep your arms out to the sides for a steadier base.

name: Resistance Band Overhead Press
desc: Stand on a band, hold the other end at shoulder height. Press arms overhead against the band resistance. 10 reps.

phases.label: Stand on a band, hold the other end at shoulder...

progression: Add a 2-second hold at the top

pairs_with.name: Overhead Reach
pairs_with.reason: Mobility enables the press, press builds strength in the range

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Flexion with Dowel
pairs_with.reason: Both work overhead shoulder function

form_cue: Stand tall with the band under the middle of both feet, hands at shoulder height, wrists straight. Press up until the arms are nearly straight and slightly in front of your ears, ribs down, then lower slowly. Feel it in the shoulders and arms.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching at the top of the shoulder, sharp pain, neck strain, chest pain or pressure, dizziness, or numbness or tingling. Keep the band secure under both feet and check it for nicks, as a band that slips or snaps can hit your face.
regression: Use a lighter band, press only part of the way up, press one arm at a time, or do fewer reps. Sitting on a firm chair with the band under the seat or your feet also makes it steadier.
remediation: If your lower back arches, your ribs flare or your shoulders shrug to your ears, the band is too strong or you are short of overhead range. Lighten the band, and practise Wall Angel first.

name: Suitcase Carry
desc: Hold a weight in one hand at your side. Walk 20 steps while keeping your body perfectly upright — resist leaning toward the weight. Switch hands and repeat.
progression: Focus on keeping shoulders perfectly level

pairs_with.name: Standing Anti-Rotation Hold
pairs_with.reason: Both train anti-lateral-flexion

pairs_with.name: Grip Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Suitcase carry also builds grip endurance

form_cue: Stand tall with shoulders level and ribs stacked over hips, weight hanging by your side, not resting on your leg. Walk with normal, unhurried steps. You should feel the side of your waist opposite the weight working.
stop_condition: Use a light weight you can lift and set down easily, on a clear floor. Stop if you feel sharp pain in your lower back, shoulder or grip hand, lose balance, or hold your breath. Bend your knees to pick it up and put it down.
regression: Use a lighter weight, such as a small bag with a book in it, and take fewer steps. Walk alongside a counter or wall.
remediation: If you lean toward or away from the weight, or the shoulder drags down or hikes up, the weight is too heavy or you are tired: put it down. Practise Standing Anti-Rotation Hold for trunk control.

name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
desc: On hands and knees, place one hand behind your head. Rotate that elbow toward the opposite hand, then rotate it up toward the ceiling. 8 reps each side.
progression: Add a 3-second hold at the top
Extend the rotating arm at the top for more range

pairs_with.name: Thread the Needle
pairs_with.reason: Both are quadruped thoracic rotation exercises

pairs_with.name: Cat-Cow
pairs_with.reason: Warm up with cat-cow, then add rotation

form_cue: On hands and knees, rest one hand lightly behind your head without pulling. Turn the elbow down toward the opposite hand, then open it toward the ceiling, eyes following. The turn comes from the upper back; hips stay over the knees.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp or pinching back pain, shoulder or neck pain, wrist pain, dizziness, or tingling in the arm. A stretch through the mid-back and chest is normal.
regression: Sit your hips back partway toward your heels and make smaller rotations, or place the hand on your shoulder instead of behind your head. Fewer reps are fine.
remediation: If your hips sway or your supporting elbow bends, the range is too big. Make it smaller and press the floor away with the supporting hand, or practise Thoracic Rotation first.

name: Band-Assisted Squat
desc: Loop a band around a pull-up bar or high anchor. Hold the band in front of you and squat using the band to assist your balance and control. 12 reps.

phases.label: Loop a band around a pull-up bar or high anchor

pairs_with.name: Bodyweight Squat
pairs_with.reason: Band-assisted builds toward unassisted squats

pairs_with.name: Deep Squat Hold
pairs_with.reason: Band assistance helps achieve deep squat position

form_cue: Hold the band with arms long, sit the hips back and down with chest up, heels down and knees in line with your toes. Let the band steady you, not haul you up. Feel the work in the thighs and glutes.
stop_condition: Muscle effort in the thighs is normal. Stop with sharp knee pain, hip pinching, low-back pain, dizziness, or if the band or anchor slips or looks worn. Check the anchor holds your weight before every set.
regression: Use a thicker band or stand so there is more tension, and squat only partway to a chair placed behind you. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If you hang back on the band, your heels lift or your knees cave in, shorten the depth and squat down to a chair so you have a target. Lean on the band less as control improves.

name: Standing Pec Minor Stretch
desc: Place your forearm high on a door frame (above shoulder height) and step through. This targets the pec minor, which pulls the shoulder forward. Hold 20 seconds each side.
progression: Add a slight upward look to deepen the stretch

pairs_with.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Standard pec and pec minor for complete chest opening

pairs_with.name: Scapular Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Stretch pec minor, strengthen the opposing muscles

form_cue: Forearm on the frame with the elbow above shoulder height. Step through gently, keeping your ribs down and the shoulder away from your ear. Feel the stretch high in the chest and the front of the shoulder or armpit.
stop_condition: Stop with pinching at the top or front of the shoulder, sharp pain, or numbness or tingling in the arm or hand, which can come on quickly with the arm high. A steady pull in the chest is the normal stretch feeling.
regression: Lower the elbow toward shoulder height, take a smaller step, or use a shorter hold.
remediation: If the shoulder shrugs up or your lower back arches, you have stepped too far or set the arm too high. Step back, lower the arm a little, and return to Doorway Pec Stretch if the high position keeps pinching.

name: Dead Hang
desc: Hang from a pull-up bar or sturdy overhead support with arms straight. Let your body decompress. Hold 20 seconds, rest, repeat 3 times. Great for spinal decompression.

phases.label: Hang from a pull-up bar or sturdy overhead supp...

progression: Feet on ground for partial support, 15 seconds
Add gentle swaying or shoulder shrugs while hanging

pairs_with.name: Shoulder Flexion with Dowel
pairs_with.reason: Both require and build overhead shoulder range

pairs_with.name: Grip Squeeze
pairs_with.reason: Dead hang also builds serious grip endurance

form_cue: Grip the bar with both hands about shoulder-width apart, arms straight, and let your body hang long and still. Keep a little tension in the shoulders rather than sinking fully into the joints. Breathe steadily. Feel a stretch in the shoulders, sides and back.
stop_condition: Stop with sharp shoulder, elbow or wrist pain, a slipping or unstable feeling in the shoulder, numbness or tingling in the hands, or a failing grip. Use only a bar rated for your body weight, low enough to step down from. Do not drop off.
regression: Keep your feet on the floor or on a sturdy step and bend your knees to take only part of your weight through your arms. Use a shorter hold.
remediation: If your grip gives out, your shoulders jam up by your ears or you start to swing, put your feet down straight away. Build up with the feet-supported version and practise Overhead Reach for the overhead position.

name: Lateral Lunge
desc: Step wide to one side, bend that knee and push hips back while keeping the other leg straight. Push back to center. 8 reps each side.
progression: Add a 2-second hold at the bottom
Alternate sides without returning to center

pairs_with.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
pairs_with.reason: Lateral lunge is the dynamic version of the adductor stretch

pairs_with.name: Sumo Squat
pairs_with.reason: Both work the hips in a wide stance

form_cue: Keep both feet flat and pointing forward, sit the hips back as the stepping knee bends in line with its toes, and keep your chest up. Feel it in the glute and thigh of the bent leg, with a stretch in the inner thigh of the straight leg.
stop_condition: Stop with knee pain, sharp or pulling pain in the groin, low-back pain or unsteadiness. Work on a non-slip floor with a counter or chair within reach. Muscle effort and a mild inner-thigh stretch are normal.
regression: Take a smaller step and bend the knee only a little, with a hand on a counter or chair back. Fewer reps is fine.
remediation: If the bent knee caves inward, the heel lifts or you cannot push back to centre in one go, shorten the step and the depth. Practise Standing Adductor Stretch to get used to the position.

name: Plank to Downward Dog
desc: Start in a plank position. Push your hips up and back into downward dog, hold 3 seconds, then flow back to plank. 8 reps. Combines core work with shoulder and hamstring mobility.
progression: Add a push-up in the plank position before each transition

pairs_with.name: Plank Hold
pairs_with.reason: Plank is the base, this adds dynamic movement

pairs_with.name: Downward Dog
pairs_with.reason: Both include the downward dog position

form_cue: In the plank, hands are under shoulders and your body is one straight line. Push the floor away and lift your hips up and back, knees bending if needed, then return forward with control so your hips do not sag.
stop_condition: Stop at once with dizziness, pressure in your head or eyes, sharp wrist, shoulder or low-back pain, or tingling in the hands. Rest on hands and knees and rise slowly. If head-down positions are a problem for you, check with a clinician first.
regression: Start from hands and knees instead of a full plank, keep your knees bent as your hips lift, and do fewer reps. Hands on a sturdy chair seat also works.
remediation: If your hips sag or your low back arches coming back to plank, drop your knees for that part and slow down. Practise Plank Hold until you can keep a straight line.

name: Slow Mountain Climber
desc: In a plank position, slowly bring one knee toward your chest, hold 2 seconds, return, then the other knee. 8 reps each side. Controlled, not fast.
progression: Speed up slightly while maintaining form

pairs_with.name: Plank with Leg Lift
pairs_with.reason: Both add limb movement to a plank

pairs_with.name: Bear Crawl Hold
pairs_with.reason: Both are intense core stability challenges

form_cue: Hands under shoulders, arms straight, body in one line from head to heels. Draw one knee forward slowly without your hips lifting or your back rounding much, then place the foot back quietly. Feel your belly and shoulders.
stop_condition: This is a hard exercise. Stop if you feel sharp pain in your wrists, shoulders or lower back, if your hips sag, or if you hold your breath. Lower your knees to rest. Hard effort is normal; joint pain is not.
regression: Put your hands on a sturdy bench, counter or the seat of a chair pushed against a wall, so your body is on a slope. Bring the knee only part of the way and do fewer reps.
remediation: If your hips pike up, bounce or sag as the knee comes in, slow down and shorten the knee drive. Return to Plank Hold until you can hold a steady line first.
